body:
Together we’re making the “impossible” possible.
| | | | | [](https://irrem7hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001ZkFZtASYL_HW_tpLw24qJF7M4V182uYzUtPHDlq_YLWqYJv9tftVv2ZwnjHl-0wtMyC1Z5IZwtpPS31JqCDNuPxa2Z7uckDFOugEfLCZKQ9prdQslfs07K7WJ82_RsGbNyESVIVc7-vinvWbvCGWucpxz6uU_9N1Lsq3jRMSaU1QQZdKZVrWXFDFcdz_C8K4WUZvyRhE6rVh3aEtr_KMl835zISDciGDl6CthrWHAgOjek5V3PTFby4VfSGH7fWk&c=q93nXXDRPwH5ZdOq6McgK2j2g75LjSfxCz2YZ_c41hY9Lw4mWIf6HA==&ch=IlX1mwVc7x4ooQbuKv7GFYKVu-0QBEExPFbiuG_-xOXcZbwjETItUg==)
---
| Peter,
In the past many weeks, people have asked me, "How are you feeling?" And I've had just the hardest time articulating how I feel.
So I just default to saying, "I'm excited!"
But now that Tuesday's win is official, I want to tell you how incredibly proud and honored I am to be part of this movement for a better world that so many of you have been building for years and years.
Over the last several months, I've heard people talk about this being their first time canvassing, how nervous they were, and how much it mattered to them to overcome that fear for the DSA slate.
I started canvassing in 2019 when Bernie was running for president. I remember being so frightened the first time I knocked on somebody's door. But it was people in this movement who encouraged me to keep going. They said, "No, just come back. You'll get it next time."
When they asked me to be a field coordinator, I said, "I don't actually think that that's a very good idea." And they said, "No, it's okay. We've got you."
That's exactly what we're doing now. We're building the next generation of organizers who will transform our society, and we're doing it together.
And it's not just in New York City. We're leading in this fight against fascism - not just against the Trump administration - but the fascism of huge corporations and billionaires, and the first trillionaires, and the empires these tech oligarchs are building to extract every moment of joy and human creativity and beauty out of our lives for profit. We're standing up against them.
Thanks to you, a UAW organizer is going to represent New York's Seventh Congressional District.
And I'm not going in alone. I'm going to Congress with a class of people who know that the billionaire class is our enemy, and that together we can pass Medicare for All, make it easier to organize a union, abolish ICE, and end the genocide in Gaza.
Thank you for believing a better world is possible. Thank you for fighting for it.
In solidarity forever, Claire Valdez

## Hinojosa, Talarico Swearing-In Dates
Democrats Gina Hinojosa and James Talarico won two of Texas' biggest races Tuesday, as Hinojosa unseated Republican Gov. Greg Abbott and Talarico [beat Attorney General Ken Paxton](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD3u3CAQR0-DO1Ywxh8ULtK4-6dNaY3xsCbBsILJsrl95Fwh3ZNm9KT3-_G1fWGIIT2_40ULf3zeErUaiZnKdtCVXUGujL-oMjKd-XclnzdQMEqtpRo2dBzetOnuWHZ1WN3Roifbz7NS1nTnMjvvtMdpH0dPABZAGzjQWNy13z12YbltWqtBg9K9evT9YMbBjgot0GgPYRQdgXN58ElMH6w-_slvKg-Xry4uJ_Oriv6bgFXA2lp73A2NKtv7Q8CKhYOLJGC9LwLWV46Bg7uRIjkOOd3cTkqyhRglnyQTNelyehaqVe4ka8slyZDkT7yoSsaIJbgsYIV5kJMiZWlAeSg7SzMrJ_cBtXRmVJPxOzlyXVmO1-0PdZyEUc8LQ_xXwf85_nuBvwEAAP__hwOZyQ) to become the state's first Democrat U.S. senator since 1993. Talarico will be [sworn in at noon Jan. 3](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGS6yAMRb_G7vAIsAkUFK9Jl9du6dHacswuhoxR4uTvd8h-wpYaaa7OuR-X8YIhhnT9jxt5fi55THSUSMy0jzNtedqRC-M3FUamNd8LLXlUoIyQUsAw4sThQaNsZ_8Js5MteXly2loA17ern7W2Wg_WgrJ2IAWg1YLgrCNjjcY2-JomJQxSgdTQaT30ZnAG0Ckybm56oDlw3jteiemJZYmv_KC9m_LWRr8y30qj_zXq3KjzcRzdkp_KVFbOqR416ly16nalJL5woyIYI-5hyuIIMYq8LGEKGONLVNvfmcSBZQ3pyjmJ92eR6BB3UUShhJz3dvfzrQaEYk5ND9cNQ3xz8R_rfHj1EwAA___o2oxx), when the new Congress convenes in Washington. First, state officials must certify the final vote and issue his official election certificate, and his six-year term will run through early 2033. Hinojosa waits a bit longer. The Texas Constitution sets [her inauguration for Jan. 19](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL1ygzAQhJ8GOjGS-LMKFWnonDYlc4YDLhE6j3Q2zttn8Cuk22Jnv939uo5XoEBx_YQdvbwWHiMeOaAIpnHGnacEkgV-MAsIbvzIuPBote2UMUq3I0xCTxxNOfubnp0p0Zve1ZeL1q4pN983xoLrdXubmu7iHLYwQQ_Qt65fzA1K8meaMbo1VptaV3XdNl3rOg3OYufmotE4k3CqZEPBF-Ql_PITUzXxXga_idxzUX8UdijscBxHtfCrOXechsIOpyzssGFCRVlNHLOQPIQ4QlBCOwaKqI4No1opgtoo8jdnUJDzY8eseFloQvWGq_VkR05l8vP9oBAod33R6HUHCu9O8s8rn97-BQAA__9A_Yyj), the third Tuesday of January, when she'll become the state's first Latina governor and first Democrat governor since Ann Richards left office in 1995. Hours after the wins, the pair headed to Whataburger. Talarico [posted a photo of them](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLFy5CAQRL8GZWzBSGiXgOASMl96oWoEo4UzEi4Yr3x_fyX_gpNOuqpfd_95W94wl3w8f-NOjr-2uhx09kLM1JZIew0NuTO-U2dkSvWz01YXUDBLraUyCwbOL1r0EN2qotUDOX234-OhlJ2G5IKxYIKdHzHOG5hNrWY1k472rmkdNQ3ZXWlaK6NB6VHdxtFMs7GzQgs02ygmRTFzbTdOxPSFfSv_6ovaLdR9KC4xf3Qx_hLgBfjzPG_vHfkyBfhrjgBfasAiwF8oAV5rAV5NAjxjwZZDlXhEmfJR_9aOMlChtSGTTLlzbTnIb7A883EJJ4nyTMi4frYnNckVOwvwQ3Px48yl5D7fxaSeO-by3ZN_eO_Lwf8AAAD__9ERj_A) grinning and clinking oversized orange-and-white cups as supporters packed the restaurant, captioned "_First stop post-win: Whataburger_."
## Democrats Take House, GOP Holds Senate
Texas Democrats [took control of the state House](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkbvO3CAQhZ8Gd6y42bsUFGno_rQpLQxjGwWDBbOXvH2E9SsvkHqOPp3vzK-v-cvFFPP20x1g8LOWOcO7JUCEOgc4iq8OG7rf0NAh7OXZYC2zYGKinFM2zs5jfMHMh2AWFjQfwPC7lo8HY1oNu5GPZVnuD-V10BC8ZJPiiwx6XLhwaoUhmk7jnI1cMC7ZTcpRTaOemNMCJh2IYhAilnrDHRA-rq3pT3lBvflyDMnsiGcj8gcRlgjbTvBYn0cq3qUu01NEWPz0Y3niTi8GhURP1woRtqeIsL0GEZZzIixTRNh__vQdM_UlYy2JlvUbcC1Cr0moa_R0FfuxvQHOmDe6uZgbjfk7uPXK-YCMbagmnO-YUmzTnSi2HS6mywb_8wkvI_4GAAD__9Cpn1Y) in Tuesday's elections. The win ends a Republican majority that began with the 2002 election and gives Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa allies at the Capitol. The latest AP count available Wednesday gave Democrats [76 seats to Republicans' 61](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2SrCAQRp8GMy0aFSUguInZ3HRDqwfakVqUKWjH2bffGl9h8--nzvm6zTcMMeyP_7iR5feS5p3OEomZ8uxpSy4jF8ZvKoxMazoKLWlWUukaoJb9jI7Di2aovL1Lb6AiC4Npx1FK01WrxV75-4DjOGpsO-dAL8oMA4weunsvoQr2swYge1ASWtm0bd_p3miJRpE2XnSSfOCUG16J6Y1liT_pRblxaauiXZmfRbT_hJqEms7zbJb0HvAoHPZPRKjpAyXUdJVriuQ4pL3OVI7Ipb7Q6kiPUCLykanK1j_PEGMoehCdfGwY4vXGf5T0suo3AAD__-I8fcs), the bare majority in the 150-member chamber, with 13 races still uncalled. Texas last had a split Legislature in the late 1990s and early 2000s. Republicans kept their 19-12 Senate majority after the AP called the last race in play just before 1 p.m. Wednesday. In that race, District 2, Republican state Sen. Bob Hall beat Democrat Keenen Colbert 51.4% to 48.6%. Divided control means [bills will need bipartisan support](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDHSpCAQhU-DmVY3KkpAsInZbLqhxUAzUoNiSa_O3n7LucKf9lf96n3vz2N-2Jji9vptVzL8CXne6CqJmOmYPa3ZHZYL2zcVtkxL_lso5FmCVDViDf1sHceTZqy8eYLXWJHBQbfjCKC7ajHj0I_UIyAG6L17ehyV1ENLGMIYnKqiudMQoUcJ2ELTtn2neq3AaklKe9EB-cj5aHghpo8tIf3LJx2Ny2uVzMK8F9H-EnIScrquq3l_7HZDIadbR8jp-1bvOUWO7j7suXBNiRzHvNUS5FAnesWS7K1TFyrlBvtBZ6RLyKk6jN-vmFIsahAdvFYb07cB_3C408j_AQAA__-G8YP4). The budget starts in the House, and Hinojosa will hold a veto that takes two-thirds of each chamber to override. Democratic Lt. Gov.-elect Vikki Goodwin will preside over the GOP-led Senate.
## Voters Reject School Bonds, Tax Hikes
Texas voters rejected school bonds and tax increases from El Paso to Houston on Tuesday, including [all 19 school funding measures](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkbGOpDAMQL8GOo-SEEIoKK6h22uvRCZxlmgCQYl32P37E1ucrt_GepKlJz_5z9vyhjHF4_037jTxZ8jLQVdNxExl8bRnV5Ar45MqI9OWPyqFvCihDEgJol_QcXzRIls_rcKPsqVJDmNnrRCjbrcpyCF4ozURSmnMirYT3qjVKsJgw9rG6bZJKXqphOzEo-t6bfrRCBwVmdE3WpCPnMuDN2L6xBrSV35Rebi8t2namM_adL8aNTdqvq7rcQXEe9moGQtHl6hR8x3WqPnMKXJ0N1IixzEf_zNUt-WcYM2Hh7PkM1dMFU6sFQLGBE9KiQrs7hmPg77gyIU3-D4L_kkK1Y_Et1fZAZTwI6l-hXuCttbBisMKVvteE-KInWnL5M8rphSrGRot3neM6TuQf_iX16T-BgAA__8i_aR1) on North Texas ballots, where Keller ISD alone sought about $828 million for campus repairs, technology, and turf. Patriot,

I’ll be honest with you. I’m frustrated with how the 2026 midterms turned out, and if you’re reading this, I’d guess you are too.

Look at what we watched happen this cycle. On Election Day, ballot scanners failed across Westchester County, New York, in one of the closest House races in the country, held by a Republican incumbent, and poll workers stuffed completed ballots into emergency bags saying they would just be counted later.

In California, federal officials flagged roughly 20,000 likely non-citizens who had been mailed ballots, and an appeals court let the state count them anyway.

New Jersey admitted it found 6,600 non-citizens on its own voter rolls.

And in one California county, election staff opened a locked drop box and found nearly 600 sealed ballots that had sat there uncounted for five months after the election was certified.

On top of all that, the Supreme Court ruled this summer that 14 states and D.C. can keep counting mail ballots that arrive after Election Day. Election Day is supposed to mean one day.

After a night like this, it’s tempting to tune out and wait for things to cool down. I understand that feeling. But these problems don’t fix themselves between elections. If we look away now, every one of them will be bigger in 2028, and liberals will do everything they can to steal the presidential election.

SAVE OUR ELECTIONS!

I serve on the board of Save Election Day. We’re a team of volunteer election lawyers who have worked Election Days, early voting, and recounts, so we’ve seen these problems up close.

We’re a 501(c)4 non-profit founded for one purpose: to carry President Trump’s election reforms into the states and turn them into law.

Here’s why the states matter. Washington, D.C. keeps introducing election bills that stall, and even when Congress acts, elections are still run under state law. So we write the bills, push them through statehouses, and take the fight straight to voters with ballot measures where legislatures won’t move.

Our goals are simple:

- Photo voter ID for every voter
- One national Election Day, with results on Election Night
- No more ballots counted days after the polls close
- Shorter mail-in and early voting windows
- Only American citizens voting in American elections

We’re already at work in states like Nevada and Georgia, and we’re ready to expand. The time to protect 2028 is right now, while legislatures prepare for their next sessions. By the time the presidential race heats up, the rules will already be set.

name: Ted Cruz
subject: History was made this week...
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Ted Cruz for Senate
body:
| | | | _**FROM THE DESK OF SENATOR TED CRUZ **_
---
| | | Fellow Conservative,
---
History was made this week...

For months, we were saying that 2026 was the most consequential midterm election of our lifetimes.

Unfortunately, we were right. Sometimes history is to be celebrated; other times, it is to be mourned. Always, it must be reckoned with.

2026 was not simply a blue wave; it was a blue tsunami. It was an ass kicking. It was not simply a bad 2006 midterm election. It was a Watergate-level repudiation. What happened, and why? What are the consequences, and where on earth do we go from here?

When all the votes were counted, the problem wasn't turnout. Instead, our voters, Republicans, Libertarians, Independents, showed up and voted, and rejected our candidates, voting Democrat instead. We've lost the House. We've lost the Senate. When all is said and done, we will have lost eight to 10 Senate seats.

We lost in historically red states, like South Carolina and North Carolina, Kansas and Iowa. We lost in purple states, like Michigan, and New Hampshire, and Georgia. And we just barely won by just a single point in bright red states like Florida and Louisiana, and then there's Texas.

Nowhere are the consequences of this election greater than Texas. In the Lone Star State, we lost every single statewide election. For weeks, I had been publicly warning on this podcast that we were in very real danger of losing everything in Texas. Far too few believed that was possible. I am very, very sorry that it came to pass. Texas has not had a Democrat governor since 1994. We haven't had a Democrat senator since 1993. Now we'll have both.

Why were the results so overwhelming? Pundits and analysts will break down the results for weeks or months or even years to come, but several things are already evident today.

Years ago, the very best political advice I ever got was from Heidi. She said, "It's not about you. It's about them. It's about their kids, their families, their hopes, their dreams, their futures." Too many politicians forget that.

Take the state of Kansas, for example, a state that has not elected a Democrat senator since 1932. It just did. Here's what exit polling showed were the top issues in Kansas.

Number one, cost of living, energy, and groceries. That was listed as number one by 30.6 percent of voters.
Corruption. Number two, 18.5%.
The cost of the Iran war, 10.1%.
The candidates are terrible, 7.9%.
The Canada trade war, 7.6%.
The GOP didn't do enough to support Trump, 6.6%.
Republicans didn't pass the Save America Act, 5.6%.
Trump's focus on monuments, 5.5%, and data centers and AI, 3.8%...

The top issue, cost of living, is very real. Too many in politics dismissed it. They didn't understand. They pointed to the macro numbers showing the stock markets soaring, median income at record highs, and poverty at record lows. Those data are true, but they don't tell all of the story.

Here are some stats that are a lot more real and personal. Spam, Hormel's processed meat substitute, broke record sales, selling 113 million cans last year. That is nearly as much spam as was sold during the entirety of World War II. 29 percent of Americans have used buy now, pay later for groceries this year. That's double the share just two years ago.

In August, banks repossessed 42% more homes than they did last year. In 2024, car repossessions topped 2.3 million, above the 2009 peak in the middle of the Great Financial Crisis. In 2025, 6% of 401k holders took hardship withdrawals, paying penalties. That is a record, and triple the norm.

And here's one that's really stunning. Americans made more than 75 million paid plasma donations in 2026. That's another record. That means 200,000 Americans every single day, with a needle in their arm, just to pay for groceries.

That is very real pain from real Americans, and too many Republican politicians seem like they didn't understand or they didn't care. Food is too high, gas is too high, diesel is too high, insurance is too high, life is too high.

Tariffs have made everything too expensive, and the Iran war has dragged on too long. It should have been brief, decisive, and over. It needs to end, and we should never, under any circumstances, give the Ayatollah billions of dollars.

There's a very real economic disconnect. Our K-shaped economy is a yawning divide. Last year, we saw the world's very first trillionaire, a modern-day Thomas Edison, at the very same time that millions were struggling to feed their families. Data centers being constructed were turning billionaires into centibillionaires, while simultaneously the average American's electricity bill went up 30% in the last five years.

Understandably, people were pissed off, and elected Republicans didn't do enough to address their very real pain.

So, what do we do now? We need to listen and respond. We need to champion economic policies that make a real difference in working people's lives, and we need to deal with the consequences.

Texas is blue. That is a hard sentence to utter. But Texas, today at least, is blue. As we sit here today, I am the only statewide elected Republican who remains in Texas. That's not something I ever thought I would say.

We can be certain that the Democrats in Austin and in Washington will overshoot. In Texas, they will try to raise taxes dramatically. They may even try to adopt a state income tax, or even a California wealth tax. They will try to shut down the energy industry, destroying jobs across our state. They will embrace the radical transgender agenda. They will persecute those they perceive to be enemies, especially Elon Musk.

And in Washington, they will attack Trump every single day, constantly. Impeachment hearings, subpoenas, his family, cabinet members, business leaders, open persecution, and nonstop retaliation. Make no mistake. Nationally, the radicals are in charge. The communists and the Islamists who have taken over the Democrat Party have now taken over the United States Congress. They will be unleashed.

Sadly, that means many Americans will be hurt. Texans will be hurt. Their assault on business will make Texas a much less attractive place to start or grow a small business. Texas will become more like California if they succeed in halting all new investment into AI.

The economic results will be dramatic. Over $700 billion in new projects are scheduled to start in the next year. If the Democrats shut them all down, our country will very likely go into a recession. That will suit the Democrats just fine. They'll just blame it all on Donald Trump.

In the next two years, we need to do two things.

One, fight the madness. I will work with Democrats when they're willing to be reasonable. Last night, I called James Talarico. I congratulated him on his very impressive victory. It was a pleasant conversation, and I told him that I looked forward to working with him to try to benefit Texas.

So, if there are things like flood relief for the Hill Country, or trying to get the space academy to Texas, he and I will work together. But if the newly elected radicals push policies that hurt Texas, raising taxes, destroying jobs, opening the border, releasing violent criminals, threatening our children, undermining our constitutional rights, I will fight with all of my strength to defend Texas and to defend the Constitution.

And number two, we need to rebuild, getting behind policies that directly benefit the constituents we lost.

There's a complicated story, no doubt, of what happened on Election Day, but as I see it, the key constituencies we lost were blue-collar voters, what had rightly become the core base of our party, Evangelical Christians, who didn't show up with the same numbers and fervor as prior elections, farmers and ranchers. Tragically, we alienated rural America. Young people, who excitedly had voted Republican in 2024, and who shifted hard blue this cycle. And of course, Hispanics.

For Hispanics, there's a strong overlap with young people and blue-collar workers. In 2024, just two years ago, I was proud to carry Hispanics statewide in Texas by six points, and we swung the Rio Grande Valley red for the first time in a century. It can be done, but in this election, those Hispanic voters overwhelmingly went back Democrat. We have got to turn that around.

And for young people, we need to be the party of the future. We need to champion policies that expand their future. Our two single biggest legislative accomplishments of the past two years, Trump Accounts and the school choice tax credit, which will unleash tens of billions of dollars in new scholarships for kids, are generationally powerful. I was proud to author both of those transformational policies, and yet too few candidates all across the country ran on that record.

Too few voters were even aware of what we'd accomplished for their kids and their future. But we need to build. We need to expand to continue creating a new investor class for hundreds of millions of Americans, help everyone, every American, become an owner, to have real skin in the game, to create new generations of capitalists ready to reject socialism.

People voted as they did because they were angry. Ironically, the Democrats that they elected are going to advance policies that will make affordability worse. The Democrats want gas prices higher. They want to ban gasoline engines altogether. Their extreme environmental mandates will drive up food prices and the prices of everything else.

But hear me now: we will bring Texas back. I am filled with hope and optimism. Texas will be red again. We have not suddenly become a bunch of tofu-eating, gun-banning, tutu-wearing pinko commie liberals. That ain't us. Texas is still Texas.

We will rebuild as a true blue-collar party, not by embracing socialism, but by being real free-market conservatives. The way we built the Texas economic miracle in the first place, and we will build and rebuild America as well.

When the zealots overreach, and they will, we will stand ready to lead in the direction of freedom, of prosperity, of safety, and security, and common sense. We will return to a new dawn of freedom in America.

It is dark right now, but it is always darkest before the dawn, and morning is coming. That is my fervent prayer, and that is my commitment to you.
---
Thank you,
---
---
Ted Cruz

clean_body: | | | | FROM THE DESK OF SENATOR TED CRUZ | | | Fellow Conservative, History was made this week... For months, we were saying that 2026 was the most consequential midterm election of our lifetimes. Unfortunately, we were right. Sometimes history is to be celebrated; other times, it is to be mourned. Always, it must be reckoned with. 2026 was not simply a blue wave; it was a blue tsunami. It was an ass kicking. It was not simply a bad 2006 midterm election. It was a Watergate-level repudiation. What happened, and why? What are the consequences, and where on earth do we go from here? When all the votes were counted, the problem wasn't turnout. Instead, our voters, Republicans, Libertarians, Independents, showed up and voted, and rejected our candidates, voting Democrat instead. We've lost the House. We've lost the Senate. When all is said and done, we will have lost eight to 10 Senate seats. We lost in historically red states, like South Carolina and North Carolina, Kansas and Iowa. We lost in purple states, like Michigan, and New Hampshire, and Georgia. And we just barely won by just a single point in bright red states like Florida and Louisiana, and then there's Texas. Nowhere are the consequences of this election greater than Texas. In the Lone Star State, we lost every single statewide election. For weeks, I had been publicly warning on this podcast that we were in very real danger of losing everything in Texas. Far too few believed that was possible. I am very, very sorry that it came to pass. Texas has not had a Democrat governor since 1994. We haven't had a Democrat senator since 1993. Now we'll have both. Why were the results so overwhelming? Pundits and analysts will break down the results for weeks or months or even years to come, but several things are already evident today. Years ago, the very best political advice I ever got was from Heidi. She said, "It's not about you. It's about them. It's about their kids, their families, their hopes, their dreams, their futures." Too many politicians forget that. Take the state of Kansas, for example, a state that has not elected a Democrat senator since 1932. It just did. Here's what exit polling showed were the top issues in Kansas. Number one, cost of living, energy, and groceries. That was listed as number one by 30.6 percent of voters. Corruption. Number two, 18.5%. The cost of the Iran war, 10.1%. The candidates are terrible, 7.9%. The Canada trade war, 7.6%. The GOP didn't do enough to support Trump, 6.6%. Republicans didn't pass the Save America Act, 5.6%. Trump's focus on monuments, 5.5%, and data centers and AI, 3.8%... The top issue, cost of living, is very real. Too many in politics dismissed it. They didn't understand. They pointed to the macro numbers showing the stock markets soaring, median income at record highs, and poverty at record lows. Those data are true, but they don't tell all of the story. Here are some stats that are a lot more real and personal. Spam, Hormel's processed meat substitute, broke record sales, selling 113 million cans last year. That is nearly as much spam as was sold during the entirety of World War II. 29 percent of Americans have used buy now, pay later for groceries this year. That's double the share just two years ago. In August, banks repossessed 42% more homes than they did last year. In 2024, car repossessions topped 2.3 million, above the 2009 peak in the middle of the Great Financial Crisis. In 2025, 6% of 401k holders took hardship withdrawals, paying penalties. That is a record, and triple the norm. And here's one that's really stunning. Americans made more than 75 million paid plasma donations in 2026. That's another record. That means 200,000 Americans every single day, with a needle in their arm, just to pay for groceries. That is very real pain from real Americans, and too many Republican politicians seem like they didn't understand or they didn't care. Food is too high, gas is too high, diesel is too high, insurance is too high, life is too high. Tariffs have made everything too expensive, and the Iran war has dragged on too long. It should have been brief, decisive, and over. It needs to end, and we should never, under any circumstances, give the Ayatollah billions of dollars. There's a very real economic disconnect. Our K-shaped economy is a yawning divide. Last year, we saw the world's very first trillionaire, a modern-day Thomas Edison, at the very same time that millions were struggling to feed their families. Data centers being constructed were turning billionaires into centibillionaires, while simultaneously the average American's electricity bill went up 30% in the last five years. Understandably, people were pissed off, and elected Republicans didn't do enough to address their very real pain. So, what do we do now? We need to listen and respond. We need to champion economic policies that make a real difference in working people's lives, and we need to deal with the consequences. Texas is blue. That is a hard sentence to utter. But Texas, today at least, is blue. As we sit here today, I am the only statewide elected Republican who remains in Texas. That's not something I ever thought I would say. We can be certain that the Democrats in Austin and in Washington will overshoot. In Texas, they will try to raise taxes dramatically. They may even try to adopt a state income tax, or even a California wealth tax. They will try to shut down the energy industry, destroying jobs across our state. They will embrace the radical transgender agenda. They will persecute those they perceive to be enemies, especially Elon Musk. And in Washington, they will attack Trump every single day, constantly. Impeachment hearings, subpoenas, his family, cabinet members, business leaders, open persecution, and nonstop retaliation. Make no mistake. Nationally, the radicals are in charge. The communists and the Islamists who have taken over the Democrat Party have now taken over the United States Congress. They will be unleashed. Sadly, that means many Americans will be hurt. Texans will be hurt. Their assault on business will make Texas a much less attractive place to start or grow a small business. Texas will become more like California if they succeed in halting all new investment into AI. The economic results will be dramatic. Over $700 billion in new projects are scheduled to start in the next year. If the Democrats shut them all down, our country will very likely go into a recession. That will suit the Democrats just fine. They'll just blame it all on Donald Trump. In the next two years, we need to do two things. One, fight the madness. I will work with Democrats when they're willing to be reasonable. Last night, I called James Talarico. I congratulated him on his very impressive victory. It was a pleasant conversation, and I told him that I looked forward to working with him to try to benefit Texas. So, if there are things like flood relief for the Hill Country, or trying to get the space academy to Texas, he and I will work together. But if the newly elected radicals push policies that hurt Texas, raising taxes, destroying jobs, opening the border, releasing violent criminals, threatening our children, undermining our constitutional rights, I will fight with all of my strength to defend Texas and to defend the Constitution. And number two, we need to rebuild, getting behind policies that directly benefit the constituents we lost. There's a complicated story, no doubt, of what happened on Election Day, but as I see it, the key constituencies we lost were blue-collar voters, what had rightly become the core base of our party, Evangelical Christians, who didn't show up with the same numbers and fervor as prior elections, farmers and ranchers. Tragically, we alienated rural America. Young people, who excitedly had voted Republican in 2024, and who shifted hard blue this cycle. And of course, Hispanics. For Hispanics, there's a strong overlap with young people and blue-collar workers. In 2024, just two years ago, I was proud to carry Hispanics statewide in Texas by six points, and we swung the Rio Grande Valley red for the first time in a century. It can be done, but in this election, those Hispanic voters overwhelmingly went back Democrat. We have got to turn that around. And for young people, we need to be the party of the future. We need to champion policies that expand their future. Our two single biggest legislative accomplishments of the past two years, Trump Accounts and the school choice tax credit, which will unleash tens of billions of dollars in new scholarships for kids, are generationally powerful. I was proud to author both of those transformational policies, and yet too few candidates all across the country ran on that record. Too few voters were even aware of what we'd accomplished for their kids and their future. But we need to build. We need to expand to continue creating a new investor class for hundreds of millions of Americans, help everyone, every American, become an owner, to have real skin in the game, to create new generations of capitalists ready to reject socialism. People voted as they did because they were angry. Ironically, the Democrats that they elected are going to advance policies that will make affordability worse. The Democrats want gas prices higher. They want to ban gasoline engines altogether. Their extreme environmental mandates will drive up food prices and the prices of everything else. But hear me now: we will bring Texas back. I am filled with hope and optimism. Texas will be red again. We have not suddenly become a bunch of tofu-eating, gun-banning, tutu-wearing pinko commie liberals. That ain't us. Texas is still Texas. We will rebuild as a true blue-collar party, not by embracing socialism, but by being real free-market conservatives. The way we built the Texas economic miracle in the first place, and we will build and rebuild America as well. When the zealots overreach, and they will, we will stand ready to lead in the direction of freedom, of prosperity, of safety, and security, and common sense. We will return to a new dawn of freedom in America. It is dark right now, but it is always darkest before the dawn, and morning is coming. That is my fervent prayer, and that is my commitment to you. Thank you, Ted Cruz | | | | | | | | | | Paid for by Ted Cruz for Senate | | PO Box 25400 Houston, TX 77265 | | | To stop receiving emails from Ted Cruz for Senate, to unsubscribe.

body:
# [](https://act.janepac.com/go/30?t=1&akid=19%2E6803%2EnBsfiI)
Hi
We’re sure many of you, like us, are still celebrating Tuesday’s election victories and looking forward to what a new wave of leadership will accomplish at every level of government.
But as we celebrate, our current Congress is preparing legislation to gut some of America's most important environmental protections, and shockingly, Democrats are helping lead the charge. **[We need you to call your senators today and urge them to stop this dangerous legislation before it’s too late.](https://act.janepac.com/go/54?t=3&akid=19%2E6803%2EnBsfiI)**
The bill is called the _Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act_ , but don't let the name fool you. It threatens laws that have protected our air, water, wildlife, and public lands for decades, while giving polluters sweeping new rights to sue the government over permitting decisions.
This dangerous bipartisan Senate bill would speed up permitting and make it easier for fossil fuel companies, mining corporations, and Big Tech to bulldoze environmental safeguards, undermine Tribal sovereignty, and silence local communities. **It would also lock in the Trump Administration's fossil fuels approvals, and give them a _blank check_ to approve even more devastating projects over the next two years.**
And here's what's even more outrageous: Democratic Senators Martin Heinrich (NM) and Sheldon Whitehouse (RI) are sponsoring and advancing this legislation alongside Republicans, even as Donald Trump wages an all-out assault on our environment.
**And the clock is ticking.** **The Senate is scheduled to vote on November 9** on whether to advance this bill — just six days after the midterm elections. We cannot let Congress use a lame-duck session to gut hard-won environmental protections and hand Big Oil a victory that could haunt us for generations.
**[Will you call your Senators and urge them to oppose this dangerous permitting deal before the November 9 vote?](https://act.janepac.com/go/54?t=4&akid=19%2E6803%2EnBsfiI)**
**[Click to Call ››](https://act.janepac.com/go/54?t=5&akid=19%2E6803%2EnBsfiI)**
**To be clear, this is not just a tweak or small rollback of environmental protections** – it’s a massive shift away from protecting the public from corporations to protecting corporations from government oversight.
For decades, laws like the National Environmental Policy Act, Clean Water Act, National Historic Preservation Act, and Endangered Species Act have protected our drinking water, public lands, and Tribal cultural sites. But this bill would permanently erode those protections, make it almost impossible to challenge dangerous development projects, and strip communities of critical tools to prevent irreversible environmental damage.
And for what? To fast-track fossil fuel infrastructure and power-hungry AI data centers while leaving nearby residents to bear the consequences.
Some proponents of the bill say it will help accelerate clean energy development. Of course, we need to build clean energy faster. But stripping environmental safeguards to benefit corporations and tech billionaires isn't real climate progress. **It's a corporate handout.**
At a time when Trump is taking a wrecking ball to environmental safeguards, Congress should be fighting to protect them — not helping him finish the job.
With the November 9 vote fast approaching, we have a narrow window to stop this legislation. **[Will you call your Senators and urge them to oppose this dangerous permitting deal before the November 9 vote?](https://act.janepac.com/go/54?t=6&akid=19%2E6803%2EnBsfiI)**
**[Click here to get started.](https://act.janepac.com/go/54?t=7&akid=19%2E6803%2EnBsfiI)** Our calling tool will connect you directly to your senators. You can use the provided talking points, or speak from your heart and tell them why we must stop this bill.
Onward,
JanePAC Advocacy Team

[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ms_jfcp_em_footer?refcode=em20261105-19-&t=9&refcode2=19_6803_nBsfiI&akid=19%2E6803%2EnBsfiI)
---

On Wednesday, Thomas Aquinas College published a study it commissioned from the Johns Hopkins Institute for Education Policy: a side-by-side of the verbal sections of three official SAT practice tests -- 1980, 1987, and 2026. The headline on the college's own summary is admirably blunt: shorter passages, less vocabulary, more time. Read it as an epitaph for a measurement.
In 1980, sixty of the eighty-five verbal questions -- 70.6 percent -- tested vocabulary straight on. Antonyms, analogies, sentence completions: formats where you either owned the word or you didn't, with no helpful sentence nearby to plead your case. 1987 held the line. On the 2026 test, ten questions -- 15 percent -- touch vocabulary at all, and every one hands you a sentence and asks you to fill a blank using the words around it. The definition of the word is in the room with you. It is the world's most elaborate method of never having to know anything cold.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f7119483-7020-44b7-8d6c-220ba9c13592?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The passages tell the same story. The old exams averaged 300 to 340 words and leaned on argumentative and persuasive writing -- the kind that assumed you had met the Enlightenment somewhere before. The 2026 test averages about 97 words per passage and supplies whatever background the question needs inside the text. Nothing is assumed, because nothing is left to assume. Even the clock relents: "more time" per question is the third leg of the retreat...

Every fraternity has a house. Some are known for the keg on the porch; some for the couch the fire marshal condemned in 1997. The house at 111 Taylor Street in San Francisco's Tenderloin is known for a different kind of brotherhood: at least 31 registered sex offenders, a guard at the door, and a weekly meditation group -- because even predators need help staying centered.
Welcome to rush week. It never ends. The California Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation and the federal Bureau of Prisons keep offering bids, and the private GEO Group serves as house manager. The chapter sleeps 240, and the programming is genuinely inspiring: cultural diversity education, gender-responsive groups, and meditation. Nothing says rehabilitation quite like teaching a man to breathe deeply 400 feet from a daycare...

name: Chris Westfall
subject: Take Urgent Action for Wildlife: Tell your senators to oppose anti-ESA legislation!
body:
New legislation would harm imperiled wildlife and undermine the ESA – contact your senators today!

New legislation would harm imperiled wildlife and undermine the ESA – contact your senators today!
                  

(https://support.defenders.org/s/6253897/38SyG9Xl)

(https://support.defenders.org/s/6253898/38SyG9Xl)

SIGN NOW: Keep Threatened and Endangered Animals Protected! (https://support.defenders.org/s/6253899/38SyG9Xl)

Defender,

We want to let you know that your chance to speak up in defense of America’s imperiled wildlife is almost gone! (https://support.defenders.org/s/6253900/38SyG9Xl)

Next Monday, the Senate is poised to begin the voting process for one of the worst attacks we’ve seen on threatened and endangered wildlife, the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026, or BAAJA. If passed, this bill would make vast and dangerous changes to the Endangered Species Act, our country’s strongest tool for preventing extinction.

There is clear evidence that the ESA is not the obstacle to development that opponents claim it is. BAAJA would weaken fundamental wildlife protections without addressing the problems that actually slow development.

There is a better way forward! We can improve agency coordination, invest in modernized technology to process permits, and give federal agencies the resources they need to make timely decisions without sacrificing wildlife.

Send a message today telling your senators to vote NO on BAAJA! (https://support.defenders.org/s/6253901/38SyG9Xl)

BAAJA could cut the expert scientists at the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service out of reviewing and reducing the impacts of federal projects – like data centers on public lands - on endangered animals.

This change could have a clear and damaging impact: State agencies, many of which are already underfunded, would shoulder the burden of identifying if federal projects could harm endangered species, and they’d have to decide whether and how to protect any animals at risk.

Your senators need to hear from you now: Click here to send an urgent message telling them to protect endangered wildlife by voting NO on legislation that would make dangerous changes to the ESA! (https://support.defenders.org/s/6253902/38SyG9Xl)

The ESA currently requires federal agencies to consult with the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service to ensure federal actions don’t jeopardize an endangered species.

The new permitting legislation would hand over that authority to state agencies. Instead of one national process, we could have a slower, patchwork system of 50 states charged with protecting endangered wildlife without the resources or specialized knowledge they need to make informed decisions.

Now is the time to speak up to keep wildlife safe. Take a moment right now to send a message to your senators urging them to vote NO on BAAJA. We can build more infrastructure without sacrificing America’s wildlife! (https://support.defenders.org/s/6253903/38SyG9Xl)

DEEFEND AMERICA’S IMPERILED WILDLIFE! (https://support.defenders.org/s/6253904/38SyG9Xl)

Thank you for taking this important step on behalf of threatened and endangered animals.

Sincerely,

Chris Westfall

Sr. Government Relations Legislative Counsel

Defenders of Wildlife

(http://www.facebook.com/DefendersofWildlife) (http://twitter.com/defenders) (https://www.instagram.com/defendersofwildlife/?hl=en) (http://www.youtube.com/defendersofwildlife) (https://www.tiktok.com/@defendersofwildlife)

Defenders of Wildlife 1130 17th Street NW • Washington, DC 20036 defenders.org (https://defenders.org)

Inside this 532-page, beautifully bound volume, you'll journey through the entire year, five days a week, with devotionals arranged by season to help you grow spiritually:
---

* **Spring:** Prepare your heart for Holy Week as you reflect on our Lord Jesus Christ, then gain a clearer understanding of His role in God's plan for the end times.

name: Shelly Arnoldi
subject: Subject: Thank You!
body:
Lets make history in 2027! 166 Seats are open. Let’s Fill Them with Patriots!
| | | | |
---
| |
---
| Dear Neighbors,
Thank you to everyone who supported me, especially those who took the time to send an email or make a call simply to be kind. Your encouragement meant more than you know. My goal has always been to reach neighbors one at a time--face to face and conversation by conversation.
My goal all along was to show regular people how easy it is to get on the ballot. But we do need a team to actually make an impact. A team who will work for voters, not big donors or PACs.
Neither party is working for Northern Virginia. Dominion Energy, teachers' unions, and other special interests own the politicians. Taxes keep rising while uninformed voters allow the area to drift further left.

body:
A predator promised a mother a new life. Then one alarm changed everything.

| [View in Web Browser](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e6911774/VaHR0cHM6Ly93cm8ubnVjbGV1c2VtYWlsLmNvbS9hbXBsaWZ5L3YvUmRXc3VGQnBwSA/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjExMDU/LbmNsOVJEU0dMYQ/qP2hpZHM9bmNCNzBJMDllc3g3WXJscw/gauyQ-g/s8l1c180932)
| | | [](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e6911774/VaHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuc291bmRvZmZyZWVkb21mb3VuZGF0aW9uLm9yZy9zb2ZfbG9sYV8yMDI2X2FjcQ/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjExMDU/LbmNsOVJEU0dMYQ/qP3NvdXJjZV9jb2RlPVdBUlIxNTc0NDcmdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fc291cmNlPWhhcmRhc2tfYWNxJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1zb2ZfbG9sYV8yMDI2/gauyQ-g/s4hc0f9fa64)
---
| |
---
| | God’s Children Are Not For Sale
---
|
---
| | | Friend,
---
My name is Eduardo Verástegui.

I am the producer of the film _Sound of Freedom_ and the founder of **Sound of Freedom Foundation.**

Years ago, I met the people who rescue children from trafficking. When I heard what is done to these children, I asked myself one question:

** _What if it were my child?_**

That question changed my life. And it is why I am writing to you today.

I want to tell you about a little girl. For her safety, we call her “Lola.”
---
[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e6911774/VaHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuc291bmRvZmZyZWVkb21mb3VuZGF0aW9uLm9yZy9zb2ZfbG9sYV8yMDI2X2FjcQ/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjExMDU/LbmNsOVJEU0dMYQ/qP3NvdXJjZV9jb2RlPVdBUlIxNTc0NDcmdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fc291cmNlPWhhcmRhc2tfYWNxJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1zb2ZfbG9sYV8yMDI2/gauyQ-g/s4hc0f9fa64)
---
Lola’s mother was a hardworking single mom, doing everything she could for her little girl.

Then she met a man online.

He promised her the moon and the stars.

He traveled a long way to get them. He said his parents had a beautiful home in California and they would all be cared for.

**It was a lie.**

Soon, Lola and her mother were missing.

One of our house parents moved fast. Investigators believed the family had reached southern Mexico.

So she sounded the alarm.

**She worked with authorities to get an AMBER Alert out with Lola’s picture and pushed her case into the public eye.**
---
[ Sound the Alarm Now. Give Today ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e6911774/VaHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuc291bmRvZmZyZWVkb21mb3VuZGF0aW9uLm9yZy9zb2ZfbG9sYV8yMDI2X2FjcQ/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjExMDU/LbmNsOVJEU0dMYQ/qP3NvdXJjZV9jb2RlPVdBUlIxNTc0NDcmdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fc291cmNlPWhhcmRhc2tfYWNxJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1zb2ZfbG9sYV8yMDI2/gauyQ-g/s4hc0f9fa64)
---
And that very same day Lola was dropped off and left in front of child protective services.

Alone. Frightened. But alive.

Lola said her mother had died on the journey while she was crossing water. She could not swim.

We may never know what truly happened. But everything pointed to one terrible fear — that this man groomed her mother to get to her daughter. And that he planned to take Lola into the United States to be trafficked.

**But he did not get to keep her.**

**We stopped him.**

Today, Lola is safe. She was reunited with her grandparents and adopted by her loving aunt.
---
[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e6911774/VaHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuc291bmRvZmZyZWVkb21mb3VuZGF0aW9uLm9yZy9zb2ZfbG9sYV8yMDI2X2FjcQ/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjExMDU/LbmNsOVJEU0dMYQ/qP3NvdXJjZV9jb2RlPVdBUlIxNTc0NDcmdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fc291cmNlPWhhcmRhc2tfYWNxJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1zb2ZfbG9sYV8yMDI2/gauyQ-g/s4hc0f9fa64)
---
Friend, this is not a movie.

About two million children are exploited in the sex trade around the world, according to the U.S. State Department.

**Two million. Each one made in the image of God.**

Our nation was built on the belief that every life has worth because God gave it.

**That truth does not let us look away.**

Jesus said, “ _Let the little children come to me, and do not hinder them, for the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these._ ” (Matthew 19:14 NIV)

That is why **Sound of Freedom Foundation** exists — **to stop the sale of God’s children.**

And Lola’s story shows the most important truth of all: **children are found when people pay attention.**

Here is how you can join the fight today:

1\. **Stay alert.** Traffickers often start online with kindness and big promises.

2\. **If you see something, say something**. Read every AMBER Alert. Share it. If something feels wrong, call 911 or report a trafficking tip through **Sound of Freedom Foundation's** partner, Rescue America, at 1-833-599-3733.

3.**Make your first gift**. Help **Sound of Freedom Foundation** and our partners keep sounding the alarm.
---
[ Sound the Alarm Now. Give Today ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e6911774/VaHR0cHM6Ly9zZWN1cmUuc291bmRvZmZyZWVkb21mb3VuZGF0aW9uLm9yZy9zb2ZfbG9sYV8yMDI2X2FjcQ/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjExMDU/LbmNsOVJEU0dMYQ/qP3NvdXJjZV9jb2RlPVdBUlIxNTc0NDcmdXRtX21lZGl1bT1lbWFpbCZ1dG1fc291cmNlPWhhcmRhc2tfYWNxJnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj1zb2ZfbG9sYV8yMDI2/gauyQ-g/s4hc0f9fa64)

clean_body: A predator promised a mother a new life. Then one alarm changed everything. | | | | | | | | God’s Children Are Not For Sale | | | | Friend, My name is Eduardo Verástegui. I am the producer of the film Sound of Freedom and the founder of Sound of Freedom Foundation. Years ago, I met the people who rescue children from trafficking. When I heard what is done to these children, I asked myself one question: What if it were my child? That question changed my life. And it is why I am writing to you today. I want to tell you about a little girl. For her safety, we call her “Lola.” Lola’s mother was a hardworking single mom, doing everything she could for her little girl. Then she met a man online. He promised her the moon and the stars. He traveled a long way to get them. He said his parents had a beautiful home in California and they would all be cared for. It was a lie. Soon, Lola and her mother were missing. One of our house parents moved fast. Investigators believed the family had reached southern Mexico. So she sounded the alarm. She worked with authorities to get an AMBER Alert out with Lola’s picture and pushed her case into the public eye. And that very same day Lola was dropped off and left in front of child protective services. Alone. Frightened. But alive. Lola said her mother had died on the journey while she was crossing water. She could not swim. We may never know what truly happened. But everything pointed to one terrible fear — that this man groomed her mother to get to her daughter. And that he planned to take Lola into the United States to be trafficked. But he did not get to keep her. We stopped him. Today, Lola is safe. She was reunited with her grandparents and adopted by her loving aunt. Friend, this is not a movie. About two million children are exploited in the sex trade around the world, according to the U.S. State Department. Two million. Each one made in the image of God. Our nation was built on the belief that every life has worth because God gave it. That truth does not let us look away. Jesus said, “ Let the little children come to me, and do not hinder them, for the kingdom of heaven belongs to such as these. ” (Matthew 19:14 NIV) That is why Sound of Freedom Foundation exists — to stop the sale of God’s children. And Lola’s story shows the most important truth of all: children are found when people pay attention. Here is how you can join the fight today: 1\. Stay alert. Traffickers often start online with kindness and big promises. 2\. If you see something, say something. Read every AMBER Alert. Share it. If something feels wrong, call 911 or report a trafficking tip through Sound of Freedom Foundation's partner, Rescue America, at 1-833-599-3733. 3.Make your first gift. Help Sound of Freedom Foundation and our partners keep sounding the alarm. Your gift helps equip investigators to find children fast, sound the alarm through film and media, support house parents who welcome rescued children home, and teach everyone the warning signs. When good people keep quiet, they become part of the problem. But when good people speak up, God’s children come home. Tonight, a child is waiting to be found. body:
Latino voters led the way.
#
Peter,
**We’re celebrating major wins across the country this week.** People are calling it a blue tsunami, and honestly, even that doesn’t capture what just happened.
Americans voted this way because they’re tired — tired of rising prices, tired of being ignored, and tired of leaders who promised relief and delivered the opposite. And Latino voters led the way.
**An estimated 14.5 million Latinos voted in this midterm. Democratic House candidates won 69% of the Latino vote, a 29-point shift from 2024.**
Here’s just some of what we accomplished together because of your support:
* We won **20 out of 22 battleground districts** , and we’re keeping a close eye on Colorado’s 3rd Congressional District, which is still too close to call.

* **Gina Hinojosa** became the first Latina governor of Texas and unseated a three-time Republican incumbent.

* **James Talarico** flipped a U.S. Senate seat in Texas that hasn’t been held by a Democrat in more than three decades.

* Democratic candidates _**won four of five gerrymandered districts** _in Texas.

* **Keisha Lance Bottoms** made history as the first Black woman elected governor of any U.S. state.

* **Jon Ossoff** held his Senate seat in Georgia.

* **Roy Cooper** defeated a MAGA Republican and became the next U.S. Senator for North Carolina.

* **Katie Hobbs** won reelection in the Arizona Governor’s race.

* **Aaron Ford** unseated Republican Joe Lombardo to become Nevada’s next governor.

* **Josh Shapiro** won reelection in the Pennsylvania Governor’s race.

_**You helped make every one of these wins possible, Peter.**_
But if we want to protect the victories we won in 2026 and win even bigger in 2028, we can’t afford to take our foot off the gas.
**Most political donations dry up after Election Day, but the work doesn’t stop.** Your support right now is what lets us keep registering new voters and staying connected with Latino voters heading into 2027 and 2028.
**[Peter, if you want to help us step into this next phase on the right foot, will you make a donation of any amount right now?](https://act.votolatino.org/go/57?c0=em-ms-voto-20261105-1.1MEm63&amount=3&refcode=em20261105-759&t=1&akid=759%2E1366028%2EmDnfqQ)**

Thank you,
Voto Latino

Team, Elections around the country, from a U.S. Senate race in Mississippi down to local offices, could still come down to a handful of votes. In some cases, these are ballots that have been provisionally cast; in others, they are mail-in ballots with a small error that need to be "cured;" and in a lot of states, there are still valid, eligible ballots arriving in the so-called "grace period." That's where a ballot has been mailed and postmarked _before_ Election Day but is delivered in the next few business days _after_ Election Day. These ballots need to be counted. Voters who can fix and "cure" their ballots deserve the chance to do so. That's a key part of our fundamental right to vote. **[We hate to ask after all you've done so far, but will you pitch in with $35 or whatever you can to help us make every vote count in our elections?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142947688/658580008/-1725532854?refcode=110526_2&amount=35&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAwNy8xLzg5MjE1IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjc5ODBiMmI4LTI5ZDktZjExMS1iZjViLTAwMGQzYTU0NDQyZSIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=fqhhCvrROkIzmNirj2iXnZlgwTow4e68BiN3SCP0mQk=)**

Opponents of voting rights have attacked these mail-in ballot grace periods in the past and will be doing everything they can to get ballots tossed in this election or the next if we don't fight them. In a 5-4 decision back in June, the Supreme Court rejected arguments that federal laws setting Election Day preempted states from accepting ballots after that federally set date. This issue and so many others relating to mail-in voting rest on a knife's edge, where a differently argued case might have lost. We can't afford to lose vital protections for mail-in voting, not after all the progress this week. States count thousands of ballots after Election Day, from grace period ballots to votes provisionally cast to cured ballots. These votes deserve the same equitable treatment as the votes cast in-person during early voting or on Election Day. In some cases, these are ballots that have been provisionally cast; in others, they are mail-in ballots with a small error that need to be "cured;" and in a lot of states, there are still valid, eligible ballots arriving in the so-called "grace period." That's where a ballot has been mailed and postmarked before Election Day but is delivered in the next few business days after Election Day. These ballots need to be counted. Voters who can fix and "cure" their ballots deserve the chance to do so. That's a key part of our fundamental right to vote. = = Opponents of voting rights have attacked these mail-in ballot grace periods in the past and will be doing everything they can to get ballots tossed in this election or the next if we don't fight them. In a 5-4 decision back in June, the Supreme Court rejected arguments that federal laws setting Election Day preempted states from accepting ballots after that federally set date. This issue and so many others relating to mail-in voting rest on a knife's edge, where a differently argued case might have lost. We can't afford to lose vital protections for mail-in voting, not after all the progress this week. States count thousands of ballots after Election Day, from grace period ballots to votes provisionally cast to cured ballots. **November 5, 2026**
One of the sweetest chores in this time of holiday cheer has nothing to do with relaxing.
Preparing to make sugar syrup is work I have usually done by myself. There is something deeply personal about it, a creative connection between my hands and the harvest, just me and Nature.
"How can I help you, Ivette?"
I cut down the cane. She peeled the leaves. We hauled the stalks to the working station. I cut each one just so. She rinsed the pieces and placed them into the pots where they would turn, then filled the pots with water. Together, we lifted each one onto the fire.
We peered into the pots periodically, as one is wont to do after all that work . . .
Tiffany is my daughter-in-law. We were alongside one another that one season.
I watch the color change, the stalks soften, and breathe in the sweet aroma as it wafts throughout the house. After a measure of time, there it is: that deep golden, amber thickness, with a beauty and sweetness all its own.
I remember Tiffany, but on this day I remember her not with a heaviness of heart for the life she did not get to live, nor with sorrow for what I could not change, but with joy for the work we shared, through which I came to know her for who she was and who she wanted to be.
**Pause.
Breathe.
Look Deeper.**
**Refuel.**
**Welcome to Sweet Ground.**

On June 10, 2026, schoolteachers in one of the poorest corners of Louisiana opened the richest envelopes of their careers.
The checks came from the Richland Parish School Board's annual "13th check" -- a year-end bonus paid out of a local _sales tax_ that, for as long as anyone could remember, generated modest little stipends. The year before, vested teachers got about $10,000. That was already remarkable; most parishes pay nothing of the kind. This year, vested, certified teachers received $50,900. Support staff received more than $17,000. In some cases the bonus doubled a teacher's _annual salary_.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4314856c-f3d6-438d-8e1a-9a4a8e162267?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Richland Parish is a farming community of roughly 19,800 people in Louisiana's northeastern corner, with about 3,000 students and 164 classroom teachers. The median household income is about $53,500. Read those numbers together and you understand what actually happened: _a single bonus check equal to an entire year 's household income_, delivered not by a federal program, not by a grant application, not by an equity initiative -- but by a construction site.
**The Engine**
The engine is Meta's Hyperion data center near Holly Ridge, outside the parish seat of Rayville. Announced in December 2024 as a $10 billion, 2-gigawatt campus, it has since been expanded to 5 gigawatts, with cost estimates now running from $27 billion to $50 billion. It is projected to cover about six square miles and draw seven times as much electricity as the city of New Orleans. It is the _largest private investment in the history of Louisiana_.
The tax consequences were immediate. For the first nine months of the fiscal year, the parish collected $42.9 million in sales and use tax -- more than double the prior year, according to the Northwest Louisiana Finance Authority. Sandie Lollie, president of the Northeast Federation of Teachers and School Employees, put the school-dedicated share more vividly: "The taxes grew almost 2,000%." Meta also cut the parish a separate $22.4 million tax payment in May. More than $1.6 billion in contracts have gone to Louisiana businesses since construction began.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/40066bfb-28e5-492b-af4b-1077f2d85cf2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**Nobody Had to Redesign Anything**
Here is the detail that should make this story the conservative parable of the decade: _the mechanism predates the data center by decades_.
Richland Parish voters approved a dedicated school sales tax long before anyone in Rayville had heard of artificial intelligence. The "13th check" was already law, already administered, already funded. When Meta's capital crashed into that existing structure, the checks simply got bigger. No new agency. No federal compliance officer. No application, no means test, no pilot program with a five-year evaluation.
Washington's answer to underpaid rural teachers is always the same: a new program, a new office, a new acronym, and a takeaway for administration. Northeast Louisiana's answer was to make the parish a place where someone wanted to build something so enormous that the existing tax base doubled -- and the teachers got their cut, exactly as the voters who set up the tax always intended.
This is what it looks like when private capital does the work that redistribution only promises. The average federal teacher-quality program spends millions on administration to move thousands. Hyperion moved the actual money into actual local bank accounts in one fiscal year.
**" But Can It Last?"**
The objections arrived on schedule, so let's take them in order.
**First** : it's a sugar high. The New York Times ran the story under the headline "The A.I. Boom Boosted Teacher Pay in a Rural County. Can It Last?" -- and the point is fair. Data centers employ relatively few permanent workers once the cranes leave. Sales tax will normalize when construction ends.
But notice what the critics concede in making this argument. Superintendent Sheldon Jones anticipates "elevated bonuses for the duration of the Hyperion construction project" -- which is to say, for years, in a parish that had no comparable revenue source at all. Construction is a multi-year event, the windfall compounds, and Jones notes the multiplier effect: other industries are already looking at Richland Parish because the growth is visible. Neighboring parishes, the trade press reports, are now actively recruiting data centers of their own. The alternative on the table was not permanent prosperity. It was a parish that had been emptying out for a generation, collecting zero.
**Second** : corporate welfare. A Sherwood News analysis, picked up by Fortune, tallies roughly $3.3 billion in tax incentives Meta negotiated -- sales-and-use exemptions on its own equipment under Act 730, property tax abatements, a payments-in-lieu arrangement. The Times followed with an investigation titled "How Meta Got Everything It Wanted in a Secret Louisiana Data Center Deal."
Two responses. The first is arithmetic: an incentive is foregone revenue on a project that would not otherwise exist. The counterfactual was never Meta paying full freight in Richland Parish. It was Meta building in another state, and Richland Parish continuing its long decline with its pristine, un-discounted tax base -- still generating almost nothing. A 90%-off coupon on a $30 billion investment is a better deal than 100% of nothing.
The second response is to notice the irony. The same progressive commentators who shrug at billions in federal subsidies for politically favored industries -- EV credits, green-energy grants, Chips Act slush -- have discovered the phrase "corporate welfare" for a project that is actually building something, in a place the federal government forgot, and that just handed rural schoolteachers five-figure checks. Their objection is not that the money was wasted. It is that the money worked.
**Third** : the strain AKA real cost. Roads, water, the grid -- a project drawing seven times New Orleans' power is a genuine infrastructure event. Concede it plainly. It is also what the $22.4 million payment, and the payments that follow it, are for. Those are the growing pains of growth, which is a categorically different problem from the shrinking pains of decline Richland Parish had grown expert at managing.
**" Like Nobody's Ever Seen"**
President Trump says America is building data centers like nobody has ever seen before. For once, the boast undersells the record. In one rural Louisiana parish, an AI buildout doubled the local tax base in a single year and cut schoolteachers checks equal to a year's household income -- through a tax mechanism the voters themselves created, administered by a school board, with no one in Washington involved at any step of the transaction.
Major teachers' unions--primarily the National Education Association (NEA) and the **[American Federation of Teachers](https://substack.com/redirect/d2264926-009d-4004-93af-f2c78945330a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** (AFT)--have consistently directed **at least 94 percent** (with some reports and cycle estimates showing **98 to 99 percent**) of their direct candidate and political party contributions to Democrats. Does Republican Speaker of the House from Louisiana not now this?
That is the real contrast in American politics right now, and it is not between "pro-education" and "anti-education." It is between two theories of how teachers get paid more. One theory runs money through the federal government and calls whatever dribbles out a victory. The other theory builds a $30 billion machine in a cotton field and lets a parish sales tax do the rest.
Richland Parish chose the second theory. Its teachers got $50,900. Nobody had to fill out a federal form -- except Meta, for the bonuses' withholding, and it was glad to.

How an AI Data Center Did More for Rural Schools Than Any Federal Program | | | Nov 5 | | | | | | | | | | | | On June 10, 2026, schoolteachers in one of the poorest corners of Louisiana opened the richest envelopes of their careers. The checks came from the Richland Parish School Board's annual "13th check" -- a year-end bonus paid out of a local sales tax that, for as long as anyone could remember, generated modest little stipends. The year before, vested teachers got about $10,000. That was already remarkable; most parishes pay nothing of the kind. This year, vested, certified teachers received $50,900. Support staff received more than $17,000. In some cases the bonus doubled a teacher's annual salary. | | ---|---|--- Richland Parish is a farming community of roughly 19,800 people in Louisiana's northeastern corner, with about 3,000 students and 164 classroom teachers. The median household income is about $53,500. Read those numbers together and you understand what actually happened: a single bonus check equal to an entire year 's household income, delivered not by a federal program, not by a grant application, not by an equity initiative -- but by a construction site. The Engine The engine is Meta's Hyperion data center near Holly Ridge, outside the parish seat of Rayville. Announced in December 2024 as a $10 billion, 2-gigawatt campus, it has since been expanded to 5 gigawatts, with cost estimates now running from $27 billion to $50 billion. It is projected to cover about six square miles and draw seven times as much electricity as the city of New Orleans. It is the largest private investment in the history of Louisiana. The tax consequences were immediate. For the first nine months of the fiscal year, the parish collected $42.9 million in sales and use tax -- more than double the prior year, according to the Northwest Louisiana Finance Authority. Sandie Lollie, president of the Northeast Federation of Teachers and School Employees, put the school-dedicated share more vividly: "The taxes grew almost 2,000%." Meta also cut the parish a separate $22.4 million tax payment in May. More than $1.6 billion in contracts have gone to Louisiana businesses since construction began. | | ---|---|--- Nobody Had to Redesign Anything Here is the detail that should make this story the conservative parable of the decade: the mechanism predates the data center by decades. Richland Parish voters approved a dedicated school sales tax long before anyone in Rayville had heard of artificial intelligence. The "13th check" was already law, already administered, already funded. When Meta's capital crashed into that existing structure, the checks simply got bigger. No new agency. No federal compliance officer. No application, no means test, no pilot program with a five-year evaluation. Washington's answer to underpaid rural teachers is always the same: a new program, a new office, a new acronym, and a takeaway for administration. Northeast Louisiana's answer was to make the parish a place where someone wanted to build something so enormous that the existing tax base doubled -- and the teachers got their cut, exactly as the voters who set up the tax always intended. This is what it looks like when private capital does the work that redistribution only promises. The average federal teacher-quality program spends millions on administration to move thousands. Hyperion moved the actual money into actual local bank accounts in one fiscal year. " But Can It Last?" The objections arrived on schedule, so let's take them in order. First : it's a sugar high. The New York Times ran the story under the headline "The A.I. Boom Boosted Teacher Pay in a Rural County. Can It Last?" -- and the point is fair. Data centers employ relatively few permanent workers once the cranes leave. Sales tax will normalize when construction ends. But notice what the critics concede in making this argument. Superintendent Sheldon Jones anticipates "elevated bonuses for the duration of the Hyperion construction project" -- which is to say, for years, in a parish that had no comparable revenue source at all. Construction is a multi-year event, the windfall compounds, and Jones notes the multiplier effect: other industries are already looking at Richland Parish because the growth is visible. Neighboring parishes, the trade press reports, are now actively recruiting data centers of their own. The alternative on the table was not permanent prosperity. It was a parish that had been emptying out for a generation, collecting zero. Second : corporate welfare. A Sherwood News analysis, picked up by Fortune, tallies roughly $3.3 billion in tax incentives Meta negotiated -- sales-and-use exemptions on its own equipment under Act 730, property tax abatements, a payments-in-lieu arrangement. The Times followed with an investigation titled "How Meta Got Everything It Wanted in a Secret Louisiana Data Center Deal." Two responses. The first is arithmetic: an incentive is foregone revenue on a project that would not otherwise exist. The counterfactual was never Meta paying full freight in Richland Parish. It was Meta building in another state, and Richland Parish continuing its long decline with its pristine, un-discounted tax base -- still generating almost nothing. A 90%-off coupon on a $30 billion investment is a better deal than 100% of nothing. The second response is to notice the irony. The same progressive commentators who shrug at billions in federal subsidies for politically favored industries -- EV credits, green-energy grants, Chips Act slush -- have discovered the phrase "corporate welfare" for a project that is actually building something, in a place the federal government forgot, and that just handed rural schoolteachers five-figure checks. Their objection is not that the money was wasted. It is that the money worked. Third : the strain AKA real cost. Roads, water, the grid -- a project drawing seven times New Orleans' power is a genuine infrastructure event. Concede it plainly. It is also what the $22.4 million payment, and the payments that follow it, are for. Those are the growing pains of growth, which is a categorically different problem from the shrinking pains of decline Richland Parish had grown expert at managing. " Like Nobody's Ever Seen" President Trump says America is building data centers like nobody has ever seen before. For once, the boast undersells the record. In one rural Louisiana parish, an AI buildout doubled the local tax base in a single year and cut schoolteachers checks equal to a year's household income -- through a tax mechanism the voters themselves created, administered by a school board, with no one in Washington involved at any step of the transaction. Major teachers' unions--primarily the National Education Association (NEA) and the (AFT)--have consistently directed at least 94 percent (with some reports and cycle estimates showing 98 to 99 percent) of their direct candidate and political party contributions to Democrats. Does Republican Speaker of the House from Louisiana not now this? That is the real contrast in American politics right now, and it is not between "pro-education" and "anti-education." It is between two theories of how teachers get paid more. One theory runs money through the federal government and calls whatever dribbles out a victory. The other theory builds a $30 billion machine in a cotton field and lets a parish sales tax do the rest. Richland Parish chose the second theory. Its teachers got $50,900. Nobody had to fill out a federal form -- except Meta, for the bonuses' withholding, and it was glad to. ? | | ---|---|--- You're currently a free subscriber to . name: Chuck Rocha
subject: The Latino Vote in 2026: What We Built and What Comes Next
body:
The Latino vote shifted in 2026. Read Chuck Rocha's New York Times op-ed on what drove the gains and what comes next. | | | |
---
| | |
#### **The Latino Vote in 2026:
What We Built and What Comes Next**
---
|
---
| Friends,

The 2026 midterms marked a historic moment for Latino political engagement in America, and we're proud of the role Solidarity Strategies played in helping campaigns reach communities across the country through a multi-media, culturally competent winning strategy.

For decades, Latino voters have been overlooked in modern political communications, with Spanish-language outreach too often treated as an afterthought. This cycle, Democratic Leadership challenged that approach through unprecedented investments in Latino outreach, bilingual messaging, creative storytelling, and direct voter contact.

---
|
---
**_Campaigns Solidarity Strategies supported throughout the 2026 election cycle_**
| We worked on a combination of 32 competitive Senate, House, and Gubernatorial races this year in states and districts with significant Latino electorates to bring their messages to life by connecting the economic pain families were experiencing, raising questions about failed Republican leadership and corruption, and presenting the Democratic platform as an alternative offering solutions–all in English and Spanish.

**In a new New York Times op-ed, our founder and president Chuck Rocha reflects on the Latino vote in 2026, the lessons Democrats should take from this election, and why continued investment will be essential in the cycles ahead.**

[**Read Chuck Rocha's New York Times op-ed here**](https://us.list-manage.com/12tylKxj6Yy?e=b8f90417f9&c2id=150df94da93954b2128cfda2414939d1)

We should not mistake one election's progress for a permanent political realignment. Election Day may be behind us, but the work of earning and maintaining voters' trust is far from over.

¡Pa'lante!

**The Solidarity Strategies Team**

name: Christina (personal)
subject: A triumph for our district
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY CHRISTINA BOHANNAN FOR CONGRESS
body:
Thank you for everything

| Peter, there really are moments when words fail.

Yesterday was Election Day, and I'm still not sure I know how to tell you what this win means to me. I've tried to put my gratitude into words a dozen different ways, and every time, “thank you” doesn't seem like nearly enough.

Right now, I'm thinking about the people who gave up their evenings and weekends to knock on doors, who spent hours making phone calls, who donated money they had worked hard to earn, and who kept believing in this campaign even when we faced impossible odds. I wish I could thank each of you in person.

**It's hard to explain what this victory means without going back to the little girl I used to be.** Growing up, I never imagined I would run for office, let alone have the opportunity to serve in Congress. Politics felt a world away from our trailer door. When my Dad got sick, my family lost everything. We were figuring out what came next day by day, and I certainly wasn't imagining a future like this.

What I had, though, was a family who loved me, taught me to work hard, and showed me what it meant to keep going when life didn't go according to plan. My parents did everything they could to help me reach my potential, and my public school teachers helped me forge a path where I could get ahead and use my voice to help others do the same.

That's why I kept running for Congress. Despite the losses, every time I talked with a parent worried about their family's future, a farmer trying to keep their operation going, or a small-business owner struggling to stay afloat, I was reminded why I ran in the first place. **And this time, we did it.**

We built an extraordinary team and ran a campaign focused on the people of Iowa. We knocked on tens of thousands of doors, raised the resources to compete against a powerful political machine, and kept showing up, day after day. I think about the conversations on front porches, the people who opened their homes and told me about their lives, the volunteers who gave up their weekends, and the supporters who invested time and money to give this campaign a fighting chance.

I can't promise every challenge will have an easy answer, but I can promise I will bring everything I have to this responsibility. I'll keep you informed about what I'm doing, and I'll make sure the issues you care about are always front and center. I have so many plans for what we'll achieve for our district together, and so many things I'm dying to work on that I can barely sit still. I can't wait to officially be your representative, and I hope to make you proud.

Thank you for everything,

Christina P.S.
