| | | | | | Team Mackenzie,All I can say is thank you. Thank you for being part of something bigger than all of us and for showing your support in so many different ways.This campaign had it all. We had people willing to knock on doors, make phone calls, write postcards, work at the polls, and contribute financially. I am deeply humbled by the support our team has received and incredibly grateful for every person who gave their time, energy, and money.Two years ago, we set out to make a difference in the Lehigh Valley, and I am proud to say that we did. With your help, you sent me to Congress, where we resolved thousands of constituent cases, secured funding for community projects and first responders, and cast critical votes that helped the people of the Lehigh Valley and our beloved country.Obviously, the results did not go the way we had hoped. We saw crushing losses across the country. But I ask you not to give up. We won a race in 2024 that we were not supposed to win because people refused to give up and gave it their all. We gave it our all this year, but we came up short. That does not mean we will always come up short. It means we buckle down, learn from this experience, and work even harder.It has truly been an honor to serve as your congressman, and I will not stop working to deliver for the community I love.Thank you, and God bless you.Congressman Ryan Mackenzie

name: Justice Democrats
subject: Our 2026 midterm takeaways →
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY JUSTICE DEMOCRATS
body:
[1]Justice Democrats

Peter,

The 2026 midterms are over, and we just witnessed one of the largest and
most historic blue waves in U.S. history!

Democrats didn’t just take back the House. They secured a majority with
more than three dozen red-to-blue wins and flipped the Senate by at least
4 seats with 7 pickups — more than anyone expected.

So far, we’ve seen one win and one loss in the general election, with our
last race in California’s 7th district still too close to call. We’ll
update you as soon as we have those final results.

We already have some clear takeaways from this year’s midterm elections.
With a big jump in Democratic voter turnout across the country (especially
among young people), voters made their mandate very clear:

* Take on corporations to tackle the affordability crisis and lower
costs;
* End Donald Trump & Israel’s illegal war in Iran;
* End U.S. funding for Israel’s genocide and war crimes;
* Ban new data centers and regulate Big Tech;
* Fight corporate-backed MAGA fascism!

And those victories came in spite of the Democratic Party — not because of
it. Despite their unpopularity, the progressive movement drove excitement
by leading campaigns that centered working-class people nationwide and
gave voters something to believe in.

Another major takeaway? The establishment can no longer claim that
progressives — like Minnesota’s Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed — who support
bold policies like Medicare for All can’t win general elections.

Voters made it crystal clear: Democratic candidates don’t have to sell out
to corporate backers and lobby groups like AIPAC. They don’t have to throw
vulnerable communities like trans folks and immigrants under the bus.

In fact, when they do, they lose. Our voters want to reward our
candidates’ moral clarity & political courage.

Voters want fighters who are unbought and willing to be bold in order to
deliver real change for struggling working-class families and our
communities.

As we look ahead to the new Congress in 2027, one thing is for certain:
the Democratic Party better fight hard and go big, or their majority won't
last longer than a term.

These House and Senate majorities are too big and too important to waste.

No more strongly worded letters from Democratic leadership about Trump’s
unconstitutional actions.

No more putting off the bold and necessary policies we deserve — like
Medicare for All, raising the federal minimum wage, and a Green New Deal.

No more funding for endless wars & genocide for AIPAC.

In this second half of Trump’s presidency, it’s time for Democrats to
start acting like a true opposition party. Our bloc of progressive
champions is bigger than ever before, and they’re going to fight like hell
to lead the way.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20261105.wVGq-8&refcode=em20261105-38417&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1002&akid=38417%2E1203867%2EQkukeb ]Let’s celebrate these historic victories and prepare for the fights
ahead: if you can spare, pitch in $5 or more to help us
keep up the pressure on the Party to deliver →

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20261105.wVGq-8&refcode=em20261105-38417&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1021&akid=38417%2E1203867%2EQkukeb ]Contribute $5

There is so much more work to do, and we can’t wait to see what our new
Justice Democrats accomplish in Congress next year. This victorious cycle
was all thanks to grassroots donors like you,
Peter.

In solidarity,

Justice Democrats

Contribute to Justice Democrats: https://secure.actblue.com/donate/justicedemocrats?refcode=em20261105-38417-footer&t=1022&refcode2=38417_1203867_Qkukeb&akid=38417%2E1203867%2EQkukeb

This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Email is the most important way for us to reach you about opportunities to get involved. name: API PA
subject: We made history. Thank you.
body:
This moment is exactly why API PA exists.
| |
---
| Dear Peter, Yesterday I was in Dauphin County, surrounded by API PA’s team and our partners CASA in Action and One Pennsylvania with one message: Time’s up. Time’s up on the wealthy getting wealthier while people struggle to keep a roof over their heads. Time’s up on billions of dollars for wars and ICE prisons and no money for schools and healthcare. Time’s up on tax breaks for gambling, data centers, and crypto scams while manufacturing, agriculture, and public service jobs disappear. Across Pennsylvania and across the Commonwealth, our elections weren’t just about the candidates. They were about us. How we pay the rent. How we take care of our children. How we work, how we love, and how we live as a community. API PA voters delivered. Our field teams knocked 100,000 doors, made over 3 million calls, and had over 50,000 conversations with AAPI voters. In Congressional District 10, API PA worked with community partners to organize Nepali-Bhutanese refugees who were targets of ICE deportations and Scott Perry’s anti-immigrant vitriol. Nothing made me prouder than witnessing two amazing refugee women leaders head up API PA’s civic engagement, organizing, and field efforts that threw out Scott Perry and ushered in new leadership.
* In Pennsylvania’s 1st Congressional District, we helped elect Bob Harvie and flip a critical congressional seat, knocking on nearly 26,000 doors in Bensalem alone.
* In Pennsylvania Senate District 6, we were proud to support Eileen Abillar and help flip one of four state senate seats that delivered a Democratic trifecta in Harrisburg for the first time in decades.
* Our year-round phone banking team also helped deliver AAPI voters to power victories in North Carolina, Texas, and Arizona.

On Election Day, we showed what can happen when we organize, engage, and mobilize for each other. We don't just win elections — we fundamentally shift the balance of power. API PA exists to turn grassroots energy into lasting political power for Asian American and diverse immigrant communities across this Commonwealth so that our voices can never be ignored. **I am writing to you today to say thank you. Thank you to every single volunteer, member, donor, and supporter who made this possible. You built a movement. You made history.** **[If this work matters to you, keep supporting API PA by donating here or joining us as a member!](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/4LUf8Ftk1Sr9yLuKqj1tQRKZRz7CjltH/click?signature=cdec22d07f80cc7ea4d6f3264b43193ba4e366ee&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.apipennsylvania.org%2Fmembership)** Our work is just beginning. It’s one thing to win an election. It’s another thing to prove that an election will actually make a difference in our people’s lives. Alongside a growing and diverse coalition, API PA is gearing up to make sure our legislature and our elected officials fight for the people who put them there. Stay tuned. Stay active. Stay hopeful. In solidarity, Helen Gym Interim Executive Director, API PA
---
|

The election, or, if you're a Republican, the total and complete beating, is now two days behind us. In Mississippi, the GOP is still counting absentee ballots and hoping for a "win" in the Senate race between Cindy Hyde-Smith and Scott Colom. A final result could be days away. But even if the GOP pulls it out by a handful of votes we need to ask: what does this beatdown tell us?
There's a lot to learn. CNN and its socialist friends will tell you it means Americans have embraced their agenda and are ready to follow Venezuela, China, Cuba, and a long list of other failed countries down their preferred socialist path. Some will tell you it's your fault because you didn't vote, you anti-American fool. At least, that's what they think of you. Others will say it's because we didn't support Israel vigorously enough. Never mind that we've sent billions upon billions of dollars already. And if you object, they'll call you an anti-Semite. How dare you not want to put your kids in debt for Netanyahu and his band of warmongers? For the record, I don't believe for one second that God expects you or me to risk our nation's future to support a secular government run by fallible men. Even if you believe God's promise to the nation of Israel has not yet been fulfilled, nothing in God's word says I must let a man lead my nation into economic destruction.
So what happened? Start with the Republican Party itself. Can you tell me what exactly the GOP stands for today? In Mississippi, most of our local officials put an R behind their names. But have you ever asked one of them to explain the Republican Party platform? Most of them couldn't tell you there is a platform, and the ones who know about it don't care. That makes our local "Republican" officials completely useless at governing by the standards of the party, standards that most of the citizens in their towns actually believe in.
Next, consider your state representative and senator. They also call themselves Republicans, but do they actually care about conservative policy? Mine certainly don't. They treat their office as an excuse to spend a few months a year away from their families having fun in the big city of Jackson. When they're "in session," you and conservative policy are the last things on their minds.
Mississippi has a reputation as a conservative state. Is it, really? Supposedly we have great gun laws. Here's a test. Last year, President Trump and Congress zeroed out the $200 federal tax on firearm suppressors, and this fall the ATF announced it would stop enforcing the federal registration requirement. Great news for gun owners, right? Not so fast. Mississippi law says you can only own a suppressor if you're "authorized under federal law." In other words, your gun rights in "conservative" Mississippi depend on whoever happens to be running the ATF in Washington. Our own Attorney General has warned that a future administration could reverse the change and has asked the Legislature to cut the federal reference out of our law. Bills to fix it have been filed before, and our "conservative" Legislature never got it done. That isn't conservative leadership. It's a bunch of politicians who like the conservative label but always take the easy way out. Following is not leading.
And if you want to bring up the abortion law that went to the Supreme Court and overturned Roe v. Wade, let me tell you what I saw with my own eyes. I watched Republicans in the House Republican Caucus beg the Speaker to kill that bill because they didn't want to deal with the fallout of voting on another pro-life measure. Our Legislature is full of, and run by, some of the weakest, most mind-numbingly spineless people you'll ever meet. They care only about getting back to Jackson every year so they can pretend to be important.
Then there's our "representation" in Washington. Unless you're deeply involved in the Republican Party, I don't know a single citizen who thinks Roger Wicker or Cindy Hyde-Smith are great examples of conservatives fighting for the people of Mississippi. Local and state politicians love them because they bring home cash, which is really just your money cycled through the federal government, so those politicians can grow government while still pretending to be conservative. Beyond that, nobody believes our senators or our field of wet-noodle congressmen fight for anything other than themselves and big government.
Then there's President Trump. Most of us enthusiastically voted for him and had high hopes that he would be the leader this nation needs. And honestly, the first year of his hard-fought second term was fantastic. He hit D.C. like a man with a plan. He promised to fix the border, fix the economy, end the war between Russia and Ukraine, and stop the cycle of war after war after war.
Ukraine proved harder than he expected, and most of us didn't blame him for that. We still trusted that, with his help, the war would end sooner rather than later, and that at the very least we would stop spending ourselves into bankruptcy supporting it. He fixed the border in short order. That's one issue, maybe the only one, we can all call a huge success. He brought Elon Musk to D.C. to start wringing out waste and fraud. But Trump found out what the rest of us already knew: nobody else in Washington, especially the Republicans in the House and Senate, cared one bit about eliminating waste, fraud, and abuse. In fact, most of us are convinced they support all of it. Not a single one of our "conservative" representatives in D.C. lifted a finger to help Trump or Musk save this country from the economic disaster ahead.
And let's not forget Trump made two more promises: no war with Iran, and the release of the Epstein files, so that the pedophile and human-trafficking ring of government officials and big-business leaders would finally be exposed and prosecuted. What do we have instead? An endless war with Iran, and a Justice Department, Congress, and executive branch that have decided to protect the pedophiles at the expense of their victims and the American people. Thomas Massie led the fight to release the Epstein files while nearly every Republican in Congress stood on the sidelines. For his trouble, Trump and the GOP turned on him.
So, you want to know why Republicans lost Tuesday? It's simple. No one believes they make any difference at all. They don't believe in anything. They aren't conservative. They have zero interest in anything but serving themselves, growing government, and continuing the waste, fraud, and abuse.
Where do we go from here? As a nation, the honest answer is down. We are headed toward Cuba and Venezuela. If you're waiting on the GOP to slow that down, you'll still be waiting when you're standing in the bread line.
The only answer is for you to change the direction. Start with your mayor, your county supervisor, your state representative and senator, your governor and lieutenant governor, because D.C. is all but lost. Outside of Rand Paul, Thomas Massie, and a handful of fighters in the House Freedom Caucus, all that's left there are useless Republicans and socialist Democrats, and a few good men can't hold back the tide by themselves. So hunker down, fix your community and your state, and ride out the storm. A storm is coming. Trump and the GOP opened the floodgates, and a wave of socialist Democrats is about to pour through.
Hold on. This ain't going to be fun.

Kirk just wrapped up this year's "See You at the Library Day," where we countered the Left and brought conservative values straight to America's children.Kirk is busy spearheading the "Bible Revival" movement that gets Biblical values -- that America was founded upon -- back into schools. And Kirk just finished filming Season 3 of our television show "Iggy and Mr. Kirk" that teaches children how to respond to the deceitful culture with Biblical values and steadfast faith.**I'm writing you with such urgency because Season 3 of "Iggy and Mr. Kirk" is in jeopardy.** **[And if I can't raise $48,523 in the next four weeks, "Iggy and Mr. Kirk" will be delayed -- or even postponed indefinitely.](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckctu2zAQRb-G2tHgQy8utHAgK1BRp0UMpEtiTI4UxqIokJSL_n3hoPmBbg9mLnDu_XXWZ3CLW-cX8Ni5lHRM-ubizYDHGFZIN7Qec0i42j9aMFFTzimrNJjs7qhLKGxXCd5ObYEdb5RsVcMFL947YzlUraknVbaNUjUiQsuAGabMdL3KwnWPPM5Zxeuy4upQTlWDyJSFqRaCc1KyfbOQ8eDW5CwmE8K2hcVlZ9IhxLlYuvect0TkkYiBiCGh2SMeYEUb8sEET8RwjXBHOoVI5xAsEcMGlalaSdE0jJaST1S1H_6jFEQOe_Y6hT0aJLJ_Pb0RUT-QR-t2T2R_Oh_H7_-gAb-Bm1ci-08RJpR-6p_10_D8Q7-e3vTnsR7Hl2_055GOl8vXY1gzrpnIfrxc6FcJRezs9tsti0t1Q0o2e3DLw6HI_7nMvRN_AwAA__9Au5qL)** The radical Leftists who attack us because we're reaching America's children with God's Truth would love nothing more than to see "Iggy and Mr. Kirk" shut down.They hate that "Iggy and Mr. Kirk" has skyrocketed to the top of Angel Studios' streaming service. They hate that we've created a path around the addictive mind rot they put on TV.It's like Kirk always says... It's not enough to complain about culture raising our children. We must create something better for them. The first 2 seasons of "Iggy and Mr. Kirk" have reached millions of children and counting, but Season 3 is in jeopardy.If "Iggy and Mr. Kirk" isn't funded, there will be no voice on TV countering the Left's dangerous lies.Lies like Drag Queens leading a Pride Parade SingAlong on Blue's Clues...Same-sex weddings on Arthur... And Sesame Street using YOUR tax dollars to normalize same-sex parents and men in dresses.And that's just what's on TV. Not to mention the thousands of 'Queer Kid' videos on platforms like YouTube Kids.The days of The Andy Griffith Show and Father Knows Best are gone. The Left has purposely used TV to create a generation of zombie children who are glued to their screens."Iggy and Mr. Kirk" is the antidote to that Leftist TV brainwashing.It uses low-stimulation production and teaches children how to respond to the deceitful culture with Biblical values and steadfast faith. Like when Mr. Kirk teaches Iggy:

* to love how God created him as an iguana, even when the villainous Culture the Vulture says Iggy must become a human to fit in.
* to rely on the wisdom of parents -- one mom and one dad -- to solve life's problems.
* to be BRAVE by speaking truth in the face of the Left's lies.

# Iran
* **Vance blames Republican election losses on Iran war; Iran 's Ghalibaf accuses U.S. of putting Israel first: **The Iran war was the main reason Republicans lost the 2026 midterm elections, U.S. Vice President JD Vance [wrote](https://substack.com/redirect/2f3a7211-6ba0-46a4-8868-21f05acab7f0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Thursday, arguing that voters who backed President Donald Trump in 2024 switched to supporting Democrats despite strong Republican turnout.
* Citing private polling that he said accurately anticipated the results, Vance identified four leading reasons former Trump voters abandoned Republicans: "End the war," "Focus on cost of living/inflation," "Put America First," and "Change our relationship to Israel."
* He said the findings vindicated calls for a diplomatic resolution to the conflict, and he warned against attributing the losses to the Trump administration's far-right immigration policies. "The reason we lost is the war. The president himself said so last night," Vance wrote. "If you'd like to argue it was worth it, that losing the Senate for the next 6 years was worth it, then do so."
* Responding to Vance, Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf [accused](https://substack.com/redirect/7ca8e4f3-c75b-474e-8bd0-0a9b1f664717?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the Trump administration of preparing another phase of the conflict while prioritizing Israel over American interests. "Boss is prepping the next war phase while America teeters on an Israel-First cliff," Ghalibaf wrote, adding: "Why not say this to your boss?"
* **Iran 's Khamenei says U.S. midterm results will not change Washington's hostility toward Tehran: **Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei said on Wednesday that anyone expecting a change in U.S. policy following Republican losses in the midterm elections is "seriously mistaken."
* "Those who still harbor even the slightest hope that the behavior of the hegemonic system might change through partisan or factional shifts . . . are seriously mistaken," Khamenei said in a written statement published on his website.
* **Iran says two tankers, tugboat catch fire in Strait of Hormuz; UK reports tanker attacked near Qatar:** Two oil tankers [caught fire](https://substack.com/redirect/bbecabf7-a17d-4ce1-832f-a6e8a608b359?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in separate incidents in the Strait of Hormuz after attempting to use "unauthorized" shipping routes, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy said on Thursday. A tugboat attempting to extinguish the fire also caught fire.
* A tanker was struck by two unidentified projectiles approximately 50 nautical miles north of Madinat Al-Shamal, Qatar, the UK Maritime Trade Operations reported on Thursday. The condition of the crew and the extent of damage remain unconfirmed.
* **South Korea plans to expand naval mission near Strait of Hormuz:** South Korea [plans](https://substack.com/redirect/600f4625-49a7-4a56-9741-c2f57045bbf7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to expand its anti-piracy naval mission in the Gulf of Aden toward waters south of Oman, near the Strait of Hormuz, and deploy additional military assets, Yonhap reported on Thursday.
* It would be Seoul's first military contribution to maritime security efforts in the region since the U.S.-Iran war began in February. In September, South Korea declined U.S. requests for direct military support against Tehran.
* South Korean defense officials stressed that the mission would not involve combat forces and would remain independent of allied military operations. They said that aircraft will be prohibited from monitoring Iranian territory or entering the Strait of Hormuz.
* **U.S. sanctions Indian, Turkish firms over alleged ties to Iranian oil, aviation:** On Wednesday, the U.S. Treasury Department [imposed](https://substack.com/redirect/41642233-fb49-428c-9830-849f4dee9243?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) sanctions on individuals and companies in India and Turkey over their alleged support for Iran's oil and aviation sectors, as part of the Trump administration's Operation Economic Outcast campaign to restrict Iranian oil revenues during the war.
* The Treasury Department accused Indian entities of falsifying vessel registrations for ships transporting Iranian oil. It also sanctioned Turkey-based Fugo Ground Services Inc. for supporting Iran's aviation sector.

Iwasawa said that the court will deliver its judgment in The Gambia's genocide case against Myanmar on November 19.

A threat targeting flights to Rome was sent via email from a group describing itself as "anti-feminist," the AP [reported](https://substack.com/redirect/f22c583b-d793-42ce-89c2-9c067cfbad07?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), saying that at least one other airport received a similar message. The disruptions follow a series of other bomb threats in Europe earlier this week.

Thursday, November 5, 2026 -** Iran: Vice President JD Vance blames Republican election losses on Iran war; Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf accuses U.S. of putting Israel first. Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei says U.S. midterm results will not change Washington's hostility toward Tehran. Iran says two tankers, tugboat catch fire in Strait of Hormuz; UK reports tanker attacked near Qatar. South Korea plans to expand naval mission near Strait of Hormuz. U.S. sanctions Indian, Turkish firms over alleged ties to Iranian oil, aviation. UAE airline profits plunge 66% amid Iran war. Palestine: Israeli attacks kill three Palestinians, including child, in Gaza. Israeli settlers seize homes near Jericho, expelling Palestinians; settlers say they are "dismantling the Oslo Accords." Israel demolishes five buildings, displacing 105 Palestinians, and shuts down club in occupied East Jerusalem. Israeli settlers burn olive trees, assault Palestinians as soldiers demolish homes across the West Bank. Yemen: Saudi-led strikes kill around 20 across Yemen; Ansarallah shelling kills woman, wounds five in Taiz. WSJ: Ansarallah demands recognition of sovereignty over Yemen, $51 billion in compensation in exchange for halting attacks on Saudi Arabia. Lebanon: Israeli strike kills one in southern Lebanon, again violating ceasefire. Lebanon issues arrest warrants for two Hezbollah members over seized explosives. U.S.: Democrats extend power in House, state races in latest midterm election results. Exclusive: Civil-society groups propose delaying fight over Iran war until 2027. CBS: Trump asks advisers if he should remove War Secretary Pete Hegseth. NYT: SCOTUS justice Samuel Alito privately says he won't retire immediately, despite Democrats' Senate win. House Speaker Mike Johnson will not seek leadership role. Billionaire Leon Black sues Rep. Robert Garcia for defamation over remarks about Epstein ties. International: World Health Organization approves Ebola vaccine trials for dangerous Bundibugyo strain. Sudanese Army strike in North Kordofan kills two women, destroys water station. Ethiopia, Sudan close each other's consulates. Workers strike and march across France. Russian and Ukraine exchange attacks; Russia kills four civilians in Donetsk. Syria secures $400+ million Saudi loan in new defense agreement. Stabbing attack outside Sri Lanka embassy in Jordan kills security officer. Colombia expected to pass law toughening terms of surrender for armed group, breaking with "total peace" policy. UN elects five judges to International Court of Justice. Bomb threats disrupt European air travel. This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Iran Vance blames Republican election losses on Iran war; Iran 's Ghalibaf accuses U.S. of putting Israel first: The Iran war was the main reason Republicans lost the 2026 midterm elections, U.S. Vice President JD Vance on Thursday, arguing that voters who backed President Donald Trump in 2024 switched to supporting Democrats despite strong Republican turnout. Citing private polling that he said accurately anticipated the results, Vance identified four leading reasons former Trump voters abandoned Republicans: "End the war," "Focus on cost of living/inflation," "Put America First," and "Change our relationship to Israel." He said the findings vindicated calls for a diplomatic resolution to the conflict, and he warned against attributing the losses to the Trump administration's far-right immigration policies. "The reason we lost is the war. The president himself said so last night," Vance wrote. "If you'd like to argue it was worth it, that losing the Senate for the next 6 years was worth it, then do so." Responding to Vance, Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf the Trump administration of preparing another phase of the conflict while prioritizing Israel over American interests. "Boss is prepping the next war phase while America teeters on an Israel-First cliff," Ghalibaf wrote, adding: "Why not say this to your boss?" Iran 's Khamenei says U.S. midterm results will not change Washington's hostility toward Tehran: Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei said on Wednesday that anyone expecting a change in U.S. policy following Republican losses in the midterm elections is "seriously mistaken." "Those who still harbor even the slightest hope that the behavior of the hegemonic system might change through partisan or factional shifts . . . are seriously mistaken," Khamenei said in a written statement published on his website. Iran says two tankers, tugboat catch fire in Strait of Hormuz; UK reports tanker attacked near Qatar: Two oil tankers in separate incidents in the Strait of Hormuz after attempting to use "unauthorized" shipping routes, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Navy said on Thursday. A tugboat attempting to extinguish the fire also caught fire. A tanker was struck by two unidentified projectiles approximately 50 nautical miles north of Madinat Al-Shamal, Qatar, the UK Maritime Trade Operations reported on Thursday. The condition of the crew and the extent of damage remain unconfirmed. South Korea plans to expand naval mission near Strait of Hormuz: South Korea to expand its anti-piracy naval mission in the Gulf of Aden toward waters south of Oman, near the Strait of Hormuz, and deploy additional military assets, Yonhap reported on Thursday. It would be Seoul's first military contribution to maritime security efforts in the region since the U.S.-Iran war began in February. In September, South Korea declined U.S. requests for direct military support against Tehran. South Korean defense officials stressed that the mission would not involve combat forces and would remain independent of allied military operations. They said that aircraft will be prohibited from monitoring Iranian territory or entering the Strait of Hormuz. U.S. sanctions Indian, Turkish firms over alleged ties to Iranian oil, aviation: On Wednesday, the U.S. Treasury Department sanctions on individuals and companies in India and Turkey over their alleged support for Iran's oil and aviation sectors, as part of the Trump administration's Operation Economic Outcast campaign to restrict Iranian oil revenues during the war. The Treasury Department accused Indian entities of falsifying vessel registrations for ships transporting Iranian oil. It also sanctioned Turkey-based Fugo Ground Services Inc. for supporting Iran's aviation sector. The Treasury Department said last week that its sanctions campaign had contributed to the collapse of Iran's currency and increased inflation almost 90%. UAE airline profits plunge 66% amid Iran war: The Dubai-based Emirates Group airline sustained a 66% decline in its after-tax profits, it on Thursday. Year-on-year, the airline's profit fell to $1 billion in the first half of its 2026-27 financial year, as the Iran war disrupted air travel and pushed up fuel costs. The Emirates airline carried 21.8 million passengers between April and September, down 22% from a year earlier. The company said that it remained profitable despite the disruptions, with cash reserves declining to $14.7 billion by the end of September. Palestine Israeli attacks kill three Palestinians, including child, in Gaza: Israeli forces a woman in Al-Mawasi, west of Khan Younis in southern Gaza, and a child in the Bureij refugee camp in central Gaza on Thursday, WAFA reported. Another Palestinian was killed in an Israeli airstrike west of Al-Zawayda in central Gaza. Israeli settlers seize homes near Jericho, expelling Palestinians; settlers say they are "dismantling the Oslo Accords": Around 30 Israeli settlers, some of whom were armed, eight homes in Ein Al-Duyuk Al-Tahta on the outskirts of Jericho in the occupied West Bank on Wednesday. Activists warned that settlers could be reproducing the situation in Hebron, where armed Israeli settlers live in enclaves inside the Palestinian city, contributing to displacement and severe restrictions on Palestinian freedom of mobility. The operation near Jericho was organized by the Nachala settlement movement, which claims to have secretly purchased the properties. Sixty-five Palestinian residents fled after settlers attacked them with stones, an activist the Times of Israel. Residents said that Israeli forces subsequently blocked access to the area, leaving homeowners afraid to return. The new outpost is reportedly located in Area C, under full Israeli control under the Oslo Accords, just meters from parts of Jericho classified as Area A, where the Palestinian Authority is supposed to exercise civilian and security control. Yisrael Gantz, head of the West Bank settler council, framed the move as an effort to dismantle the Oslo Accords, declaring: "Today we begin reversing the trend, dismantling the Oslo Accords through actions, house by house, family by family." Palestinian National Council Speaker Rawhi Fattouh condemned the takeover as "organized terrorism" carried out under Israeli government protection, charging Israel of encouraging settlement expansion and forced displacement. Israel demolishes five buildings, displacing 105 Palestinians, and shuts down club in occupied East Jerusalem: Israeli forces five residential buildings containing 12 apartments in the town of Biddu, northwest of occupied East Jerusalem, on Thursday, displacing 105 Palestinians without prior warning, citing construction without permits. Soldiers fired stun grenades and tear gas at residents and prevented families from removing their belongings before demolishing their homes, according to the Jerusalem Governorate. Separately, Israeli authorities shut down the Abna Al-Quds Club in Jerusalem's Old City under an order issued by National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir. The governorate condemned both measures as part of an escalating Israeli campaign targeting Palestinian homes, institutions, and community life in Jerusalem. Israeli settlers burn olive trees, assault Palestinians as soldiers demolish homes across the West Bank: Ramallah: Israeli settlers to dozens of centuries-old olive trees in the village of Burqa, east of Ramallah, on Thursday, according to WAFA. Jericho: Three Palestinians were after settlers, accompanied by Israeli forces, raided Palestinian homes in the Bedouin communities of Ard Satih, west of Jericho, beating residents and spraying them with pepper spray. Nablus: Settlers farmers in Beita, south of Nablus, injuring one Palestinian. Israeli forces also demolished a home in Furush Beit Dajan, east of Nablus. Salfit: Israeli forces a home in Qarawat Bani Hassan and issued a stop-work order for another home. Three Palestinians were also injured in assaults by Israeli soldiers and settlers in the town. Yemen Saudi-led strikes kill around 20 across Yemen; Ansarallah shelling kills woman, wounds five in Taiz: Saudi-led coalition bombardment killed around 20 people across the Yemeni governorates of Al-Jawf, Al-Bayda, Saada, and Taiz over the past 24 hours, according to Ansarallah-affiliated media. Ansarallah military spokesman Yahya Saree said that the coalition carried out 104 attacks across areas controlled by the group, including the capital, Sana'a. Meanwhile, Yemen's Saudi-backed government reported that Ansarallah shelling in Taiz killed a woman and wounded five people. WSJ: Ansarallah demands recognition of sovereignty over Yemen, $51 billion in compensation in exchange for halting attacks on Saudi Arabia: Yemen's Ansarallah $51 billion in compensation for years of Saudi airstrikes and blockade and formal recognition as Yemen's sovereign power in exchange for halting attacks on Saudi Arabia, the Wall Street Journal reported. Riyadh reportedly approached the group after Ansarallah attacks on Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea and territorial advances near the strategic Bab al-Mandab Strait. Saudi officials told the WSJ that Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman is reluctant to negotiate without military leverage but fears that deploying additional ground troops could result in heavy casualties. The UAE's withdrawal from the anti-Ansarallah campaign, Washington's refusal to provide direct military support, and Saudi's reliance on regional allies further complicated Riyadh's options, the report said. Lebanon Israeli strike kills one in southern Lebanon, again violating ceasefire: An Israeli drone strike killed one person and wounded another in Qabrikha, in the Marjeyoun district of southern Lebanon, on Wednesday, Lebanon's National News Agency reported. The Israeli military that it targeted two people who were "observing" its forces in the area, without providing any evidence that the individuals were military targets. Separately, Israeli warplanes two airstrikes on Tallousa and its outskirts in the Marjeyoun district, and struck the outskirts of Aita al-Jabal in the Bint Jbeil district. Lebanon issues arrest warrants for two Hezbollah members over seized explosives: Lebanon's Military Court issued arrest warrants for two Hezbollah members in connection with the seizure of 780 kilograms (1,720 pounds) of explosives at the Dahr Al-Baydar checkpoint linking Beirut to the Bekaa Valley, the National News Agency reported. The explosives were seized last month. Lebanese authorities indicted 13 people in the case, on charges involving state security, illegal possession of weapons and explosives, and forming unlawful organizations. Beyond the two Hezbollah members, the remaining 11 defendants are still at large. The government's attempt to question six defendants was postponed following an objection filed by their lawyer. U.S. News Democrats extend power in House, state races in latest midterm election results: Additional races were called on Wednesday, extending Democrats' commanding lead in the House of Representatives and in state-level posts. Senate elections in Mississippi and Alaska remain uncalled as of Thursday morning, while an unexpectedly tight Senate race in Louisiana was called in favor of the Republican, Julia Letlow. Sam Forstag, a labor union leader and smokejumper endorsed by Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez , won his election to represent Montana's first congressional district, a seat previously held by Trump's former Interior Secretary, Ryan Zinke. Forstag is the first Democratic candidate to win a congressional race in the state since former Sen. Jon Tester won in 2018. He is also the youngest congressional representative from the state since the 1930s. Progressive activist William Lawrence officially Republican incumbent Tom Barrett in Michigan's seventh congressional district. Lawrence, a co-founder of the Sunrise Movement, won one of the most competitive elections this cycle by emphasizing the rising cost of living in Michigan, opposing data centers, calling for restrictions on Flock cameras, and pushing for tighter regulation of artificial intelligence. Republican incumbent Rep. Max Miller , who was accused of physical and verbal abuse by his ex-wife, conceded defeat to Democrat Brian Poindexter in Ohio's seventh congressional district, which covers much of the Cleveland suburbs. Progressive Angela Gonzales-Torres defeated incumbent Democrat Rep. Jimmy Gomez in California's 34th congressional district. The 31-year-old was backed by Justice Democrats and the Los Angeles chapter of the Democratic Socialists of America in her May primary against the AIPAC-backed Gomez. Two other races featuring progressives in California have yet to be called. Mai Vang , a progressive from the Sacramento area, trails incumbent Doris Matsui by 15 points with less than half of the vote counted. Aisha Wahab , a progressive who won a special election to fill the northern California seat vacated by Eric Swalwell , leads her opponent, Melissa Hernandez, by 13 points, with just over half of the votes counted. Nithya Raman , whose Los Angeles City Council campaigns were boosted by the local D.S.A. chapter, incumbent Mayor Karen Bass in a contentious race. Los Angeles's D.S.A. chapter endorsed her candidacy for mayor, despite Raman's acceptance of an endorsement from a pro-Israel group and lack of clarity on whether she supports the Boycott, Divestment, Sanctions movement. Raman maintains that she was an early advocate for a ceasefire in Gaza, and has characterized Israel's conduct in Gaza as a genocide. The national D.S.A. narrowly voted against rescinding the Los Angeles chapter's endorsement. Civil-society groups propose delaying fight over Iran war until 2027: A draft letter circulating among civil-society organizations, a copy of which was obtained by Drop Site Daily, initially proposed punting on the critical fight over war funding until 2027. After Drop Site approached the groups who had signed, the letter was adjusted to be more forceful. The background: Funding for the government expires on December 11, 2026. Rep. Ro Khanna have proposed using that date as leverage to force an end to the war, not through a war powers resolution--which Trump has already ignored--but by legally barring the government from spending money on the war. Instead, the groups signing the letter proposed focusing on measures that have no bearing on the administration's ability to prosecute the war. The letter read: "In Tuesday's elections, people across the United States made their will resoundingly clear: they want to end President Trump's war on Iran, its resulting violence, and its downstream economic hardship, immediately. Ending this war cannot wait." "We, the XX undersigned civil society organizations, urge you to respond to this mandate by voting down any defense authorization or defense appropriations bills that would continue funding this disastrous war or increase Pentagon funding beyond the already outrageous $1 trillion that the White House pushed through Congress last year" (emphasis added). But: Congress has no plans to fund the war through a defense appropriations bill. The plan is to pass a continuing resolution on or before December 11. So far, signatories to the draft letter include the Center for International Policy Advocacy, Indivisible, J Street, MoveOn, National Iranian American Council Action, and Win Without War. The letter went on: "If Trump continues the war into the new year, we further urge returning members to prioritize and pass legislation expressly defunding this war early in the new Congress. " Such an approach would let Trump have November and December to wage war before " expressly defunding this war early in the new Congress." That line is being stripped out, sources said. Matt Duss , executive director of CIPA, one of the signatories, emphasized his support for the more aggressive approach proposed by Van Hollen. "Congress needs to use every tool it has right now to stop this war," he said. "We want everyone to be going all the way." At issue is the question of just how hard Democrats should fight Trump's war. Not every group involved, sources said, was yet convinced to take the approach called for by Duss and Van Hollen, despite the resounding mandate. CBS: Trump asks advisers if he should remove War Secretary Pete Hegseth: Trump is his advisers if he should remove War Secretary Pete Hegseth from his post, CBS News reported on Wednesday, suggesting that the president is searching for a scapegoat after the Republican Party suffered historic election losses driven by voter anger over the Iran war. Some aides predict that blame will fall on U.S. military Commander Adm. Brad Cooper , the head of Central Command, and the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, Gen. Dan Caine. Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis is being floated as a replacement for Hegseth. If Hegseth is replaced, he may try to take up the Tennessee Senate seat that Marsha Blackburn is vacating to become governor. Trump has told reporters that Hegseth would be "very popular" as a senator. NYT: SCOTUS justice Samuel Alito privately says he won 't retire immediately, despite Democrats' Senate win: The Supreme Court Justice Samuel Alito privately says he intends to remain on the bench after Democrats swept the Senate, two people close to Alito the New York Times. His announcement follows speculation that he or Justice Clarence Thomas might retire during the lame-duck session. Some experts speculate that outgoing Republican senators--such as John Cornyn, Bill Cassidy, or Susan Collins--might try to help Trump push a new SCOTUS nominee through the confirmation process. House Speaker Mike Johnson will not seek leadership role: Following the Democratic takeover of the House of Representatives, SpeakerMike Johnson told staff on Wednesday he will not the minority leader post in the new Congress. After the news broke, House Majority Leader Steve Scalise a "consensus-driven" bid for the Minority Leader position, saying that the election "was far worse than any of us expected." He will Judiciary Chairman Jim Jordan , who also announced a bid to become House Minority Leader on Wednesday, touting his "battle-testing" in oversight hearings and his readiness to counter Democratic investigations. Republicans will vote for new leadership on November 10. Rep. Tom Emmer(R-Minn.), the current Majority Whip and the presumptive Minority Whip, a challenge from Rep. August Pfluger(R-Texas), ABC News reported on Wednesday. Emmer told colleagues in a letter that he took Tuesday's failures "personally" and could not "sugarcoat" Republican defeats. Pfluger, for his part, promoted his ability to make "the changes" the caucus would need to win in 2028. Billionaire Leon Black sues Rep. Robert Garcia for defamation over remarks about Epstein ties: Private equity magnate Leon Black a lawsuit in New York federal court on Wednesday, claiming that California congressman Robert Garcia defamed him for saying that Black was among the last people to interact with Jeffrey Epstein before his death, and that victims credibly named Black as involved in abuse. Black acknowledges knowing Epstein and paying him $158 million for tax and estate planning, but he denies knowledge of Epstein's crimes and says that he cut ties with Epstein in 2018. Black said that Garcia's statements cost him investment opportunities and $775,000 in private security, and accuses Garcia of seeking political benefit from public anger over Epstein. In September, the House of Representatives held Black in contempt for ignoring subpoenas from the Oversight Committee about possible nondisclosure agreements with women tied to Epstein. Black has sued the committee, arguing that the subpoenas were invalid. Garcia has vowed to pursue the Epstein investigation. He is expected to head the House Oversight Committee in the new Congress. 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com Other International News WHO approves Ebola vaccine trials for dangerous Bundibugyo strain: On Monday, the World Health Organization two trials for Ebola vaccines that target the Bundibugyo strain. The strain has killed more than 5,300 people since May, with a fatality rate of about 50%. Currently, there is no strain-specific vaccine or treatment available. The new vaccines are being jointly developed by the University of Oxford, the Serum Institute of India, and Moderna, WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said. They will be tested in a trial led by the Democratic Republic of the Congo's National Institute for Biomedical Research. Trial results are expected by early 2027. Sudanese Army strike in North Kordofan kills two women, destroys water station: The Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) a neighborhood in the Um Badr area of North Kordofan, killing two women and injuring 10 other people, the Sudan Tribune reported. The same wave of airstrikes hit the Al-Kabjark water station at Khor Dardaq, destroying tanks, pumps, and solar panels at a vital water facility for residents. Ethiopia, Sudan close each other 's consulates: On Wednesday, Ethiopia the Sudanese consulate in Assosa and ordered Sudanese diplomats to leave, Reuters reported. Sudan then closed the Ethiopian consulate in Gedaref and expelled Ethiopian diplomats. Sudan accuses Ethiopia of supporting the Rapid Support Forces and allowing the RSF to launch drone strikes from Ethiopian territory. Ethiopia accuses Sudan of backing the Tigrayan rebels who launched an offensive against Ethiopian forces in September. Workers strike and march across France: Labor unions in France a strike on Thursday to demand a higher minimum wage, higher salaries for all workers, tax reforms, and better school conditions. Protests are planned in 260 cities and towns, and the Education Ministry expects 16% of the country's public-school teachers to strike. President Emmanuel Macron convened a meeting with his defense and security advisers on Wednesday to "ensure public order." Security forces have already begun brutalizing protesters: In Lyon, riot police fired tear gas at a demonstration, Reuters reported. Russian and Ukraine exchange attacks; Russia kills four civilians in Donetsk: Russian attacks killed four civilians and injured five others in Donetsk on Wednesday, Al Jazeera , and drones caused large fires at a logistics center in Bucha outside Kyiv district. Russian forces also attacked a postal terminal near Kharkiv, a power substation in Dnipropetrovsk, and a dry cargo ship carrying military equipment near Odesa, its Defense Ministry said on Thursday. More than 80 Russian drones hit Odesa, injuring six people, including a child, according to Ukrainian officials. Ukraine launched over 200 drone attacks on Russia's Ryazan region overnight, Russian officials said. The strikes injured one person, caused fires at sites including an oil refinery, and left areas without power. Syria secures $400+ million Saudi loan in new defense agreement: On Wednesday, the defense ministries of Saudi Arabia and Syria a new agreement that will give Syria more than $403 million in Saudi loans for energy, housing, and infrastructure projects. The terms of the agreement have not been disclosed. The Saudi Fund for Development agreed to six concessional loans: $100 million for healthcare facilities; $60 million for housing; $105 million for civil defense; $90 million for the Aleppo thermal power plant; and $30 million for drinking water in Damascus and Idlib. The deal comes just days after the Syrian foreign minister, Asaad al-Shaibani, said that Syria may join the Saudi-Turkey-Pakistan "Mecca alliance." Stabbing attack outside Sri Lanka embassy in Jordan kills security officer: An assailant stabbed and an officer outside the Sri Lankan embassy in Amman on Thursday. The attacker reportedly tried to seize a guard's weapon before he was subdued. He sustained injuries and is in critical condition. The attack injured a second officer, who is being hospitalized. In its preliminary investigation, Jordan's Public Security Directorate said that the attacker had planned "to commit the terrorist act against the officers of the General Security Directorate." The attacker was previously convicted of joining "terrorist groups," according to court filings, and of conspiring to carry out attacks in Jordan. Colombia expected to pass law toughening terms of surrender for armed group, breaking with "total peace" policy: Colombia's Congress a bill that increases the scope of punishments for militants who lay down their arms. The legislation bars surrendering militants from holding elected office or entering peace negotiations. It would put conditions on the length of their prison sentences. In exchange for reducing their sentences by up to 50%, they must disarm, identify fellow militants, hand over recruited and kidnapped minors, help search for the missing, surrender their assets, and disclose their political and corruption networks. On election night, Donald Trump became what _every_ two-term president eventually becomes: a divided-government president. Democrats won the House and the Senate in the same night, and they did it with margins that should retire the phrase "a historic midterm correction" from every talking head's mouth in America.
Let's put the numbers on the actual historical ledger, because the comparison is the whole argument:
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/73df1355-00dd-4a44-9886-a1b9701e4a03?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
2026: Democrats netted roughly 27 to 31 House seats -- and that's after Republicans redrew Texas and Florida to hand themselves nine extra seats. The final House count is heading toward 250-plus Democratic seats, their largest majority since the early 2010s. In the Senate, Democrats flipped at least seven seats -- Iowa, Kansas, Maine, North Carolina, Ohio, South Carolina, and Texas, with Alaska and Mississippi still counting -- for a 54-47 majority, possibly 55-56\. That is _half the Obama 'shellacking'_. And five governorships flipped: Georgia, Iowa, Nevada, Ohio, and Texas. Democrats now hold _more governorships_ than at any moment since before 2010.
The honest historical analog, is not 1982. It's Obama 2006 -- a minus-30 House night that cost the Democrats both chambers. Except this one happened on a map Republicans personally gerrymandered to prevent exactly this outcome. They flipped a handful of majority-black Democratic seats in the South and still lost everything that mattered. The AP's voter polling gives the autopsy: inflation that got _worse_ , not better, the Iran war, immigration, and a corruption smell that wouldn't wash off.
Trump's own response -- "I can work with Dems on many more things than people understand" -- is pure Truman-after-1946. Fine. But here is what should frighten movement conservatives far more than a lost Capitol: **the states AKA heartland**.
**Two revolutions, same night**
Look at the personnel list, because it tells you where the energy actually is.
In the deep-blue cities, the left didn't just win -- it consolidated. Zohran Mamdani took New York City last year. This month, DSA member Nithya Raman ended Karen Bass's mayoralty in Los Angeles, becoming the first Asian American mayor in that city's history. In San Francisco, Scott Wiener crushed Nancy Pelosi's own endorsed candidate, 55 to 45, for the seat Pelosi held for four decades. New York sent a DSA-backed slate to the House -- Brad Lander, Claire Valdez, Darializa Avila Chevalier -- alongside AOC and presumptive next Speaker Jeffries. Kentucky elected its first socialist state legislator since the 1800s. There are now a record seven Muslim Americans in Congress, including the first Muslim US senator, and at least 36 winners nationwide at every level of government. In Michigan, Abdul El-Sayed carried Dearborn by 65 points on the _biggest turnout in that city 's recorded history_.
To be precise -- and precision matters if you want to win -- several of these wins are more complicated than the horror-show version. Wiener is a YIMBY progressive who beat the machine, not a DSA member. El-Sayed calls himself a capitalist. The socialist wave, as Brookings put it, showed "gains but limited reach": almost all of it inside safe blue seats. But that's actually the worse diagnosis, not the better one. You can beat an ideologue with a well-funded moderate. What you cannot beat is an organized, multi-cycle, city-level machine that treats school boards, state houses, and congressional seats as one continuous ladder. Funded from out of state. That machine now exists on the American left, it just ran its most successful election in history, and it has a farm system the right simply does not have.
**The states are the emergency**
Because here's the part of the night that got lost under CNN and MSNOWs 'the DC wreckage: **the same electorate that did this also flipped Texas**.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9f4ac0bc-597e-40d2-952c-dd1068ea0b43?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
2,848 of 3,109 counties moved toward Democrats
Gina Hinojosa unseated Greg Abbott. Talarico took the Senate seat. Democrats broke a Republican trifecta in the Texas House that had stood since 2003. Republicans kept the state Senate by a thread. And the mechanism wasn't mysterious -- the Texas Tribune's county data shows _border_ _counties_ that went R+16 and R+22 for Trump in 2024 swinging to D+56 and D+41 in 2026, on record Latino turnout and a massive expansion of the electorate, especially young voters. That is what an erosion looks like in real time. If it's turnout, it's fixable. If it's realignment, Texas 2028 is gone and the Electoral College is effectively gone with it. Nobody in Texas Republican politics currently knows which one it is -- and _the party has about 24 months to find out_.
Then there's the governance record, which is where "cleaned up" stops being a slogan and becomes a to-do list. Minnesota is the case study every state should be forced to read: 78 people charged, 57 convicted in the Feeding Our Future orbit, fourteen separate Medicaid-funded programs under federal and state investigation, federal child-care money frozen outright. And note the detail that blows up the comfortable version of the story: the Columbus, Ohio daycare allegations broke under a Republican governor. This is not a blue-state disease and not an immigration story -- it is a _program-oversight failure_ that happens wherever nobody audits the vendors. Every state in the union passes through federal money with 2010-era verification behind it. "Clean up the programs" is a governing agenda that polls in every swing state without a single culture-war word attached. This is why Marsha Blackburn's first presser after winning Tennessee Governor mentioned a DOGE for her state to begin during her transition period.
Republicans have two years of divided government in DC to pass nothing -- so the statehouse agenda is the only agenda.
And the two-year clock is real. The first tests of the post-2026 Republican Party arrive in 2027, in the off-year governor's races in Kentucky, Louisiana, and Mississippi -- Jeff Landry's own race in Baton Rouge becomes the opening referendum on whether the party can hold what it has, or whether the 2026 tide was the start of something. Then comes 2028, the last election cycle before the **2030 Census** redraws every map in the country. Will it be citizens only or like 2020 headcount? Lose the states through 2028 and the next decade is drawn for you.
**The verdict**
DC is already broken, Speaker Johnson and Leader Thune didn't help -- and 2026 made it worse than any midterm in modern memory for a Republican president, worse than 2010 in the Senate, worse than 2006 in consequence, on a map built to make it milder. Trump will spend 2027 vetoing things and calling it strategy. Fine.
But DC was always going to be lost in a sixth-year-type environment. The states are where the loss becomes _permanent_ or gets _reversed_ -- and the **heartland** is exactly where the other side just built its deepest bench, its strongest turnout machine, and its cleanest governing argument. Two years. Three governor's races in 2027. One census after that.
Clean up the states, or the states clean up the map -- and keep it.

* * *
Election night was amazing for so many reasons. Watching a new generation of Democratic leaders rise, Texas turning blue, and getting the chance to put one hand back on the wheel for sanity and decency in this country, was extraordinary.
But I'll be honest. There was something else I was enjoying, too: the total meltdown of MAGA influencers as they lose their grip on reality. They're being forced to accept that they're unpopular, and that they've spent the last two years destroying this country. A lot of them can't handle it.
Exhibit A, my old pal Laura Loomer. Conspiracy theorist, right-wing lunatic, deeply unwell human being. On Elon Musk's Twitter, she announced that America was over, that we're now an Islamic country, and basically threatened to leave.
That one has stuck with me, because I know what it feels like to lose.
When Democrats lost in 2024, when someone I have a great deal of respect for--Kamala Harris--lost, I didn't say America was over. I didn't threaten to leave. I didn't claim we'd been overrun by Nazis. I went back to work. I tried to figure out what I had done to contribute to this mess and what I could do differently over the next two years. Out of that came Endless Urgency and much of what I'm building right now to help rebuild the Democratic Party and fix this country.
Loomer isn't doing that. She's threatening to leave. Which, by the way, I'd support.
That's the message I sent her on Twitter, and I want to repeat it to all of you, because these people are disgustingly unpatriotic: You're free to leave.
The American people have spoken. Apparently they're the last institution in this country willing to stand up to Donald Trump and the Republican Party. MAGA doesn't like it. Fine. You can leave.
And that goes double for Laura Loomer, Tim Pool, Benny Johnson, and the rest of the MAGA influencer class, who are so very clearly taking money from foreign governments to pollute our politics and spread propaganda. Get the fuck out of our country. Go to whatever Middle Eastern nation has been paying your bills and go live there. Leave us the fuck alone.
And it isn't just the influencers. The craziness is everywhere.
I was on a right-wing show yesterday and suggested that Republicans lost because they've lost touch with reality. They spend too much time in their echo chambers and let crazy people run their campaigns, run for office, instead of qualified human beings who might actually know what the fuck they're doing.
* * *
#### **[Here's the difference between us and MAGA: when we lose, we organize. When they lose, they melt down. Endless Urgency exists because outrage alone isn't enough. We need to turn that energy into action, build our own media infrastructure, and fight for the future of this country every single day. Your paid subscription helps us expand our team, launch our content studio, and keep doing this work without answering to billionaires or corporate interests.](https://substack.com/redirect/d7510169-f4f8-4222-a754-7446e275dc13?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

* * *
A woman from Texas started screaming at me. James Talarico, she said, was going to steal my child and turn him trans. I hadn't even recovered from that when she explained the real reason Greg Abbott lost: he let too many Muslims into Texas.
That's where the Republican Party is right now. In 2025 there were a million think pieces about whether Democrats would learn the lesson of 2024: that we were too often focused on the wrong things instead of passing legislation and focusing on ways to make a material difference in your life. That's the lesson Republicans should be learning right now. Instead, they're doubling down on the same stupid shit. Loomer crashing out about America becoming Islamic and a woman screaming about Muslims in Texas aren't outliers. They are the party.
These people contribute nothing to society and nothing to public discourse except hate and lies. I hope someday they see the light and become more than the miserable human beings they are. I don't expect it.
Here's where the fun of election night ends. As much they'll threaten to leave, they're not going anywhere. There's a presidential election coming, and it will be a huge opportunity to make money and steal influence. JD Vance is already rebuilding the freak coalition for 2028. He won't fully condemn Nick Fuentes, who is basically a white supremacist, and he's back-channeling with Tucker Carlson to keep him out of the race.
They'll all make up and get back on the same page, because they hate Democrats, they hate liberal democracy, and they believe the American government is simply a piggy bank for corrupt billionaires like Donald Trump and Elon Musk, instead of the mechanism to improve your life.
So yes, enjoy this week. You earned it! But these people will remain a corrosive force in American politics until they're removed from it, or at least marginalized to the point that they have no meaningful influence. Democrats aren't perfect. But, we have a real chance to show people what good government looks like, and part of that job is taking these people on and exposing exactly what they're doing.
That doesn't happen on its own.
When they lose, they whine on the internet. They threaten to leave. They blame Muslims and trans kids and anyone but themselves.
When we lose, we go back to work the next morning. That's what I did in 2024, and it's what we'll keep doing until these people are gone from our politics.
With urgency,
--Mike

MAGA lost, and now they want to quit America. | | | Nov 5 | | | | | | | | | | | | Already a paid subscriber? Then like, share, and keep showing up in the comments. It matters more than you know. Election night was amazing for so many reasons. Watching a new generation of Democratic leaders rise, Texas turning blue, and getting the chance to put one hand back on the wheel for sanity and decency in this country, was extraordinary. But I'll be honest. There was something else I was enjoying, too: the total meltdown of MAGA influencers as they lose their grip on reality. They're being forced to accept that they're unpopular, and that they've spent the last two years destroying this country. A lot of them can't handle it. Exhibit A, my old pal Laura Loomer. Conspiracy theorist, right-wing lunatic, deeply unwell human being. On Elon Musk's Twitter, she announced that America was over, that we're now an Islamic country, and basically threatened to leave. That one has stuck with me, because I know what it feels like to lose. When Democrats lost in 2024, when someone I have a great deal of respect for--Kamala Harris--lost, I didn't say America was over. I didn't threaten to leave. I didn't claim we'd been overrun by Nazis. I went back to work. I tried to figure out what I had done to contribute to this mess and what I could do differently over the next two years. Out of that came Endless Urgency and much of what I'm building right now to help rebuild the Democratic Party and fix this country. Loomer isn't doing that. She's threatening to leave. Which, by the way, I'd support. That's the message I sent her on Twitter, and I want to repeat it to all of you, because these people are disgustingly unpatriotic: You're free to leave. The American people have spoken. Apparently they're the last institution in this country willing to stand up to Donald Trump and the Republican Party. MAGA doesn't like it. Fine. You can leave. And that goes double for Laura Loomer, Tim Pool, Benny Johnson, and the rest of the MAGA influencer class, who are so very clearly taking money from foreign governments to pollute our politics and spread propaganda. Get the fuck out of our country. Go to whatever Middle Eastern nation has been paying your bills and go live there. Leave us the fuck alone. And it isn't just the influencers. The craziness is everywhere. I was on a right-wing show yesterday and suggested that Republicans lost because they've lost touch with reality. They spend too much time in their echo chambers and let crazy people run their campaigns, run for office, instead of qualified human beings who might actually know what the fuck they're doing. * A woman from Texas started screaming at me. James Talarico, she said, was going to steal my child and turn him trans. I hadn't even recovered from that when she explained the real reason Greg Abbott lost: he let too many Muslims into Texas. That's where the Republican Party is right now. In 2025 there were a million think pieces about whether Democrats would learn the lesson of 2024: that we were too often focused on the wrong things instead of passing legislation and focusing on ways to make a material difference in your life. That's the lesson Republicans should be learning right now. Instead, they're doubling down on the same stupid shit. Loomer crashing out about America becoming Islamic and a woman screaming about Muslims in Texas aren't outliers. They are the party. These people contribute nothing to society and nothing to public discourse except hate and lies. I hope someday they see the light and become more than the miserable human beings they are. I don't expect it. Here's where the fun of election night ends. As much they'll threaten to leave, they're not going anywhere. There's a presidential election coming, and it will be a huge opportunity to make money and steal influence. JD Vance is already rebuilding the freak coalition for 2028. He won't fully condemn Nick Fuentes, who is basically a white supremacist, and he's back-channeling with Tucker Carlson to keep him out of the race. They'll all make up and get back on the same page, because they hate Democrats, they hate liberal democracy, and they believe the American government is simply a piggy bank for corrupt billionaires like Donald Trump and Elon Musk, instead of the mechanism to improve your life. So yes, enjoy this week. You earned it! But these people will remain a corrosive force in American politics until they're removed from it, or at least marginalized to the point that they have no meaningful influence. Democrats aren't perfect. But, we have a real chance to show people what good government looks like, and part of that job is taking these people on and exposing exactly what they're doing. That doesn't happen on its own. When they lose, they whine on the internet. They threaten to leave. They blame Muslims and trans kids and anyone but themselves. When we lose, we go back to work the next morning. That's what I did in 2024, and it's what we'll keep doing until these people are gone from our politics. | | Friend,

On Tuesday Oakland, Berkeley, Alameda, San Leandro, Piedmont, Emeryville, and Albany voted to send me back to Congress. I could not be more grateful.

And across the country, voters delivered a generational mandate for change.

We have our work cut out for us.

As the member of Congress for the East Bay, I can promise you this:

I will demand, and we will win affordability for our people. For the Oakland teachers who cannot afford a one-bedroom apartment, and for everyone struggling to make ends meet.

I will fight for healthcare for all – so that no child has to go without cancer treatment in the richest country on Earth.

I will fight with everything I have to dismantle Jim Crow 3.0 and end the attacks on Black life, and on the right to vote.

I will protect our neighbors who are immigrants, as well as our queer and trans community members.

I will demand that our taxpayer dollars never be used to buy bombs for Gaza, for Yemen, for Sudan, or for Haiti.

I will say no to illegal wars and I will vote for meals over munitions every single time.

I will spend my time chasing resources, not cameras – because I measure my success on the results that I deliver, rather than the headlines I generate.

**In the next Congress I will be even more determined, focused, and committed to the fight, because this moment requires it.**

So show up, hold me to every word, and call us out when we fail to deliver on the change that voters so clearly and desperately need.

I didn't get into politics because I enjoy shaking hands and raising money.

I ran for office to fight like hell for the people of the East Bay. God willing, that is what I am going back to do.

Thank you for your support, and I cannot wait to get back to work.

With hope,

Lateefah

I could not be more grateful. And across the country, voters delivered a generational mandate for change. We have our work cut out for us. As the member of Congress for the East Bay, I can promise you this: I will demand, and we will win affordability for our people. For the Oakland teachers who cannot afford a one-bedroom apartment, and for everyone struggling to make ends meet. I will fight for healthcare for all – so that no child has to go without cancer treatment in the richest country on Earth. I will fight with everything I have to dismantle Jim Crow 3.0 and end the attacks on Black life, and on the right to vote. I will protect our neighbors who are immigrants, as well as our queer and trans community members. I will demand that our taxpayer dollars never be used to buy bombs for Gaza, for Yemen, for Sudan, or for Haiti. I will say no to illegal wars and I will vote for meals over munitions every single time. I will spend my time chasing resources, not cameras – because I measure my success on the results that I deliver, rather than the headlines I generate. In the next Congress I will be even more determined, focused, and committed to the fight, because this moment requires it. So show up, hold me to every word, and call us out when we fail to deliver on the change that voters so clearly and desperately need. I didn't get into politics because I enjoy shaking hands and raising money. I ran for office to fight like hell for the people of the East Bay. God willing, that is what I am going back to do. Thank you for your support, and I cannot wait to get back to work. # One last favor, and a big thank you
---
| | | | | | Friend,
I want to start with two words: thank you.
Thank you for the doors you knocked, the calls you made, the yard signs you put up, the events you showed up for, and every dollar you gave to this campaign. Whether you gave $5 or volunteered every weekend since spring, you were part of something that mattered.
The result wasn't what we worked for. But I'm proud of the campaign we ran and the ideas we put in front of New Mexicans: safer communities, a stronger economy, schools that deliver for our kids, and a state government that answers to the people it serves. Those ideas don't go away because an election is over. They're still worth fighting for, and I'll keep fighting for them.
I have one last favor to ask.
Our signs are still standing in yards, along roads, and on street corners across New Mexico. If you put one up, or you see one on property where you have permission, please take it down this week and either recycle it or throw it away. Please don't remove signs from private property without the owner's okay, and stay safe near traffic.
Leaving our communities cleaner than we found them is the right way to close out this campaign.
Being your candidate has been one of the great honors of my life. Carrie and I are grateful to every one of you.
With gratitude,

Thank you for the doors you knocked, the calls you made, the yard signs you put up, the events you showed up for, and every dollar you gave to this campaign. Whether you gave $5 or volunteered every weekend since spring, you were part of something that mattered. The result wasn't what we worked for. But I'm proud of the campaign we ran and the ideas we put in front of New Mexicans: safer communities, a stronger economy, schools that deliver for our kids, and a state government that answers to the people it serves. Those ideas don't go away because an election is over. They're still worth fighting for, and I'll keep fighting for them. I have one last favor to ask. Our signs are still standing in yards, along roads, and on street corners across New Mexico.
