name: Ryan Grim
subject: What’s next for Drop Site
body:
The newsletters that run Capitol Hill are written for insiders. Ours won't be.

| |
---|---|---
|
# What's next for Drop Site
### The newsletters that run Capitol Hill are written for insiders. Ours won't be.
| | | [Ryan Grim](https://substack.com/@ryangrim)
---
| Nov 5
---
| [](https://substack.com/@ryangrim)
---
At Drop Site, [we're launching something new that we need your help with](https://substack.com/redirect/064bac69-eb30-4607-8e3e-c53975464461?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). More on how you can help below, but first, let me lay out the problem we plan to solve.
### **What voters asked for**
Look at what even JD Vance said out loud after the election. In his own words, he interpreted the results of Tuesday's election as an order from the voters to:
1. End the war
2. Focus on cost of living/inflation
3. Put America First
4. Change our relationship to Israel

Democrats, broadly, agree with that set of priorities, particularly the new candidates who won this week. So the agenda of Congress, and the approach to covering it by the media, obviously ought to reflect this new mandate, right? If only it was that easy.
### **What the coverage left out**
CNN's first impulse, for instance, was to ask James Talarico - apparently in all sincerity - if he will stand up to Abdul El-Sayed in the Senate. And as votes were being cast on Tuesday, Punchbowl, which runs a powerful and widely read Capitol Hill newsletter, reported in a text message, exclusively to subscribers: "Top House and Senate Republican and Democratic appropriators are planning to meet early next week to discuss FY2027 funding. Gov. funding runs out on Dec. 11. This four corners meeting will kick off lame-duck spending talks."
You might notice something about that news report: **It is utterly inscrutable to anybody who isn 't steeped in Capitol Hill minutiae**. What funding choices will be discussed? What are the battle lines? What on earth is a "four corners meeting" and is this something the public can participate in - since, after all, they will be spending the people's money on, allegedly, the voters' priorities.
If the goal of the news item was to mystify the process and keep the public out of it, mission accomplished.
What the news item left out is crucial, however: The December 11th deadline is an opportunity for Democrats and antiwar Republicans to cut off money for the war in a way that would genuinely force it to end, just as Vice President J.D. Vance says we ought to. That's how the Vietnam war was brought to an end by Congress, and that's how this one can be.
Yet top-ranking Democrats and Republicans are working quickly and quietly behind the scenes to pass a spending bill that makes it impossible to have that fight, leaving the war-making power in the hands of President Trump. Sounds like big news, right?
That's the news people need to know, so they can act on it before it's too late, and before we're back in another phase of the war voters so fiercely rejected.
_**[That's why Drop Site is launching a new Capitol Hill newsletter, written for the public, not lobbyists, that tells you what Congress is planning before the votes happen. Help us launch it.](https://substack.com/redirect/064bac69-eb30-4607-8e3e-c53975464461?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**_
_We need to raise $100,000 before December 11 to get this off the ground.[Can you chip in today? ](https://substack.com/redirect/064bac69-eb30-4607-8e3e-c53975464461?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_
[HELP US RAISE $100K - DONATE NOW](https://substack.com/redirect/064bac69-eb30-4607-8e3e-c53975464461?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
### **Who Capitol Hill news is written for**
The structure of today's congressional reporting is such that it can't truly produce the kind of journalism the public needs to be able to weigh in. The audience is lobbyists and insiders, and the advertisers are the ones most heavily affected by Congress: defense contractors, AI, Big Pharma, financial institutions and crypto, and Big Oil make up the bulk of the revenue for the media companies covering Capitol Hill.
The dominant forces are Punchbowl, Politico, and Axios, each of which publish influential newsletters. But when it comes to issues of war and peace, AI, or Israel, their coverage routinely pulls punches.
Capitol Hill's information ecosystem is heavily contaminated by newsletter culture, but there isn't a single newsletter that is aimed at a mass public audience. The thinking is that the public just doesn't care enough. But there used to be one in the 2010s. It was called HuffPost Hill, and in its prime it had a huge readership and was highly influential on the Hill. Everyone read it because everyone read it, and it broke news that the others would miss. I co-wrote it for years, but it's sadly gone defunct.
In January, ten or eleven new Democratic senators will arrive in town, joined by many dozens of House freshmen. What they produce as lawmakers will depend significantly on the information diet they have available to them. If it's simply the toxic corporate brew that's served up today, we shouldn't be surprised at what comes out the other end.
### **Drop Site is entering the arena**
Over the past two years, Drop Site has built up the institutional credibility -- partly thanks to the video interviews done by our indefatigable and omnipresent colleague Julian Andreone -- to compete in this space. Not only can we produce a newsletter that helps drive the conversation, but it will also act as a check against the others, and push them to beat us in the areas where we'll focus: war, our complicity with war crimes and genocide, the role of AI in society, and, as Vance put it, "cost of living/inflation." (Looks like he was afraid of the term affordability.)
_That 's the gap our new Hill coverage will fill._ We plan to launch ahead of the Dec. 11 war funding deadline, and I'll dust off my congressional loafers to help the small team we're building.
**[But we need your help building it. Our goal is $100,000, to make sure this is fully funded and we can expand. Can you chip in today?](https://substack.com/redirect/064bac69-eb30-4607-8e3e-c53975464461?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Too often investigative journalism tells us what has already happened. The public needs to know what our political leaders are planning to do before they do it. [If you can make a contribution - big or small - that goes a long way.](https://substack.com/redirect/064bac69-eb30-4607-8e3e-c53975464461?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[FUND OUR HILL COVERAGE - DONATE TODAY](https://substack.com/redirect/064bac69-eb30-4607-8e3e-c53975464461?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
We need millions of people reading this newsletter who can then produce social media content based on it, which'll give the public the chance to weigh in on congressional action.
### **The December fights**
It doesn't just start in January. In December there will be major votes on Senate majority leader, the war funding measure, and perhaps the National Defense Authorization Act, which pro-Israel forces are trying to use to fuse the Israeli and U.S. military industrial bases.
When that happens, with your support, Drop Site will be front and center in covering it - and you'll be able to learn what's happening in time to do something about it.
[PUT THE PUBLIC IN THE ROOM - DONATE NOW!](https://substack.com/redirect/064bac69-eb30-4607-8e3e-c53975464461?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
See you on the Hill,
Ryan Grim
P.S. Building a newsroom on Capitol Hill that answers to the public, not lobbyists, takes serious investment. If you believe in what we're building and want to play a bigger role in launching it, email [majorgiving@dropsitenews.com](https://substack.com/redirect/7db224e2-1787-42a8-99e3-474cb073397e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) or visit our [Ways to Give page.](https://substack.com/redirect/a0a657ba-61eb-4d15-b718-42ca33369729?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

Drop Site News Inc., 1930 18th St NW
Ste B2 #1034, Washington, DC 20009

body:

Friend,
---
| | | Her name is Luka Hein. She was **16 years old** when doctors removed her breasts. **Now she wants a jury to hear what happened to her.** But getting Luka into that courtroom has become a battle of its own. I’m Mark Trammell, CEO of the**Center for American Liberty** , a nonprofit public interest law firm that takes on cases many organizations won’t touch. And I’m asking you to help us fight for Luka.
---
[](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
[ **Help Luka Get Her Day in Court** ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
As we described in her lawsuit, Luka was a deeply troubled teenager. Her parents had divorced. She struggled with anxiety, isolation, school, panic attacks, self-harm, and thoughts of suicide. Then she encountered transgender influencers online. At 15, Luka began receiving gender-related care. At 16, doctors removed her breasts. Testosterone came months later. Luka now alleges that the medical professionals who treated her failed to provide the proper standard of care and failed to obtain informed consent. **Her case is headed toward a jury trial currently scheduled for June, 2027.** **But the legal battle is already raging.** Right now, the defendants are challenging expert testimony Luka intends to present regarding the standard of care. **These kinds of fights mean more motions, more legal work, more time, and more expense.**
---
[ **Help Luka Get Her Day in Court** ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
And that can become a strategy all its own — **make litigation so long and expensive that the other side runs out of resources.** **We refuse to let that happen.** We’ve been here before. The **Center for American Liberty** represents detransitioner **Chloe Cole** in her lawsuit against the medical providers she alleged harmed her. The hospital defendants aggressively filed motions delaying Chloe’s trial by years. We fought back and now Chloe’s trial is scheduled for April. **We are prepared to fight just as hard for Luka.** But unlike the powerful institutions we face, the **Center for American Liberty** is a nonprofit. **We depend on Americans like you.** **[Your first gift of $25, $50, $100, $250, or whatever you can give, helps us answer these legal challenges and keep Luka’s case moving toward a jury.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)**
---
[ **Help Luka Get Her Day in Court** ](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
---
**This is why our organization exists.** There are Americans all across this country who have been silenced, pushed out, or left to fight powerful institutions alone. We stand beside them. **And we fight.** I came to the **Center for American Liberty** because I wanted to get my hands dirty and be in the courtroom fighting these cases because somebody has to do it. As I often ask: **Who’s going to represent these people if we don’t?** Luka had the courage to put her name on this lawsuit. She is prepared to tell a jury what happened. Now she needs Americans willing to stand behind her. Please make your first gift to the **Center for American Liberty** today. Help us fight every legal obstacle between Luka and her day in court. For Liberty,
---
| | | Mark Trammell
Chief Executive Officer
Center for American Liberty

---

Now she wants a jury to hear what happened to her. But getting Luka into that courtroom has become a battle of its own. I’m Mark Trammell, CEO of theCenter for American Liberty , a nonprofit public interest law firm that takes on cases many organizations won’t touch. And I’m asking you to help us fight for Luka. As we described in her lawsuit, Luka was a deeply troubled teenager. Her parents had divorced. She struggled with anxiety, isolation, school, panic attacks, self-harm, and thoughts of suicide. Then she encountered transgender influencers online. At 15, Luka began receiving gender-related care. At 16, doctors removed her breasts. Testosterone came months later. Luka now alleges that the medical professionals who treated her failed to provide the proper standard of care and failed to obtain informed consent. Her case is headed toward a jury trial currently scheduled for June, 2027. But the legal battle is already raging. Right now, the defendants are challenging expert testimony Luka intends to present regarding the standard of care. These kinds of fights mean more motions, more legal work, more time, and more expense. And that can become a strategy all its own — make litigation so long and expensive that the other side runs out of resources. We refuse to let that happen. We’ve been here before. The Center for American Liberty represents detransitioner Chloe Cole in her lawsuit against the medical providers she alleged harmed her. The hospital defendants aggressively filed motions delaying Chloe’s trial by years. We fought back and now Chloe’s trial is scheduled for April. We are prepared to fight just as hard for Luka. body:
Derek –

I wanted you to get this update from me:
Ballots are still being counted, and right now, it’s still too close to
call.

We are going to do everything we can to make sure every single vote is
counted in this race.

But I’ll be honest: That is going to take time – and plenty of resources
that we don’t currently have.

As we fight to make sure every ballot is counted, we’re going to remain
the top target of the DC establishment.

We put everything we had into winning this race, so I’m counting on your
help to fight back against their attacks.

It looks like we’re in this for the long haul, so I need your help to
sustain our fight until every vote is counted.

From the very beginning, this campaign has been powered by grassroots
donations from people like you. I’m proud of that fact, but it means it’s
going to take lots of us to stand up to their pressure in the coming days.

That’s why I have to ask:

us keep fighting.

Friend, The results are in, and our race for the 7th Congressional District was called in favor of Michael Alfonso. I called Michael on Election Night and congratulated him.

I’m disappointed, of course, and I know that disappointment is shared by our team and so many of our enthusiastic supporters. And on behalf of our team I want to extend our sincere gratitude to the hundreds of people who have helped us run this campaign.

**It’s worth looking at the big picture to see how far we’ve come. For a seat won by a 26% margin in 2024, we cut that margin by more than half to 12%. **

We launched this campaign knowing we wouldn’t have millions to spend and knowing we’d have to earn every dollar and every vote. We worked hard, we looked out for all our neighbors, and we ran a campaign that showed respect for everyone.

And we’ve already accomplished some things that all that Washington and corporate money could never buy. We built a stronger and broader coalition than we have seen in many years here in Northern Wisconsin. And that coalition lives on, and that’s only going to get stronger.

We can be proud that our efforts helped contribute to strong Democratic majorities in Congress and in Madison.

**I’m asking all our supporters today to make a promise: Let’s hold elected officials of all parties in Washington and in Madison accountable for a government that’s constitutional, fair, and moral. **

And let’s rest up and go back tomorrow, or the next day, to the work of being citizens and members of an incredible community.

Along with so many of you, we’ve created a movement and it’s bigger than me or any one of us, and it will last as long as we continue to invest in this work together.

_“You are not obligated to complete the work, but neither are you free to abandon it.” — _The Talmud

On behalf of our entire team, I want to extend our warmest and most sincere thanks to everyone who has supported our campaign in so many different ways. Together we _have_ made a difference.

With deepest gratitude,
Fred

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142961040/658628363/1489846760?refcode=email_header&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MDQ3MSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3OThiNDQ4YS0zZWQ5LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=M9eGjBR4vqYt2vCHDaCt43eEOEPc4dHOY6H5peSqnGA=) Peter, **Tuesday night, we delivered a historic BLUE WAVE across the Commonwealth and nation.** You knocked doors, made calls, rallied your communities, chipped in when you could, and voted like our future depended on it — _because it did._ **And together, we reelected Governor Josh Shapiro and Lieutenant Governor Austin Davis. We flipped the Pennsylvania Senate and expanded the Pennsylvania House, delivering a Democratic Trifecta in Harrisburg for the first time in 30 years. We won every single toss-up congressional race and are sending four incredible leaders — Bob Harvie, Bob Brooks, Paige Cognetti, and Janelle Stelson — to Washington.** Under Governor Shapiro’s leadership and with support from our grassroots team, the Pennsylvania Democratic Party built the historic midterm coordinated campaign that registered voters, drove Democratic turnout, competed everywhere, and organized up and down the ballot. **Today, we celebrate our wins and prepare for the work ahead. Your Pennsylvania Democratic Party is looking ahead to 2027 and 2028, focused on what we can accomplish together next — with Democrats leading in Harrisburg, fighting for working families across the Commonwealth, and building a stronger future for every Pennsylvanian.** We made history together, Peter. And I couldn’t be more proud of us. Thank you for being part of it, and let's get back to work! Sincerely, Larry K. Hailsham Jr.

subject: Sick of the cheating? Read this.
body:
Non-citizens on the rolls, ballots counted days late, machines that won't work. We can fix this

Non-citizens on the rolls, ballots counted days late, machines that won't work. We can fix this.

| | | |
---
| | | Friend,
---
I'll be honest with you. I'm frustrated with how the 2026 midterms turned out, and if you're reading this, I'd guess you are too.Look at what we watched happen this cycle. On Election Day, ballot scanners failed across Westchester County, **New York** , in one of the closest House races in the country, held by a Republican incumbent, and poll workers stuffed completed ballots into emergency bags saying they would just be counted later. Throughout this election cycle, you stood with EMILYs List women — even when the polls had us behind, the odds seemed stacked against us, and the future looked uncertain. name: Chris Deluzio
subject: So now what?
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Chris Deluzio for Congress
body:
We kept faith with the idea that we're a government of the people, by the people, for the people.
# [](https://act.chrisforpa.com/go/46?t=1&akid=165%2E42639%2E9tRW-W)
First and foremost, I want to thank you.
To everyone who donated, volunteered, posted, shared a kind word about me or the importance of this election with friends or family members... Thank you.
Together, in this election, we did the most American thing possible: We took power into our own hands and we did it at the ballot box.
We kept faith with the idea that we're a government of the people, by the people, for the people.
We sent a message to Trump and his friends in the Epstein class, to the oligarchs, to the robber barons, to the corrupt: your time in power is ending.
We did it in my district in western Pennsylvania, we did it across the entire commonwealth, and we did it across the country.
So what happens next?
It doesn't need to be complicated.
We must end the war in Iran.
And we must ensure that the people of this country who work hard, bust their butt, and play by the rules have a shot at a decent life.
That if you do those things, you have a roof over your head, living where you want to and being able to do it with one job. That you get to start a family when you want and be able to spend time with your newborn child after they are born. That you get to go to the doctor when you need to and can get the medicine you need to live a healthy life without going bankrupt.
Not complicated. Not radical.
Not easy, either.
Because while we won an election — that is not the end point, it is simply a checkpoint in a larger journey. A necessary one... but not the final one.
So thank you for your support and everything you did to make Tuesday possible. And I look forward to taking the next steps together in the future.
Don't give up the ship,
Chris Deluzio

| | Dear Team Maxine, **Tuesday was an incredible night.** I am deeply grateful to the people of Oregon's 3rd Congressional District for placing their trust in me to continue representing them in Congress. It is an incredible honor to serve this community, and I don't take that responsibility lightly. The results of this election were beyond our wildest imagination. Up against hundreds of millions of dollars from billionaires and corporate interests, we saw the extraordinary power of people coming together. No amount of money could silence the volunteers knocking on doors, the neighbors organizing their communities, or the people who showed up for one another and refused to give up. **This victory belongs to you.** I first ran for Congress because, as a physician, I know that the health, safety, and resilience of our communities depend on elected leaders who put people ahead of corporations and special interests. Over the past two years, I've brought that commitment to Congress, fighting to lower costs, protect access to healthcare, defend our fundamental freedoms, and hold those in power accountable. From standing up for our immigrant neighbors and protecting our environment to delivering meaningful results for veterans and working families, I'm proud of what we've accomplished.
---
| | |
---
| |
---
| |
---
| |
---
| | | **And we're just getting started.** The promise of America has never been about where we come from. It's about what we can build together and the future we choose to create. When we show up for one another, we demonstrate what we stand for: dignity, compassion, community, and the belief that our greatest strength comes from one another. **Elections matter. Showing up matters. And what we do next matters just as much.** To everyone who knocked on doors, donated, volunteered, shared our message, encouraged a neighbor, or simply believed in what we're working toward: **thank you. You made this possible.** As we look toward the next Congress, my commitment remains the same: to listen, lead with compassion, fight for the people I represent, and work every day to build a future where everyone has the opportunity to thrive. I'm energized by what's ahead, and I'm grateful to have you alongside me. Now, let's get to work. **❤️** With gratitude,Maxine

name: Chris Pappas
subject: The first out gay man in the U.S. Senate
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Chris Pappas for Senate
body:
My community showed me what’s possible.
# [](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1&akid=9992%2E582294%2Elq2v3e)
When I was a kid, reading this kind of headline would have been unimaginable:
[](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261105_1.V0CLfD&refcode=em20261105-1&t=2&akid=9992%2E582294%2Elq2v3e)
Growing up as a gay person in New Hampshire, I never imagined I could live openly — let alone serve in the U.S. Senate. But my community showed me what's possible.
**You helped me win _four times_ in one of the swingiest congressional districts in the country, and on Tuesday you elected me as your next U.S. Senator from New Hampshire.**
We’ve made tremendous progress since I was younger. And this week New Hampshire did something our country has never done before. **We elected an out gay man to the U.S. Senate.**
I didn’t run to make history. I ran for Granite Staters and for all of us. But moving the needle of progress forward is deeply meaningful to me.
This is a moment for long-overdue representation in Washington. It’s also important that LGBTQ+ people have more seats at the table at a time when our rights are under attack.
**We won this election for the people of New Hampshire, charting a path forward for our shared future — and we tore down a barrier and made history at the same time.**
**[Will you make a $5 contribution right now to help us build on this historic win and start getting to work for New Hampshire?](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261105_1.V0CLfD&refcode=em20261105-1&t=3&akid=9992%2E582294%2Elq2v3e)**
**Thank you for supporting me in this campaign.** No matter who you are, who you love, who you pray to, or where you're from — know that I'll always have your back.
With gratitude,
Chris

The results of this election make it clear why Donald Trump tried so hard to restrict vote-by-mail in our state:

| | | | Since taking office as Oregon’s Attorney General in 2025, Dan Rayfield has focused on protecting Oregon’s working families and homegrown small businesses by taking on pharmaceutical companies, polluters, and large corporations driving up costs for groceries and other everyday needs. He’s been fighting hard to block the Trump Administration from taking away the rights of Oregonians, suing Trump–and winning–dozens of times.

[ ](https://us.list-manage.com/JPzigkVmUVr?e=1768325bd4&c2id=0fcd3a526fabf816bd24466788989260)

Dan grew up in Oregon and is a product of the Oregon public school system. Following his graduation from Tigard High School, Dan attended Western Oregon University and then earned his law degree from Willamette University College of Law. In 2005, prior to his law school graduation, he clerked for the Benton County District Attorney’s office. During his time at the District Attorney’s office, he gained his first trial experience prosecuting DUIs and other misdemeanor charges. Dan has also served as a coach attorney for the OSU Mock Trial Team, a former Linn County Peer Court Judge, and Past President of the Linn-Benton Bar Association.

Since 2015, Dan served as the State Representative for Oregon House District 16, which encompasses the cities of Corvallis and Philomath, and Oregon State University. In 2022, he was elected by his colleagues to serve as Speaker of the House. Over that time, he helped lead the way on issues including a high quality education for our children, access to affordable and reliable healthcare, making sure families are able to earn a living wage while simultaneously nurturing innovation and supporting Oregon’s small businesses, and making our public safety system more effective and accountable. Dan lives in Corvallis with his wife Amanda and their son Adam.

clean_body: We want to know your biggest concerns for the new sessions| | | | | | You are invited to join our one-click issue response poll. For data integrity purposes, please do not complete this survey if your email address is not dpwillis67@gmail.com. With new majorities elected in Congress and state legislatures across the country, we need to know if your voting rights priorities have changed so that we can prioritize for January. Please take our quick one-click poll: | | | Friend, which voting rights issue is most important to you? By clicking a response below your answer will be automatically recorded: | | | = | | = | | | = | | = | | | = | | = | | | | | | | | | ---|---|---|--- Integrity First Voter Action Project is dedicated to expanding ballot access and increasing voter participation across the country. Since the Supreme Court gutted key provisions in the Voting Rights Act, extreme politicians have taken advantage to pass harsh laws that restrict access to the ballot box. These restrictions particularly affect disadvantaged communities and people of color. It’s our goal to bring awareness to these laws wherever they may crop up and organize voters to take action to ensure the right to vote is available to everyone in their states and communities. = = Contributions or gifts to Integrity First Voter Action Project are not tax deductible as charitable contributions or as business expenses under IRC Section 162(3). As we fight to make sure every ballot is counted, we’re going to remain the top target of the DC establishment. clean_body: | | | | Derek — I wanted you to get this update from me: Ballots are still being counted, and right now, it’s still too close to call. We are going to do everything we can to make sure every single vote is counted in this race. But I’ll be honest: That is going to take time – and plenty of resources that we don’t currently have. As we fight to make sure every ballot is counted, we’re going to remain the top target of the DC establishment. We put everything we had into winning this race, so I’m counting on your help to fight back against their attacks. It looks like we’re in this for the long haul, so I need your help to sustain our fight until every vote is counted. From the very beginning, this campaign has been powered by grassroots donations from people like you. I’m proud of that fact, but it means it’s going to take lots of us to stand up to their pressure in the coming days. Inside, you'll find the deadlines that matter, two public hearings on November 9, a Native American Heritage Month calendar, and an invitation to our National Day of Mourning sunrise ceremony. We also need your help — our capacity is stretched, and even a few hours a week makes a difference. Every dollar stays in our communities and goes straight to protecting the Haw River and Cape Fear watersheds and the places our ancestors rest. Can you give today, before the December 4 deadline? | | |

November is a month of remembrance, and this year it is also a month of action. Enbridge has formally filed for a state water permit on its Chatham County pipeline, and the public comment window closes **December 4**. ## The Enbridge Chatham pipeline: comments due December 4
On October 30, Public Service Company of North Carolina (now operating as Enbridge Gas North Carolina) applied to the NC Division of Water Resources for a **Section 401 Individual Water Quality Certification** for its EGNC Chatham County System Expansion Project. The state issued public notice on November 3. This permit determines whether the pipeline can cross our streams and wetlands. The project is roughly 28 miles of 12-inch pipe through the Haw River and Cape Fear watersheds. On October 26, North Carolina legislators wrote to NCDEQ asking it to deny the 401 certification over water quality concerns. **Key details**
* Project number: 20261460 Ver 1 (Chatham County)
* Comment deadline: **5 p.m., Friday, December 4, 2026** — also DWR's proposed date of final action
* Comment online: the Public Notice Comment Form on [DEQ's Individual Certifications public notice page](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.yjJN_MEbNx94PLaWzZ6hW6l1750ZTgCwLFK0Isi1cpLnPKTNm7wW7NyrRPhlHcRlqVXc1x0_HcjSwsaPhgq7lk8GoiDzU_hxcoLCyL2n3PJaukln1iXglTc9_YfxDQ3GtY27VA4iP_q416FV-gCz6hImNqPfCOrmeoER5xretsm1TGamOmWB5RHWvU9qSGpKXnRZ3x5H8xznyuiu2RV-zmMijTZAWEpRH53TaIQQAJj7idqjhFGYSk9JChgmcJrkV0tKZtYiqhk-lrXoVbT5D2Q6lGObZOXx6t-oyEYzTKA2lkrogf5jn_cs4QNf1Lb0XlmFa583wOGGpfFNneEp1L_dP1Cde2Cj22yXiRhQgwwWXSIjr7UWO8k6bQE-xQsmaRN4CEYuhwnN3uY-OBZNi2p4Tp1bx11z667iQ96-dcABsIL9xVjm6vgP0ohTA5VfZJrxuOq7R4rYEORAoHfbF9-omc-sfW503c4U66gCXteMBdBPhY_fFILxlaL8ykQaa3XPOgiHltn117VKYPVn6Q/4vh/EMEl2aPPSvS9hP4mZUTI-w/h10/h001.drfbksjJrs5aLTTVarQ2HOkm8c4a-3hbwpEuT5lvDLM)
* Comment by mail: 401 Permitting, 1617 Mail Service Center, Raleigh, NC 27699-1617
* Read the application: online at the same page, or in person at the DWR Raleigh Regional Office, 8 a.m.–5 p.m. weekdays, by appointment

**Questions worth raising in your comment**
1. Which streams, tributaries, wetlands and riparian buffers will be disturbed?
2. Has Enbridge completed archaeological surveys and consultation on historic Indigenous villages, burial grounds, and other culturally significant sites?
3. Has NCDEQ weighed this project alongside other existing and proposed industrial and energy infrastructure in the region?
4. Has the applicant shown it avoided and minimized impacts to our waters?
5. Will NCDEQ and the Army Corps hold a public hearing and give the public full access to the technical documents?

**What 7DS is doing.** We are requesting the complete administrative record from NCDEQ and the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers: delineation maps, stream and wetland crossing tables, proposed mitigation, the alternatives analysis, cultural resource consultation records, and agency correspondence. A filed application is not complete or approved. We are also watching for the federal Section 404 public notice and will share that deadline as soon as it posts.

## Pipelines in our own backyard
The T-15 project is about nine miles north of my home, up Highway 119 past Pleasant Grove and Anderson townships, in Hightowers township. This isn't a distant fight. It is in our neighborhood, and another line is planned just south of us in Chatham. The proposal connected to MVP Southgate would carry fracked gas roughly 45 miles in 30- to 36-inch pipe, with a new compressor station at Ruffin, to feed Duke Energy's two planned gas plants at Hyco Lake. **What a rupture could mean.** A high-pressure line this size would release an enormous volume of gas if it failed. People living within about a quarter mile would be inside the zone of most severe danger, and evacuation could reach a half mile or more. The roar of escaping gas can be heard for miles, and if it ignites, the fireball can rise hundreds of feet. **Who would respond?** Studies have found gaps in how federal pipeline safety programs are carried out at the state level, and North Carolina's local governments have few tools to reduce pipeline hazards. Our rural communities depend on volunteer fire departments. These neighbors are brave, but they are not equipped or trained for a large-diameter gas pipeline fire. **What could happen to our water?** Construction mistakes and ruptures can damage the rock and clay layers that protect underground aquifers. If drilling or an explosion breaches an aquifer, groundwater can flood surrounding soil and permanently lower local water tables. Many of us rely on private wells. We ask the hard questions now because once the pipe is in the ground, we have to live with these risks.

## In Washington: threats to tribal consultation and the Native count
**The permitting bill (BAAJA) and Section 106.** S. 5653, the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026, is now being debated in Congress. Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act requires federal agencies to consult with tribes before approving projects that could affect sacred sites and ancestral lands. Groups like NDN Collective call the bill's changes an unprecedented attack on tribal rights. Critics point to four changes:
* **Optional consultation:** government-to-government consultation with Tribal Nations would become optional for many projects.
* **Narrower harm:** agencies would no longer weigh indirect, visual, atmospheric or audible impacts unless they directly and significantly damage a site's physical character.
* **Unilateral decisions:** agencies could declare "no adverse effect," or that other considerations outweigh preservation, over tribal objections.
* **Rigid deadlines:** Tribal Historic Preservation Officers would face 30- to 90-day review windows. If deadlines are missed, even because developers sent incomplete information, funding could be withheld or THPO functions taken over.

**The 2030 Census proposal.** The Census Bureau has proposed removing race and ethnicity questions from the short-form 2030 questionnaire. That would eliminate the American Indian and Alaska Native checkbox and the tribal write-in line. Tribal leaders warn this would cause a systemic undercount, especially of Native people living off reservation, and shrink federal funding, health care allocations, and fair voting districts. The Bureau suggests using administrative records and the American Community Survey instead. The Native American Rights Fund and others argue those sources can't capture self-identification or tribal citizenship.
**Where the coalition stands.** Tribal leaders, the All Pueblo Council of Governors and environmental justice groups are calling on Congress to strip the NHPA amendments from BAAJA and on the Census Bureau to halt its overhaul. They argue real efficiency comes from respecting tribal self-determination and true nation-to-nation consultation.
## Native American Heritage Month
Every November honors the cultures, traditions, histories, and contributions of Indigenous peoples. President George H.W. Bush designated it a month-long observance in 1990. November marks the close of the harvest season, long a time of gathering and celebration for many Native nations.
Date | Observance
---|---
Sat, Nov 7 | **National Bison Day** — the cultural, spiritual and economic bond between Tribal Nations and the bison
Wed, Nov 11 | **Veterans Day** — Native American and Alaska Native veterans, who serve at a higher per-capita rate than any other group
Sun, Nov 15 | **Rock Your Mocs Day** — wear moccasins, boots, or mukluks to celebrate tribal identity
Thu, Nov 19 | **Red Shawl Day** — honoring missing and murdered Indigenous people (MMIP)
Fri, Nov 27 | **Native American Heritage Day** — the day after Thanksgiving, better known as Black Friday

**Thankstaking: the untold truth.** The familiar story celebrates a peaceful three-day feast between English settlers and the Wampanoag in 1621. It leaves out what followed: massacres, grave robbing, and centuries of dispossession. For many Native people, Thanksgiving is not a holiday but a National Day of Mourning — a day to honor ancestors who suffered and resisted colonization.
**Gather with intention.** If you do gather, make room for honesty and reflection alongside gratitude:
1. Open the day by acknowledging the Native peoples whose land you are on.
2. Spend part of the day giving back at a food bank, shelter, or community center.
3. Take a gratitude walk outdoors together.
4. Watch a film or documentary centered on Native history and voices.
5. Offer each guest a journal to record reflections through the day.
6. Before the meal, form a circle and share what you are grateful for.

The goal is a gathering that matches your values and tells the truth.

Enbridge has formally filed for a state water permit on its Chatham County pipeline, and the public comment window closes December 4. Closer to home, new gas infrastructure is being planned just miles from our communities. Take action today \- Ask NCDEQ for a full environmental review and public hearing on the Enbridge pipeline \- Pledge to protect Indigenous ancestral and cultural sites threatened by the Enbridge pipeline \- Support the campaign against making customers pay for the proposed pipeline \- Volunteer at the Duke Energy hearing in Lexington or the Stokes County data center hearing in Danbury \- Sign up to volunteer with 7DS, 3–5 hours a week Can't give right now? Sign the petitions below, share this newsletter, or volunteer a few hours a week. Every act of protection counts. The Enbridge Chatham pipeline: comments due December 4 On October 30, Public Service Company of North Carolina (now operating as Enbridge Gas North Carolina) applied to the NC Division of Water Resources for a Section 401 Individual Water Quality Certification for its EGNC Chatham County System Expansion Project. The state issued public notice on November 3. This permit determines whether the pipeline can cross our streams and wetlands. The project is roughly 28 miles of 12-inch pipe through the Haw River and Cape Fear watersheds. On October 26, North Carolina legislators wrote to NCDEQ asking it to deny the 401 certification over water quality concerns. Key details Project number: 20261460 Ver 1 (Chatham County) Comment deadline: 5 p.m., Friday, December 4, 2026 — also DWR's proposed date of final action Comment online: the Public Notice Comment Form on Comment by mail: 401 Permitting, 1617 Mail Service Center, Raleigh, NC 27699-1617 Read the application: online at the same page, or in person at the DWR Raleigh Regional Office, 8 a.m.–5 p.m. weekdays, by appointment Questions worth raising in your comment 1. Which streams, tributaries, wetlands and riparian buffers will be disturbed? 2. Has Enbridge completed archaeological surveys and consultation on historic Indigenous villages, burial grounds, and other culturally significant sites? 3. Has NCDEQ weighed this project alongside other existing and proposed industrial and energy infrastructure in the region? 4. Has the applicant shown it avoided and minimized impacts to our waters? 5. Will NCDEQ and the Army Corps hold a public hearing and give the public full access to the technical documents? What 7DS is doing. We are requesting the complete administrative record from NCDEQ and the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers: delineation maps, stream and wetland crossing tables, proposed mitigation, the alternatives analysis, cultural resource consultation records, and agency correspondence. A filed application is not complete or approved. We are also watching for the federal Section 404 public notice and will share that deadline as soon as it posts. Join our virtual Public Comment Party — November 20 Not sure what to say to NCDEQ? We'll help. Join us on Zoom on Friday, November 20, from 6 to 8 p.m. for a free Public Comment Party on Enbridge's Chatham County pipeline. Together we'll learn what the 28-mile pipeline could mean for the Haw River and Cape Fear watersheds, wildlife, and Indigenous cultural sites, then turn your concerns into a personal comment. We'll walk you through submitting it to NCDEQ before you log off. No experience needed. You don't have to be a scientist or a lawyer, just someone who cares about our water and land. Bring your questions and your stories. Everyone is welcome. · Comments are due December 4 at 5 p.m. (Project 20261460 Ver 1) Pipelines in our own backyard The T-15 project is about nine miles north of my home, up Highway 119 past Pleasant Grove and Anderson townships, in Hightowers township. This isn't a distant fight. It is in our neighborhood, and another line is planned just south of us in Chatham. The proposal connected to MVP Southgate would carry fracked gas roughly 45 miles in 30- to 36-inch pipe, with a new compressor station at Ruffin, to feed Duke Energy's two planned gas plants at Hyco Lake. What a rupture could mean. A high-pressure line this size would release an enormous volume of gas if it failed. People living within about a quarter mile would be inside the zone of most severe danger, and evacuation could reach a half mile or more. The roar of escaping gas can be heard for miles, and if it ignites, the fireball can rise hundreds of feet. Who would respond? Studies have found gaps in how federal pipeline safety programs are carried out at the state level, and North Carolina's local governments have few tools to reduce pipeline hazards. Our rural communities depend on volunteer fire departments. These neighbors are brave, but they are not equipped or trained for a large-diameter gas pipeline fire. What could happen to our water? Construction mistakes and ruptures can damage the rock and clay layers that protect underground aquifers. If drilling or an explosion breaches an aquifer, groundwater can flood surrounding soil and permanently lower local water tables. Many of us rely on private wells. We ask the hard questions now because once the pipe is in the ground, we have to live with these risks. The NC Oil & Gas Commission is taking comments on whether the state's fracking rules are "necessary" or "unnecessary." It is the first step in a rule review, and some commissioners have said they intend to weaken those protections. The comment period ends November 9. Organizations: sign on to the coalition letter stating that every one of these rules is necessary, by the end of the day on November 8. [[Read the letter here]]() Individuals: It will be delivered on November 9. We co-sponsored this petition with our friends at Clean Water for NC. North Carolinians fought hard for these rules in 2014–15. Let's show the Commission we are still paying attention. Show up November 9: two public hearings Two hearings on Monday, November 9, both at 6:00 p.m., could shape our land, water, and energy future. We need volunteers at each to listen, document, and, if you're comfortable, speak. | Hearing | Location | What's at stake ---|---|--- Duke Energy hearing, Davidson County | Davidson County Commissioners Room, 913 N. Greensboro St., Lexington, NC | Duke Energy plans affecting our communities and energy infrastructure Stokes County data center hearing | Stokes County Commissioners' Chambers, Ronald Wilson Reagan Memorial Building, 1014 Main St., Danbury, NC 27016 | A proposed agreement among Stokes County, developer ELSDCSP2, LLC, and owners DFC Stokes, LLC and DFC Stokes 2, LLC for data centers and related infrastructure — possibly power generation, substations, gas lines, battery backup, fuel and water storage How you can help Take notes on presentations, questions and public comments Record the names of speakers and officials when possible Take photos or video where permitted Give a public comment if you feel comfortable Send a short summary to the 7DS team afterward so we can make sure both rooms are covered. In Washington: threats to tribal consultation and the Native count The permitting bill (BAAJA) and Section 106. S. 5653, the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026, is now being debated in Congress. Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act requires federal agencies to consult with tribes before approving projects that could affect sacred sites and ancestral lands. Groups like NDN Collective call the bill's changes an unprecedented attack on tribal rights. Critics point to four changes: Optional consultation: government-to-government consultation with Tribal Nations would become optional for many projects. Narrower harm: agencies would no longer weigh indirect, visual, atmospheric or audible impacts unless they directly and significantly damage a site's physical character. Unilateral decisions: agencies could declare "no adverse effect," or that other considerations outweigh preservation, over tribal objections. Rigid deadlines: Tribal Historic Preservation Officers would face 30- to 90-day review windows. If deadlines are missed, even because developers sent incomplete information, funding could be withheld or THPO functions taken over. The 2030 Census proposal. The Census Bureau has proposed removing race and ethnicity questions from the short-form 2030 questionnaire. That would eliminate the American Indian and Alaska Native checkbox and the tribal write-in line. Tribal leaders warn this would cause a systemic undercount, especially of Native people living off reservation, and shrink federal funding, health care allocations, and fair voting districts. The Bureau suggests using administrative records and the American Community Survey instead. The Native American Rights Fund and others argue those sources can't capture self-identification or tribal citizenship. Where the coalition stands. Tribal leaders, the All Pueblo Council of Governors and environmental justice groups are calling on Congress to strip the NHPA amendments from BAAJA and on the Census Bureau to halt its overhaul. They argue real efficiency comes from respecting tribal self-determination and true nation-to-nation consultation. Native American Heritage Month Every November honors the cultures, traditions, histories, and contributions of Indigenous peoples. President George H.W. Bush designated it a month-long observance in 1990. November marks the close of the harvest season, long a time of gathering and celebration for many Native nations. Date | Observance ---|--- Sat, Nov 7 | National Bison Day — the cultural, spiritual and economic bond between Tribal Nations and the bison Wed, Nov 11 | Veterans Day — Native American and Alaska Native veterans, who serve at a higher per-capita rate than any other group Sun, Nov 15 | Rock Your Mocs Day — wear moccasins, boots, or mukluks to celebrate tribal identity Thu, Nov 19 | Red Shawl Day — honoring missing and murdered Indigenous people (MMIP) Fri, Nov 27 | Native American Heritage Day — the day after Thanksgiving, better known as Black Friday National Day of Mourning sunrise ceremony — Thanksgiving morning We are taking a break from Truthsgiving this year. Instead, please join us at sunrise on Thursday, November 26 for a ceremony honoring our ancestors. . Thankstaking: the untold truth. The familiar story celebrates a peaceful three-day feast between English settlers and the Wampanoag in 1621. It leaves out what followed: massacres, grave robbing, and centuries of dispossession. For many Native people, Thanksgiving is not a holiday but a National Day of Mourning — a day to honor ancestors who suffered and resisted colonization. Gather with intention. If you do gather, make room for honesty and reflection alongside gratitude: 1. Open the day by acknowledging the Native peoples whose land you are on. 2. Spend part of the day giving back at a food bank, shelter, or community center. 3. Take a gratitude walk outdoors together. 4. Watch a film or documentary centered on Native history and voices. 5. Offer each guest a journal to record reflections through the day. 6. Before the meal, form a circle and share what you are grateful for. The goal is a gathering that matches your values and tells the truth. Exploring our homelands: thank you, GooseChase teams! This October, families and friends took part in our GooseChase scavenger hunt, exploring the region's Indigenous history, the Haw River, historic sites, and local landscapes. 16 teams registered, 11 took part, and together they logged 102 mission submissions. Congratulations to WatkinsClan for the top point total (2,850) and The Pathfinders for the most submissions (20), with strong showings from Wolf Cubs, Journeying, Baha'i guys, 1Eyed Boyz and Seekers. Missions like Many Rivers and Still Here invited everyone to see how history, stewardship and identity connect. Thank you to every participant, whether you finished one mission or many. The adventure may be over, but our responsibility to the land, water, and one another continues. Native Vote 2026: our voices, our votes, our future The midterms are over, and the turnout was inspiring. Through October, our Native Vote 2026 initiative brought voter education and Get Out the Vote work to Occaneechi, Sappony, Meherrin and other Native communities across Alamance, Orange, Caswell and Chatham counties. Ten outreach activities included registration tables, a Native Candidates Forum and early voting education, aimed at youth, first-time voters, elders and families.A little joy: meet Maverick! Thank you to everyone who helped shuttle neighbors to the polls here in Pleasant Grove. Native civic engagement doesn't begin or end at the ballot box. It means understanding Tribal governance, holding officials accountable, and making sure Indigenous voices shape decisions about our lands, waters and future generations. Thank you, voters The midterms are over, and the turnout was inspiring. Thank you to everyone who helped shuttle neighbors to the polls here in Pleasant Grove. Showing up for each other is what we do. A little joy: meet Maverick! You know we need some baby horses to cheer us up! The votes are in, and my colt has a name: Made To Marvel (barn name Maverick). Between the Facebook poll and 56 SurveyMonkey responses, he won with about 37 combined votes, well ahead of runner-up Marvel's Golden Legacy ("Legend"). Maverick beat Sparky's Shining Doll ("Marvel") and outpaced Texas Jacks, Goldie. His new name carries a piece of his sire while giving him a strong identity of his own. Thank you to everyone who voted and sent suggestions. I can't wait to see what the future holds for this special boy! We need you: volunteer with 7DS Staffing and funding challenges have reduced our capacity, even as the work keeps growing. We are building a structured volunteer program with clear assignments, realistic weekly commitments, and defined deliverables. Even three to five hours a week helps, and much of it can be done from home. We especially need help with: Monitoring public records and tracking environmental permits Pipeline and data center monitoring and environmental research Newsletters, communications, and community outreach Grant research and administrative support Organizing turnout for public hearings and coordinating events Volunteers gain meaningful experience while strengthening an Indigenous-led organization working for environmental justice, cultural preservation, and community protection. ** Your donation makes a direct difference in protecting our communities, land, and water. A gift of $25 helps cover copies of permit documents and public records requests, while $50 provides gas and travel assistance for a community member to testify at a public hearing. A $100 contribution helps us print educational fact sheets and public comment guides for community meetings, and $250 supports independent technical reviews of potential water quality impacts. Donations of $500 or more help sustain a full month of dedicated pipeline and environmental permit monitoring. Every dollar strengthens our ability to hold corporations accountable, protect Indigenous ancestral lands, defend clean water, and ensure community voices are heard. God’s Children Are Not For Sale

Friend,

My name is Eduardo Verástegui.

I produced the film Sound of Freedom, and through Sound of Freedom Foundation, I work alongside partners who rescue children from trafficking and give them a real home.

Sound of Freedom Foundation's partner, House Parent Project, cares for 130 to 150 children every single day.

Right now, they have no functioning sewage system for the home they run.

Food alone costs House Parent Project over $20,000 a month because of inflation.

Building the larger school they need will cost an estimated $60,000, and the reliable vehicles their team needs will cost around $30,000.

Today, a generous donor is matching every gift, dollar for dollar, up to $50,000, to help meet these needs.

Your gift helps House Parent Project provide food, care, medical attention, education, clothing, and a safe, functioning place for children to grow.

body:
It is heartbreaking

It is heartbreaking
| Do you trust your neighbors, Peter?This would've been an easy question for me back when I knew my neighbors and could count on them. I would always see most of my neighbors at church, and there was a collective will among us to do something for our people and community.We used to belong to a community where everyone looked out for each other, and that's what made America great in the first place.It is heartbreaking to tell you that this is all going away.As our communities have been invaded by people from the Third World, we've lost our sense of who we are. They came here and took advantage of us.[How can you trust your neighbors when all they do is take from you while sharing none of your values, heritage, or faith?](https://trk.emails.dailygopnews._SG9RAp2bP9Ws-0drw)This is outrageous, and the fact that the Federal Government knowingly let this happen to your community and our society is beyond shameful.
---
| [STOP THE INVASION](https://trk.emails.dailygopnews.-58ab2RsynCUYYLg)
---
Our country and culture can never be strong unless we bring back trust in our communities.This is the starting point, and we can accept nothing less.[That's why I'm starting the fight in Texas.](https://trk.emails.dailygopnews.-PtbSDBu-Bdoj2QmObg)What we stand for in Texas and our country, cannot be wiped away by the Third World.And the DC Swamp that is enabling this must be destroyed immediately.
---
| [STOP THE DC SWAMP](https://trk.emails.dailygopnews._2r9aOqToZZ8GdiQ)
---
[That is why I am humbly asking for your support today. We have to fight back now, or we LOSE everything. We cannot let this madness continue, and I would be forever grateful if you lend your hand today to fight for our communities.](https://trk.emails.dailygopnews.)Thank you for putting your trust in me, a fellow American. I will never take your support for granted.

God Bless You, and God Bless America,

clean_body: It is heartbreaking It is heartbreaking | Do you trust your neighbors, Peter?This would've been an easy question for me back when I knew my neighbors and could count on them. I would always see most of my neighbors at church, and there was a collective will among us to do something for our people and community.We used to belong to a community where everyone looked out for each other, and that's what made America great in the first place.It is heartbreaking to tell you that this is all going away.As our communities have been invaded by people from the Third World, we've lost our sense of who we are. They came here and took advantage of us. is outrageous, and the fact that the Federal Government knowingly let this happen to your community and our society is beyond shameful. | Our country and culture can never be strong unless we bring back trust in our communities.This is the starting point, and we can accept nothing less. we stand for in Texas and our country, cannot be wiped away by the Third World.And the DC Swamp that is enabling this must be destroyed immediately. | you for putting your trust in me, a fellow American. | [](https://substack.com/redirect/c09038b7-2429-4541-b04e-8f0f0448a809?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Index moves locked:** The Nasdaq Composite lost 1,168.52 points to 24,567.99; the S&P 500 fell 2.8% and the Dow slid 1,153 points, or 2.2%.
* **Tech and chips hit:** Broadcom and Nvidia each dropped about 6%, Qualcomm fell 11% on a weak outlook, and the iShares Semiconductor ETF sank 11% in its worst day since March 2020.
* **Neoclouds and Musk names:** CoreWeave lost 9%, Nebius 13% and Iren 14%; Tesla fell 9% and SpaceX 7%.
* **Midterm driver:** The sell-off followed Democratic wins that raised fears of slower data-center buildouts and a cooler AI capex cycle after the prior session's relief rally.

# [Oil crashes below $90 as Vance blames Iran war for GOP rout](https://substack.com/redirect/c09038b7-2429-4541-b04e-8f0f0448a809?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Crude tumbled more than 8% Wednesday after Vice President JD Vance **[pinned Republican midterm losses on the Iran conflict,](https://substack.com/redirect/cc21bc8c-de1a-4445-bb68-a821140f4edd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** lifting hopes for a faster diplomatic exit and stripping the war-risk premium.

---|---|---
* **Vance pins the loss:** He posted that "the reason we lost is the war" and that "the president himself said so last night."
* **WTI and Brent settle:** WTI fell 8.3% to $88.12 while Brent dropped 8.7% to $94.62, a two-month low.
* **Deal incentive rises:** Lipow Oil's Andy Lipow said the results lead the market to conclude Trump might now be inclined to make a deal.
* **UBS sees a floor:** **[Dominic Ellis noted](https://substack.com/redirect/6800decc-5a2e-490a-bcdd-24240126fa7f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** fundamentals still provide support with another $10-$15 of premium near $95 even as Brent tracks its worst week since COVID.

| | We did it! Because of the time, energy, and trust YOU poured into this campaign, we not only helped ensure a Democratic majority in the House of Representatives — we also hit a record number of voter participation in El Paso. **My heart is bursting with pride and gratitude tonight.** Texas 16 didn't just show up for me. You showed up for Democrats in record numbers to send James Talarico to the U.S. Senate and Gina Hinojosa to the Governor's Mansion. I'm profoundly honored by the trust you've placed in me, and I'm proud to be part of a new Democratic majority, ready to roll up our sleeves and go to battle for all Americans, not just the interests of the ultra-rich and the well-connected. **This is just the beginning.** We've got a lot of work to undo the damage Trump and his former rubber-stamp Congress have done to our communities and the nation. This victory belongs to every volunteer who knocked on doors, every supporter who made a phone call, every young person who voted for the first time, every donor who contributed, and every El Pasoan who believed our voices matter. I am ready to deliver. I'll keep fighting to lower costs, protect Social Security and Medicare, expand access to affordable healthcare, hold the Trump administration accountable, put hardworking Americans above the billionaires, and deliver real results for El Pasoans. **Representing my hometown has been and will continue to be the greatest honor of my life. body:
Peter,
I wanted you to get this update from me: **Ballots are still being counted, and right now, it’s still too close to call.**
We are going to do everything we can to make sure every single vote is counted in this race.
But I’ll be honest: That is going to take time – and plenty of resources that we don’t currently have.
As we fight to make sure every ballot is counted, we’re going to remain the top target of the DC establishment.
We put everything we had into winning this race, so I’m counting on your help to fight back against their attacks.
It looks like we’re in this for the long haul, so I need your help to sustain our fight until every vote is counted.
From the very beginning, this campaign has been powered by grassroots donations from people like you. I’m proud of that fact, but it means it’s going to take lots of us to stand up to their pressure in the coming days.
That’s why I have to ask:
[**If you can afford it today, please pitch in anything you can to my and Small Town PAC's campaign at this critical moment. clean_body: Peter, We face powerful foes today who are willing to do anything to dominate America, even if it means destroying democracy. The Left's so-called principles are utterly incompatible with those that are the bedrock of our constitutional republic. They're incompatible with individual liberty and free will. They're incompatible with the Judeo-Christian belief system under which this nation was founded. At a time when the very values that make America great are under attack, we must continue to stand strong. We must make sure our fellow citizens understand the seriousness of this situation. I'll never stop defending America, our Constitution, our free market economy, and our Judeo-Christian traditions. And I'll never stop calling out the leftists who want to tear our country down. I know you won't either! I do a lot of things. But one of the most important things I do is work with my colleagues at Landmark Legal Foundation. Landmark Legal Foundation is on a mission. They 're here to protect liberty, property rights, constitutionalism . . . in other words, what you read in the Declaration of Independence and the Constitution. And now, I'd love you to stand with me in supporting this outstanding organization. The Left aren't saviors of democracy.They 're Marxists. And what they're doing is destroying the country. They fight desperately to undermine our election processes and, if elections go against them, they use the courts to obstruct the policies We the People voted for. They persecute their opponents, like when the Biden In justice Department waged relentless lawfare against Trump and his allies. Leftists focus so much energy on the justice system - to control it, to contort it, to use it to promote their insanely radical agenda. Again and again, they turn to rogue left-wing judges to usurp the Constitution and undermine America's founding principles. We must not be silent while these leftists destroy our republic from within. That 's why it's so great to have Landmark Legal Foundation take them on! I love these guys. I've been part of the Landmark family for over three decades . . . as president for 20 years, then Chairman of the Board, and now Chairman Emeritus. These briefs present the strongest possible argument for the constitutional position and help convince judges to do the right thing. In 2024, Landmark made a historic winning argument that special prosecutor Jack Smith lacked the legal authority to target Donald Trump in the classified documents probe. The judge in the case echoed Landmark's arguments in her decision and delivered a huge win over the Left 's lawfare. Landmark also fights to defend free, fair elections. For example, Landmark filed a supportive brief in another key election integrity case. With Bost v. Illinois Board of Elections , they're helping challenge unfair vote-by-mail procedures. Here, Illinois Congressman Mike Bost sued the Illinois Board of Elections over their practice of counting mail-in ballots received after Election Day. Such counting delays results and opens the door for abuse. When the Supreme Court agreed, it marked a major victory for free, fair elections. But this is not the last fight! This isn't political . . . it 's about the Constitution! My Landmark friends are on the frontlines of the battle to preserve our country. They're a vital part of the conservative, constitutionalist force fighting for our country today. Your support will help Landmark Legal Foundation live up to its motto of " Defending Liberty, Fighting Tyranny." Thank you in advance for actively joining the fight! | | Peter, Think about where the uncounted votes in Alaska are right now. Some are in mail planes over the tundra. Some are in post offices in villages hundreds of miles from a road. Alaska counts ballots until November 18 because that's how long it takes for every voice in the biggest, most remote state in the country to arrive — including voters in Alaska Native communities that have been part of this land for ten thousand years and part of the electorate for barely a hundred. Those are the ballots still coming. Early reporting says the remaining rural votes are expected to lean toward **Mary Peltola** — the Yup'ik leader who grew up in those communities, who leads this race by **637 votes** , and who is one count away from joining Peggy Flanagan as the second Native woman elected to the U.S. Senate in the same week. So understand what "protect the count" really means here. It means every one of those traveling ballots gets received, verified, and counted — no matter how long the mail takes, no matter who runs out of patience, no matter what the DOJ or Donald Trump says. clean_body: This is razor thin This is razor thin | ~~ | | Peter, Think about where the uncounted votes in Alaska are right now. Some are in mail planes over the tundra. Some are in post offices in villages hundreds of miles from a road. Alaska counts ballots until November 18 because that's how long it takes for every voice in the biggest, most remote state in the country to arrive — including voters in Alaska Native communities that have been part of this land for ten thousand years and part of the electorate for barely a hundred. Those are the ballots still coming. Early reporting says the remaining rural votes are expected to lean toward Mary Peltola — the Yup'ik leader who grew up in those communities, who leads this race by 637 votes , and who is one count away from joining Peggy Flanagan as the second Native woman elected to the U.S. Senate in the same week. So understand what "protect the count" really means here. It means every one of those traveling ballots gets received, verified, and counted — no matter how long the mail takes, no matter who runs out of patience, no matter what the DOJ or Donald Trump says. ~ If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | ~~ With gratitude, Indigenous Women Lead PAC | Paid for by Indigenous Women Lead PAC Indigenous Women Lead PACPO Box 15845Washington, DC 20003United States

| | | | | | Hello Peter,
Thank you. Because of you, we did something many people said couldn’t be done in Ohio’s 8th District.
In 2024, the gap between us and our opponent was more than 25 points. This year, with unofficial results still being finalized, that gap is about 4 points. That happened because of every door you knocked, every call and text you made, every dollar you gave, and every neighbor you brought to the polls.
Now we have one more job: making sure every eligible vote is counted accurately and completely.

Right now, more than 14,233 provisional ballots in our race are waiting to be reviewed. Many belong to voters who simply need to bring a valid ID to their county board of elections **by Saturday, November 7** , or their voice won’t be heard.
Over the coming weeks, county boards of elections will finish counting provisional and absentee ballots, run their official canvass, and certify the results. We are monitoring the count, tracking provisional ballots, and look forward to observing the audit, and documenting anything that doesn’t add up. If we find problems in specific precincts, Ohio law lets us request a recount, but we have to pay a deposit for each precinct up front.
We want to protect the integrity of the process every voter in this district deserves to trust, and making sure the voices of the 8th District are fully heard.
**Will you chip in $25, $50, or $100 today to help us make sure every vote is counted?**

Whatever the final count shows, we’ve built something real together, and I’m more hopeful about this district’s future than I have ever been.

body:
[ stdin# ]Our Revolution Logo

Peter Willis,

Together, we just helped deliver a progressive political earthquake.
Working people, grassroots organizers, and unapologetic progressive
candidates took on MAGA and its billionaire money — and won BIG.

Now Democrats will hold majorities in the House and Senate. But winning
power is only the beginning. The question is what Democrats will do with
our mandate — and whether they’ll finally deliver for the people who
elected them.

Our Revolution’s grassroots organizing helped win this progressive
victory. We fought to elect candidates who will confront the Trump
regime’s corruption, take on corporate power, and tackle the affordability
crisis. Now it’s time for us to make sure that WE - the grassroots - have
a real say in what comes next.

What should the Democratic majority deliver? We want to hear from you.
Take our short midterm survey and help shape the agenda for the fights
ahead.

Here’s the first question: [ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39999?source=email-20261105&t=1011&akid=11557%2E5885482%2E8oS3yy ]Progressives powered the Blue Wave. What
should Democrats tackle as their top 3 priorities now that they control
Congress?

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/39999?source=email-20261105&t=1019&akid=11557%2E5885482%2E8oS3yy ]Rein in ICE

and purple states and districts. We finally took out Susan Collins with
working-class champion Troy Jackson. We elected Abdul El-Sayed in a swing

power down ballot in Texas, Pennsylvania, and beyond.

The grassroots made these victories possible. Now the grassroots must help
set the direction, and show our majorities in the House and the Senate
that they have the responsibility to deliver. But they need to hear from
all of us about what comes first.

Let's make sure they do.

clean_body: Fellow Patriot, We face powerful foes today who are willing to do anything to dominate America, even if it means destroying democracy. The Left's so-called principles are utterly incompatible with those that are the bedrock of our constitutional republic. They're incompatible with individual liberty and free will. They're incompatible with the Judeo-Christian belief system under which this nation was founded. At a time when the very values that make America great are under attack, we must continue to stand strong. We must make sure our fellow citizens understand the seriousness of this situation. I'll never stop defending America, our Constitution, our free market economy, and our Judeo-Christian traditions. And I'll never stop calling out the leftists who want to tear our country down. I know you won't either! I do a lot of things. But one of the most important things I do is work with my colleagues at Landmark Legal Foundation. Landmark Legal Foundation is on a mission. They 're here to protect liberty, property rights, constitutionalism . . . in other words, what you read in the Declaration of Independence and the Constitution. And now, I'd love you to stand with me in supporting this outstanding organization. The Left aren't saviors of democracy.They 're Marxists. And what they're doing is destroying the country. They fight desperately to undermine our election processes and, if elections go against them, they use the courts to obstruct the policies We the People voted for. They persecute their opponents, like when the Biden In justice Department waged relentless lawfare against Trump and his allies. Leftists focus so much energy on the justice system - to control it, to contort it, to use it to promote their insanely radical agenda. Again and again, they turn to rogue left-wing judges to usurp the Constitution and undermine America's founding principles. We must not be silent while these leftists destroy our republic from within. That 's why it's so great to have Landmark Legal Foundation take them on! I love these guys. I've been part of the Landmark family for over three decades . . . as president for 20 years, then Chairman of the Board, and now Chairman Emeritus. These briefs present the strongest possible argument for the constitutional position and help convince judges to do the right thing. In 2024, Landmark made a historic winning argument that special prosecutor Jack Smith lacked the legal authority to target Donald Trump in the classified documents probe. The judge in the case echoed Landmark's arguments in her decision and delivered a huge win over the Left 's lawfare. Landmark also fights to defend free, fair elections. For example, Landmark filed a supportive brief in another key election integrity case. With Bost v. Illinois Board of Elections , they're helping challenge unfair vote-by-mail procedures. Here, Illinois Congressman Mike Bost sued the Illinois Board of Elections over their practice of counting mail-in ballots received after Election Day. Such counting delays results and opens the door for abuse. When the Supreme Court agreed, it marked a major victory for free, fair elections. But this is not the last fight! This isn't political . . . it 's about the Constitution! My Landmark friends are on the frontlines of the battle to preserve our country. They're a vital part of the conservative, constitutionalist force fighting for our country today. Your support will help Landmark Legal Foundation live up to its motto of " Defending Liberty, Fighting Tyranny." Thank you in advance for actively joining the fight! God Bless, Mark Levin Chairman Emeritus Landmark Legal Foundation Landmark Legal Foundation is a 501(c)(3) Not For Profit Organization. All donations are tax-deductible.

## Thank You
---
Dear Friends,

As this campaign comes to a close, I want to say two simple words: **Thank you.
**
Thank you for believing and standing beside me, and giving so generously of your time, talents, and resources. Whether you knocked on doors, made calls, wrote a postcard, shared your stories, put up a sign, attended a community event, contributed, or cast your vote, please know how much your support has meant to Jacelyn and me.

While the election results were not what we had hoped for, I leave this campaign with a renewed sense of hope and gratitude. Traveling across Minnesota, meeting so many wonderful people, and hearing your stories reminded me of what makes our state so special.

**An election is just one moment in time. The friendships we've made, the values we share, and our hope for a brighter future will endure.
**
I believe with all my heart that Minnesota's best days are still ahead. As long as good people continue to care, get involved, and believe in one another, there is every reason to be optimistic.

Jacelyn and I are deeply grateful for your friendship, prayers, encouragement, and kindness throughout this journey.

**The future is still full of promise. And Minnesota will always be worth believing in.
**
With heartfelt gratitude,
**Tad and Jacelyn Jude**

PO Box 1881, Maple Grove, MN 55311

Team –

I wanted you to get this update from me: **Ballots are still being counted, and right now, it’s still too close to call.**

We are going to do everything we can to make sure every single vote is counted in this race.

But I’ll be honest: That is going to take time – and plenty of resources that we don’t currently have.

As we fight to make sure every ballot is counted, we’re going to remain the top target of the DC establishment.

We put everything we had into winning this race, so I’m counting on your help to fight back against their attacks.

It looks like we’re in this for the long haul, so I need your help to sustain our fight until every vote is counted.

From the very beginning, this campaign has been powered by grassroots donations from people like you. I’m proud of that fact, but it means it’s going to take lots of us to stand up to their pressure in the coming days.

_You're getting this message because you’ve supported good causes and Democratic candidates. We need your support to continue fighting for our democracy. We love having you in our network, but if you only want our most important email updates,[click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/108?t=2&akid=3950%2E259176%2E6uG5SI) If you'd like to unsubscribe, [click here.](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/109?t=3&akid=3950%2E259176%2E6uG5SI)_

[](https://act.blueampaction.com/go/19788?source=SL_EM_FR_2026.11.05_Nez-Recount-1_B2_F1_S1_C1_180AC-360DON&t=4&akid=3950%2E259176%2E6uG5SI) Yá'át'ééh (Hello) Peter,

Thanks to your incredible grassroots support, I woke up the day after the election to a small lead! Across AZ-02, ballots are still being counted, and if we prevail I will make history as the first Native American ever elected to Congress from Arizona.

With this race being neck-and-neck, winning could be determined by “cured” ballots — ballots that have some error or mistake and must be corrected to count. **Statement from Congresswoman-elect Kristina Knickerbocker on Historic Win in OH-10**
---
| | **DAYTON, OHIO** — Congresswoman-elect Kristina Knickerbocker released the following statement:
"I’m humbled and motivated that OH-10 has put their trust in me to serve as their first Congresswoman. I never imagined this is where life would lead me but my kids, my military service and my patients taught me how resilience often results when you are tasked with the unimaginable. While many thought this would be impossible, the work is just beginning. I promise to be the patriot and servant leader our community needs to get costs down, fight for better healthcare, and serve the people of OH-10!"_###_
