subject: thank you, Hampton Roads
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Elaine Luria for Congress
body:
---
| | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142971788/658657752/-373287770?refcode=EM_BS_LUR_261105_FR_ThankYouVictory_A0_na_U1_X1_M1&amount=15&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MDA3OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5OWFjMjhhYi01N2Q5LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=FOJ7XsQIzydaQmdnRzotFxalYfBBqgmB7qRthwaGarg=) Four years ago, after MAGA spent $6 million attacking me, I lost re-election in Virginia’s 2nd Congressional District. I could have walked away from public service. Plenty of people would have understood. But I was raised to believe that the worst outcome isn’t losing the fight; it’s going down with no fight at all. I swore an oath at 17 when I walked into the Naval Academy, and again every time I took my seat in Congress. Losing an election didn’t release me from it. I looked at the country my daughter is going to inherit. I looked at Hampton Roads families working harder every year just to stay afloat. And I decided I didn’t spend the better part of two decades on combatant ships to watch the storm roll in from the pier. So I got back on deck. **We put up one hell of a fight, and it paid off. The people of Hampton Roads voted to send me back to Congress.** This win belongs to every donor, volunteer, staffer, and voter who refused to give up on this district. You knocked doors in the rain, made calls after long workdays, and chipped in when it would have been easier to sit this one out. That’s what carried us across the finish line. We didn’t get here easily. MAGA poured more than $8 million into this race to keep VA-02 under Republican control. We were outspent and underestimated. We didn’t do it alone. Democrats needed to flip three seats to take back the House. We exceeded that by a mile, and VA-02 is part of the reason why. For the first time in two years, there will be a serious check on the most corrupt administration in American history. Thanks to your support, we now have the power to defend our Constitution and our core American values. There’s a lot of work ahead. We need to make healthcare affordable, lower costs for families, combat corruption at the highest levels, do right by our men and women in uniform, and protect Medicare and Social Security. I’ll keep fighting for the things that matter most right here at home, from the Chesapeake Bay to the military families who call Hampton Roads home. I’ll work every single day to earn the trust you’ve placed in me. You’ll hear from me again soon. With gratitude,
Congresswoman-elect Elaine Luria P.S. My campaign invested every last penny we had (and then some) to win this fight. Now, I need to make sure every bill is paid and every obligation is met. **[Will you chip in $15 today before we officially close out this campaign?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142971789/658657753/-373287770?refcode=EM_BS_LUR_261105_FR_ThankYouVictory_A0_na_U1_X1_M1&amount=15&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MDA3OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5OWFjMjhhYi01N2Q5LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=FOJ7XsQIzydaQmdnRzotFxalYfBBqgmB7qRthwaGarg=)** | | | [Contribute](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142971790/658657754/-373287770?refcode=EM_BS_LUR_261105_FR_ThankYouVictory_A0_na_U1_X1_M1&amount=15&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MDA3OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI5OWFjMjhhYi01N2Q5LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=FOJ7XsQIzydaQmdnRzotFxalYfBBqgmB7qRthwaGarg=)

I’ll work every single day to earn the trust you’ve placed in me. You’ll hear from me again soon. With gratitude, Congresswoman-elect Elaine Luria P.S. Team, From the bottom of my heart, I want to thank the people of New Jersey's 9th District for the trust they have placed in me. I am grateful for your vote of confidence. Serving our 35 communities is an extraordinary honor and sacred responsibility to every resident. Over these past two years, across countless conversations, our neighbors have shared with me their hopes, challenges, and frustrations. Over and over, our residents are outraged at how little has been done and demand urgency to address the host of problems facing our country. I share their urgency. Let’s win this,

name: James O'Keefe
subject: I investigated Minnesota. Now they're prosecuting ME
body:
These charges are nothing more than an attempt to criminalize investigative journalism and intimidate anyone who dares to expose wrongdoing.
| | | | Fellow Patriot, **[I was just charged with TWO FELONIES for my undercover journalism in Minnesota.](http://links.justandfreegop.com/u/click?_t=8ca5ef3d31cc43bcb1fbe6968d953911&_m=67bff83c58b44b6891dacd1c78e4317f&_e=bTeuAIYcRSVGG_qnW8qxTLb62XnzBhxudUjq80l-HgIia7gnJzCAniayrk2-TrEavqP5ivsR1sowUV2g6F-LVf2bu9z4TqLXIKCCtGFbeLDPi4aKw_gBD7Y9LzXoVxP8SZTzIOKj9ZasELBWyachFBmSDDU5AC5npzJLC85HOeWMmaH08dqe3Nn1dXulrS-SUdrSLQWA54FfU0YPOUm3dEGkjcAFr_vQVN2IP-sNz7aE_w4do-ZLilmv6ZVyrfTQ7LJdB6zHJw3C2f2u8ph3ogN2QakEz0GpNF9Sn2fEABumZJuOtnADAgJm-e8WbNIF2Nk-L0uC0pRCykVlz6DO0BSD8IoPg2s__QojWtz2zS7tTJjQ1la1pD1OV4vicOV03OHaVKFZzIt-EhQu3lzDwaeDNM95q3_MvQ9iNQmGxYT8ili9ZWn4cAttb0jk3Y1Pcq9UUvVWr5HK7R-2n1gIk8vCc9Jkz7tSS15VmsWlFCrni7s1GkqQg5exrNGCs_JOIMF8OpauNxIGmjOhAlsnNCtSu4vYdeuZ6a77qJqHzzDtum2O5I81_O2tA5UFtc136-FDi35nvKyN2nKkb87Z0i09iFAaQjgpD9haoVXQRV5AJENUE21aoxCiqErKWPc4U35tLXiKZUWnXIYj_6Ey10apgVLOlWuscMKKEfJ3ZmLw6il28ub-cQX4vRgVM_E9EFRaCoKXTQBtVucJOQKPL8ojbyWUOAInISARJA13csjAWobjsK4NqSzaMOXAAXVFQumrT3gkdS0u16Z_gloHHdmx3j9ZBcvOqUkyp-W7HrivSutEG1LiQdVQFqAflRqp9S2gYBOSYDXLQHR3QhyFQscU8mhkbiqpDVfFz0qTcBBkAvf-K-u5nrY_w0zZK6F7)** **Back in August, we published a********bombshell investigative report on voter vouching laws****.****We never cast a ballot. We never signed a voter oath.****Yet now, fellow journalist Cam Higby and I are facing felony charges and possible JAIL TIME.** Even the county prosecutor acknowledged that we never intended to vote.**These charges are nothing more than an attempt to criminalize investigative journalism and intimidate anyone who dares to expose wrongdoing.** But I refuse to back down. Hey friends,I’m still in my robe, running on no sleep, and I can’t wait to talk to you about what Tennessee just did and what comes next!
[**[CLICK HERE to LISTEN NOW**]](https://us.list-manage.com/xvl_KAqAI4M?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0)
****
[**Listen or watch**](https://us.list-manage.com/I3l38owqw1U?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0)**now wherever you get your podcasts. 🎧**

When the first early vote numbers dropped in Knox County and I saw the early vote totals for Michaela Barnett, I started crying, because I knew we were seeing something Tennessee hadn't seen before. This week it's just me, walking you through election night: the close calls, the flips, and what the folks who ran as unapologetic progressives showed us about how to win.
I also talk about the [State House pickups](https://us.list-manage.com/ISpN1bwM9g_?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0), Knoxville candidates who moved their districts by double digits, why Tennessee doesn't get the national investment Texas and Georgia do, and what we have to demand from the new majorities in Washington: bold leadership, accountability and real help with affordability. Plus the story of the sweetest, most polite postcard that sent Tim Burchett into a tailspin.
We did not win everything. But when we vote, we win, and I'm not done thanking every one of you who knocked a door, made a call and showed up.

Thank you for being here,
Gloria

clean_body: Peter, We face powerful foes today who are willing to do anything to dominate America, even if it means destroying democracy. The Left's so-called principles are utterly incompatible with those that are the bedrock of our constitutional republic. They're incompatible with individual liberty and free will. They're incompatible with the Judeo-Christian belief system under which this nation was founded. At a time when the very values that make America great are under attack, we must continue to stand strong. We must make sure our fellow citizens understand the seriousness of this situation. I'll never stop defending America, our Constitution, our free market economy, and our Judeo-Christian traditions. And I'll never stop calling out the leftists who want to tear our country down. I know you won't either! I do a lot of things. But one of the most important things I do is work with my colleagues at Landmark Legal Foundation. Landmark Legal Foundation is on a mission. They 're here to protect liberty, property rights, constitutionalism . . . in other words, what you read in the Declaration of Independence and the Constitution. And now, I'd love you to stand with me in supporting this outstanding organization. The Left aren't saviors of democracy.They 're Marxists. And what they're doing is destroying the country. They fight desperately to undermine our election processes and, if elections go against them, they use the courts to obstruct the policies We the People voted for. They persecute their opponents, like when the Biden In justice Department waged relentless lawfare against Trump and his allies. Leftists focus so much energy on the justice system - to control it, to contort it, to use it to promote their insanely radical agenda. Again and again, they turn to rogue left-wing judges to usurp the Constitution and undermine America's founding principles. We must not be silent while these leftists destroy our republic from within. That 's why it's so great to have Landmark Legal Foundation take them on! I love these guys. I've been part of the Landmark family for over three decades . . . as president for 20 years, then Chairman of the Board, and now Chairman Emeritus. These briefs present the strongest possible argument for the constitutional position and help convince judges to do the right thing. In 2024, Landmark made a historic winning argument that special prosecutor Jack Smith lacked the legal authority to target Donald Trump in the classified documents probe. The judge in the case echoed Landmark's arguments in her decision and delivered a huge win over the Left 's lawfare. Landmark also fights to defend free, fair elections. For example, Landmark filed a supportive brief in another key election integrity case. With Bost v. Illinois Board of Elections , they're helping challenge unfair vote-by-mail procedures. Here, Illinois Congressman Mike Bost sued the Illinois Board of Elections over their practice of counting mail-in ballots received after Election Day. Such counting delays results and opens the door for abuse. When the Supreme Court agreed, it marked a major victory for free, fair elections. But this is not the last fight! This isn't political . . . it 's about the Constitution! My Landmark friends are on the frontlines of the battle to preserve our country. They're a vital part of the conservative, constitutionalist force fighting for our country today. Your support will help Landmark Legal Foundation live up to its motto of " Defending Liberty, Fighting Tyranny." Thank you in advance for actively joining the fight! In early October 2026, screenshots went viral of North Carolina arrest records showing defendants who are unmistakably Black entered into the system as "White" -- some entries reportedly reading "White African" or "White Caucasian," as if the database itself were embarrassed and hedging. A viral analysis counted hundreds of mislabeled racial identities in NC booking and arrest records. The state hasn't rebutted a single one. It doesn't need to, because North Carolina has already confessed -- in its own paperwork.
Here's the part nobody disputes. In 2019, the Urban Institute surveyed every state's criminal-justice data and found that 40 states record a race at arrest, but only 15 record ethnicity. North Carolina is one of the fifteen that does not. Elon University's campus paper flagged it that same May: NC simply doesn't collect whether an arrestee is Hispanic. That means every mestizo arrestee from Sinaloa to Sanford gets funneled into whatever race box the arresting officer feels like checking -- and officers, as the Safety and Justice Challenge bluntly documents, don't ask people how they identify. They eyeball. Light-skinned reads as White; darker reads as Black. Guesswork, digitized...

North Carolina's booking sheets can't get race right -- and someone built a narrative on top of them. | | | Nov 5| | | ∙| | Preview ---|---|--- | | | | | | | | | | | | In early October 2026, screenshots went viral of North Carolina arrest records showing defendants who are unmistakably Black entered into the system as "White" -- some entries reportedly reading "White African" or "White Caucasian," as if the database itself were embarrassed and hedging. A viral analysis counted hundreds of mislabeled racial identities in NC booking and arrest records. The state hasn't rebutted a single one. It doesn't need to, because North Carolina has already confessed -- in its own paperwork. Here's the part nobody disputes. In 2019, the Urban Institute surveyed every state's criminal-justice data and found that 40 states record a race at arrest, but only 15 record ethnicity. North Carolina is one of the fifteen that does not. Elon University's campus paper flagged it that same May: NC simply doesn't collect whether an arrestee is Hispanic. That means every mestizo arrestee from Sinaloa to Sanford gets funneled into whatever race box the arresting officer feels like checking -- and officers, as the Safety and Justice Challenge bluntly documents, don't ask people how they identify. | | Friend, Ten years ago, I woke up the morning after Election Day 2016 and made a promise to myself that I would never again wake up the morning after an election wishing that I had done more. Ten years later, we’re waking up to a blue wave because of your steadfast grit and effort. **Thanks to your hard work, late-night phone banking, door knocking, and unwavering support, we built a blue wave that will restore a Democratic House and Senate majority when the 120th Congress convenes on January 3rd, 2027.** We also made meaningful strides at the local level, electing Democrats up and down the ballot here in Maryland's Third District. I am deeply humbled to serve as your voice in Congress, and I can’t wait to build on the work we started with a Democratic majority. This election was never about partisan showboating or soundbites: voters across the country made it clear last night that they want a Congress that works, listens, and puts people first. With a Democratic majority, we have a clear path forward to deliver on the priorities that matter most to our community. We now have the gavels, subpoena powers, and tools to place a meaningful check on the reckless abuses of this Administration. I am ready to hit the ground running to hold the Trump Administration accountable, reassert our Article I authority, restore meaningful oversight, and protect our democratic institutions. At the same time, we must continue to deliver for Marylanders. That means cutting through the noise to lower costs, from groceries to medical bills and prescription drug costs. It means protecting affordable, quality health care, standing up for our federal workers, and protecting the Chesapeake Bay. Thank you for your trust, your partnership, and your commitment to moving our community forward. The work continues. Sincerely, **Sarah Elfreth**

Congresswoman Sarah Elfreth broke barriers in 2024, becoming the youngest woman ever elected to Congress from Maryland. She went to Congress with one thing in mind: delivering for Maryland families on the issues that matter most. Whether it's standing up for federal workers, supporting veterans, protecting the Chesapeake Bay, or tackling the affordability crisis head-on, Sarah is on the front lines, fighting for what is right. And Sarah has delivered on her promises. She has spent her first year in the House advocating for the Third District, successfully passing five bills into law, solving over 1,000 constituent cases, and bringing tens of millions in funding back to her community. She learned her work ethic and tenacity from growing up in a union household and honed her skills of problem-solving and collaborating over six years in the Maryland State Senate. Sarah lives in Annapolis with her husband, Eric, and their dog, Ollie. Residents in Taiz city crowding around a bakery to buy bread, as families now prefer store-bought bread to preserve their remaining household cooking gas which is in short supply. October 19, 2026. Photo by Khalid Al-Banna for Drop Site News.
TAIZ CITY, Yemen--Hana Bagash never imagined that, one day, she would have to flee Taiz, the city in southwestern Yemen where she was born and raised. But in early October, as fighting intensified around the city between Saudi-backed government forces and Ansarallah, the 40-year-old mother of four decided it was no longer safe for herself and her children and decided to flee. "On October 2, I coordinated with my sister in the town of Al-Turbah, who rented a house for us. I took my children and fled the city," Bagash told Drop Site News. Her husband is currently working in Djibouti, so she had to make the move alone.
Al-Turbah, located in Taiz governorate some 70 kilometers south of Taiz city, was safe when she arrived. Just two days later, Ansarallah (also known as the Houthis) took control of the town following the withdrawal of government forces. The transition was peaceful, she said, and the area, at first, remained safe for Bagash's family.
"There was no fighting in Turbah, but airstrikes began hitting the town. One fell very close to our house, terrifying all of us," she recalled, referring to bombing by the Saudi-led coalition. "We felt as if we were in the middle of a battle."
On October 12, Bagash decided to return to Taiz city, but she heard there were clashes on the main road back. The next day, she took her children and fled to Al-Nagesha, her ancestral village, four kilometers from Turbah. While the village was safe, it is remote, with no running water, electricity, or internet.
"Life wasn't good in the village, but it was our only choice," she added. Less than two weeks later, on October 27, fighting reached Al-Nagesha, trapping Bagash and her family in the crossfire.
"After two days, we barely managed to escape back to Turbah. My children were terrified and are now suffering from psychological trauma from what they endured in the village," she explained. "It was horrifying to suddenly find ourselves trapped in the middle of active fighting."
The main road linking Taiz city with the southern and western parts of the governorate was still open. A bus driver who traverses the route between Turbah and Taiz city told Bagash the road was safe. On November 1, she rode with him and returned to her home in the city, filled with regret for ever leaving.
"I regret fleeing the city. If I had stayed, we wouldn't have suffered through the trauma of displacement," she added. "I am not the only one; I know others who fled and have since returned, deeply regretting their decision."
## "Taiz city is still safer"
Ansarallah forces have seized control of vast areas across Taiz governorate and surround Taiz city from all directions, but active ground combat has not reached the city center itself. Taiz city suffers from shortages of fuel, food, water, medicine, and cooking gas, along with skyrocketing prices for basic items as a result of a siege that the UN and rights groups primarily blame Ansarallah for. However, much like the rest of Taiz governorate, the city remains relatively safe from direct battles compared to surrounding areas.
Conversely, fierce combat continues between Ansarallah forces, which are backed by Iran, and troops of the internationally recognized government (IRG), backed by Saudi Arabia, along the border of Lahj and Taiz governorates; the Houthis launched an advance towards Lahj last week to push the frontline further into government territory. Bagash's village lies directly between Taiz and Lahj, so her family witnessed some of the heaviest fighting.
In the rural areas of Taiz governorate controlled by Ansarallah, civilians are faced with the ever present threat of Saudi-led airstrikes. Civilians have been killed in the attacks, and while the number is disputed, many people nevertheless live in constant fear of the bombardment.
Over the past ten days, the clashes along the road have subsided, according to bus and truck drivers with knowledge of the route, and it has remained safe to leave or enter Taiz city, even with the siege and with rising food and fuel prices. Although schools and most public institutions are closed, there has not been a wave of displacement out of the city.
"No place is completely safe in Taiz governorate," Haitham Shamsan, 39, a resident of Taiz city, told Drop Site. "The clashes are surrounding Taiz city, but they haven't reached it yet. If we flee to another area in Taiz governorate, we might face an even worse situation with airstrikes and shifting battlefronts."
Shamsan works as a procurement officer for a company in Taiz. He believes that if he or any other employee flees, they risk losing their jobs, which would make survival even harder given how difficult it is to find work.
"For now, I still have a source of income, and the fighting is far enough away. But if the company closes and the battles reach the city, we will definitely flee. Right now, I believe Taiz city is still safer than some other areas in the governorate," Shamsan said.
He also referenced the experience of families like Bagash's, who fled the city only to end up trapped in the middle of heavy fighting before ultimately returning. He believes people should stay in their homes unless combat directly enters the city.
But some residents without employment have fled to other governorates, such as Aden, both out of fear the fighting may eventually enter the city and to allow their children to continue their education as schools in Taiz remain closed.
"Fleeing Taiz city for another governorate is a good decision, but most residents simply don't have the money. A family of four needs at least $2,000 to move," Shamsan added.
Ali Qaed, manager of the Executive Unit for Displaced Persons, an official government body, in Taiz governorate, confirmed that "only a negligible few have left the city, and most of them displaced to Aden and Lahj governorates."
He added, "At the same time, more than 50,000 people have reached the city during the last two months because they consider it safer than their home areas."

Mahyoub Ahmed, a farmer in his fifties from Jabal Habashi district, 40 kilometers (25 miles) south of Taiz city, usually only visits the city to seek medical healthcare or attend family celebrations.
In early October, however, his village was turned into a conflict zone between Ansarallah and government forces, trapping him and dozens of other families for four days.
"The worst part was that there was no communication network, so we couldn't call anyone to find out what was happening around us," Ahmed told Drop Site. "We were lost for four days in the middle of the fighting."

As soon as the clashes quieted down, Ahmed and dozens of other families hired cars, gathered their belongings, and fled to Taiz city. However, despite having contacts there, finding decent shelter in Taiz city proved difficult. With home rents far out of reach for a farmer who could barely afford transportation, Ahmed now lives with his wife and six children in a single room inside the basement of an unfinished building.
"Life here isn't easy because we lack basic services, but it is safe," he added. "Some relatives and generous people help us with food, and that is enough for now, safety is all I care about."
Although Ahmed's village is now fully under Ansarallah control and active clashes have ceased, he remains fearful of recurring airstrikes in the area. He has decided to stay in the city until his home village is completely safe.
Taiz is Yemen's third-largest city. Sources estimate its population at between 600,000 and 900,000, though this figure has been reshaped by the recent wave of displacement.
According to new figures from the International Organization for Migration, more than 300,000 people have been forced to flee their homes amid escalating fighting in western Yemen, almost all within the past two months.
Most displaced families arriving to Taiz city are being hosted by relatives, Qaed said, as they cannot afford to rent homes amid skyrocketing housing demand and soaring prices.
"Sometimes we see one family hosting five families of relatives who arrived in the city, and all of them are vulnerable," he added, noting that other displaced families are living in unfinished buildings lacking all basic services.
Qaed emphasized that the need in Taiz city is massive, noting that while some cash assistance is provided by humanitarian organizations, "it is nothing compared to the overwhelming demand."

subject: Eternally grateful, as the fight continues.
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY TOM PERRIELLO FOR CONGRESS
body:
| | | |
---
| | |
---
Dear Friends, I do not have the words to express the depth of my gratitude for what we have built together and how we have shattered the sense of what is possible in our politics today. In a district that McGuire won by 15 points just two years ago, we forced this race into overtime, pushed every single one of our 24 localities in our direction, reached historic levels of African-American support, had UVA students break Presidential-year voting levels, and even surpassed Gov. Spanberger’s performance by at least five points. With thousands of absentee and provisional ballots left to count, we believe the margin will continue to shrink, likely to below 1%. However, we no longer see a path to changing the outcome. We fully support our amazing election officials and bipartisan volunteers making sure that every legitimate ballot gets counted before Tuesday’s deadline, but we are almost certain to fall just shy of pulling off this miraculous upset. Together, we have built something powerful that will outlast this campaign – a coalition of farmers and nurses, veterans and doctors, seniors and students, all determined to replace a politics of extreme polarization with a promise of a new American dream that leaves no region, race, or generation behind. We have made historic gains in rural counties, and broken records for African-American and student turnout. We have built a grassroots team of incredible volunteers, many of whom I hope will be inspired to run for local and state office in 2027. We proved that every precinct and every part of Virginia is worth listening to, fighting for, and being in coalition with. I am humbled and forever grateful for those who voted, volunteered, and supported this campaign. I am grateful to the over 200 local doctors and nurses – from Chatham to Charlottesville, and Goochland to Halifax – who stepped beyond their comfort zone and into the political arena to fight for their patients to be protected from HR1. I appreciate the current and former Republicans who caught hell from friends to do what was right for our community and our country. I appreciate the young people who not only took time to vote but to make sure their classmates turned out. And I appreciate all of you who provided the time, talent, and treasure that fueled this campaign when the pundits and professionals said it was impossible. Tonight we finish one episode and click immediately on the next. I was fighting for universal healthcare, higher wages, and ending corruption long before this campaign began, and we will be fighting for all that and more long after the last vote is counted. We are seeing a new generation of politics replace what was broken in the old. I am profoundly saddened to miss the chance to represent and deliver for the people of Virginia’s Fifth from Congress. But I know that what we are building together is bigger than any one election cycle or seat. Tomorrow, the fight for a more perfect union continues. Tonight, I just say thank you, from the depths of my soul, for all you did to make this possible. Forever grateful,Tom

**1\. The claim, and the poll that tripped it**
"There is nothing more powerful than a Trump endorsement... And obviously, it's certainly his prerogative." Alabama Senator Katie Britt downplaying a poll she should have been bragging about.
**The poll** : The Alabama Poll, re-established by Michael T. Lowry -- pollster, founder/principal, ex-chief of staff to Rep. Robert Aderholt. His February 1-4, 2026 survey of Alabama Republicans tested whether Trump's endorsements actually move his state's voters. Findings, as reported by Alabama Daily News, 1819 News and al.com:
\- President Trump had endorsed Rep. Barry Moore in the open Senate seat (Tuberville's, vacant for his governor run) and former ALGOP chairman John Wahl for lieutenant governor. Both trailed anyway -- AG Steve Marshall led Moore 26%-17%; Sec. of State Wes Allen led Wahl.
\- Trump's endorsement was a net negative: 15-16% of Republican voters said it made them _less_ likely to back a candidate. Only 11% said that of a Britt endorsement...

Voters just
rejected Senate Republicans. In January, they lose their majority.

So what are they doing with the time they have left? Racing to put Trump’s
loyalists on the federal bench for life.

Here’s why. Under Senate rules, any nomination still pending when this
Congress ends goes back to the White House. The nominee starts over: new
hearings, new committee vote, new floor vote. And soon, Republicans won’t
control the process.

So they’re using the lame-duck session, the last few weeks before a new
Congress is sworn in, to jam through as many of Trump’s picks as they can.
Voters took away their power at the ballot box. Now they want to lock it
in on the courts for generations.

The Senate has already confirmed 56 of Trump’s handpicked crony judges.
Each will spend decades ruling on our fundamental rights, and on whether
anyone can check his abuses of power.

We have one message for every Democrat in the Senate: no votes for Trump’s
judges.

No unanimous consent deals to speed things along. No shortcuts. Nothing

###### A "Reader" in cigar factory, Tampa, Fla. He reads books and newspapers at top of his voice all day long.
This is all the education many of these workers receive. He is paid by them and they select what he shall read. Location: Tampa, Florida.

Photograph by Lewis Wickes Hine, January 1909.
National Child Labor Committee Collection, Library of Congress.

I walk the city streets just before sunrise, and the fog has not lifted yet.
On the porch of a Tampa bungalow, a man cups his hands around a lighter and gets his cigar going. He draws, lets the smoke go, draws again. Work boots, a jacket that has seen a few winters. Campaign signs line the curb in front of his house. He does not look at them. He has seen them before. He will see them again.
That is Tampa. Before the stadiums and the high-rises, before anyone called this place a market, it was a city of cigar makers. Cubans, Spaniards and Italians came to Ybor City and rolled tobacco by hand, ten hours at the bench. They paid a lector out of their own wages to sit up on a platform and read to them: the newspaper, the labor papers, Cervantes, Dumas. They made something with their hands and educated themselves while they did it. When the bosses pushed too far, they organized and struck. Sometimes they won. Often, they lost. Either way, they were back at the bench the next morning.
Watch a roller work and you will see how it is done. The filler goes in first: a handful of leaves, no two alike. One grew at the top of the plant, thick and strong from the sun. Another came from down low, thin and mild, there to keep the burn even. Some came from one field, some from a farm across the water. Torn, folded, uneven, every one of them is different. Rolled together, they become one thing.
Then the binder pulls them tight and last comes the wrapper. It is one whole leaf, unbroken, laid around all of it so the different pieces become a single cigar you can hold in your hand.
That is Tampa, too. Every one a leaf from a different field. Cuban, Italian, Spanish, Black, Puerto Rican, Vietnamese, old Florida families, the farmer out in Plant City and the kid who moved down from the Bronx so many seasons ago. And the leaf that wraps around all of us and holds it together is America.
Candidates come and go. The people keep working.
And we keep walking.
I Voted stickers are stuck to the wet concrete, little red, white and blue badges of honor already turning to trash. Pamphlets have gone soft in the gutter. Somebody spent money printing those. Somebody spent a Saturday handing them out, and somebody else took one just to be polite.
The signs are still up, some of them left over from the primary.
I know a few of those names.
One of them used to be mine.
I wonder how long they will stay. Eventually somebody pulls them up, stacks them in a garage, and saves them for the next cycle. The losers wonder where they fit next time. The winners decide that however they ran, it was the right way, and they will run it the same way again. Nobody learns much the morning after. Everybody is too busy being right or being tired.
Campaign signs are like Christmas lights. They go up full of excitement and promise, and they come down long after anyone is looking.
For months the whole city got told that everything depended on this one day. Every mailer, every ad, every knock on the door said this was the most important election of our lives. Maybe it was. But the man with the cigar got up this morning the same way he did yesterday. The bakery on the corner has its lights on. A delivery truck is idling with its flashers going. Nobody here is waiting on Washington or Tallahassee to tell them it is time to start the day.
That is not apathy. It is strength. The engine of a place is not just the ballot. It is the bench. It is the people who show up, do the work, and do not need a sign to prove they belong here.
Not everybody has the time, the means, or the opportunity to do more. Some people have a family to feed, a shift to work, a business to keep open. They may never knock on a campaign door, sit through a county commission meeting, or put their name on a ballot. That does not make their contribution any less important. Getting up, doing an honest day's work, taking care of their families, and being part of the community is its own kind of civic responsibility.
The ballot matters. So does the bench. One gives people a voice in who governs them. The other reminds us who keeps this place going long after the candidates have gone home.
The sun is starting to burn through now. The first cool morning of the year has the windows coming open and down the block, somebody already smoking meat, a few people walking slower than they have in months.
I pass back by his house. The man is still on the porch, and the cigar has burned down about halfway. Every leaf in it is burning together now. You cannot tell where one ends and the next begins.
He nods at me. I nod back.
The signs will come down. The lights will go up. And Tampa will keep doing what it has always done: getting up early and sanctifying the work of its hands.
**
-- Gavriel Soriano**
**Every One A King**

body:
Killin unseats Crank to become the first Democrat elected in Colorado’s 5th
| | | | [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
---
**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
| | Hi friends!
Want the full news breakdown? Listen to the Mountain Minute podcast [here](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), or watch on [YouTube](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) or [Rumble](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.).
🗳️ _**Colorado Election Update**_ _As of Thursday, Nov. 5 at 3:16pm. All results are unofficial and ballots are still being counted. Figures are from the Secretary of State and AP, as of the latest postings._
_Roughly 2.5 million ballots have been counted, a 61.24% turnout. Turnout crossed 60% for the first time in the 2:48 p.m. batch. Larimer and Arapahoe counties added 25,324 and 13,509 ballots, and Adams, Jefferson and Clear Creek counties then added 38,713. AP stands at 100 of 127 calls, with none since CD-5._
_**Congressional races**_ 🔹 **CD-5:** _**[Democrat Jessica Killin defeated Republican Rep. Jeff Crank](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**_ , 50.56% to 45.98%, a margin of 12,767 votes. AP called the race at 12:38 p.m. Thursday. _**She is the first Democrat ever elected in the district.**_ A Denver judge had already [dismissed Wayne Laugesen’s residency challenge](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) on Oct. 30 as filed outside the legal window, without ruling on where Killin lives.
🔹 **CD-4:** Democrat Eileen Laubacher leads Rep. Lauren Boebert by 2,690 votes. Three straight Weld County batches had cut her lead, and it had recovered to 2,857 before easing back. It is still the closest federal or statewide race in Colorado, and _**AP has not called it.**_
🔹 **CD-3:** Republican Rep. Jeff Hurd leads Democrat Dwayne Romero by 6,076 votes, or 49.30%, his strongest position since he took the lead Wednesday. AP has not called the race.
**_Ballot measures_** 🔹 **[Prop 133:](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** Life without parole for child sex trafficking passed with 62.05%, the highest yes share of the 14 measures and a margin of 558,873 votes. It is a statute, so [the legislature can rewrite it](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) by simple majority when it convenes Jan. 11.
🔹 **[Prop 134 and 135](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** : Both lead, at 52.56% and 52.15% yes, and _**AP has not called either.**_ Gov.-elect Phil Weiser said Wednesday that schools shouldn’t require “full-body examinations." The measure requires no exam and sets no verification method. [Weiser also said the legislature should make adjustments to the measure:](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) _“Anytime you have a ballot measure that is statutory, it is a natural and, I believe, appropriate role for the legislature to say, ‘What are the adjustments that need to be added?’”_
🔹 **[Prop NN:](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** Passed with 55.67%. It eliminates TABOR refunds for two years, and the 2% school funding increase is paid [only if enough revenue is retained](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.).
🔹 **Amendment 87** (graduated income tax): 50.75% yes, up from 50.58% this morning and a new high. At 2:48 p.m. it led by 32,837 votes. _**AP has not called, still too close.**_
🔹 **Prop 137** (conservation): 51.04% yes, crossing 51% for the first time. At 2:48 p.m. it led by 43,058 votes, and _**it remains**_ **_uncalled_**.
🔹 **Amendment 85:** 51.14% yes, still _**3.86 points short of the 55% it needs.**_
**_Legislature_** Democrat Tweed leads **HD-21** by 240 votes, down from 367 Wednesday midday, and Democrat Marsh’s lead in **HD-51** has narrowed to 1,265. In the Senate, Democrat Kevin Leung leads **SD-30** by 4,409 votes, unchanged since election night, with Douglas County yet to report since 5:15 p.m. Wednesday. *_ **Democrats need both uncalled Senate seats to reach the 24 that make a two-thirds supermajority.**_
_**Recount watch**_
_Bennett Fire Protection District 7F flipped from No to Yes and is now inside the mandatory recount margin. Yes leads 1,851 to 1,846, a 5-vote margin against a threshold of 9. It trailed by 32 votes before Adams County reported. It is the first lead change in any Colorado contest since CD-3 flipped overnight, and the first contest inside the recount margin at any point in this count. The companion question, 7G, trails by 17, just outside the threshold of 9._
This is your Mountain Minute for Thursday, November 5, 2026.
– Team RMV

**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[Killin unseats Crank to become the first Democrat elected in Colorado’s 5th](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
A Denver judge was asked six days before the election to rule that Jessica Killin does not live in Colorado.
The judge never reached the question.
On Thursday afternoon, Killin became the first Democrat elected to represent Colorado’s 5th Congressional District. The Associated Press called the race at 12:38 p.m. with an estimated 94% of the vote counted, Colorado Newsline reported.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Proposition NN: Refunds are gone for two years and the 2% is not guaranteed](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
_Voters approved Proposition NN, eliminating TABOR refunds for two years, though the promised “minimum 2% increase” to schools depends on revenue that isn’t guaranteed._
* **Refunds eliminated, costs vary by income:** A $50,000 filer gives up $21 in 2027 and $39 in 2028, while a $500,000 joint filer loses $130 then $352, per the Blue Book analysis.
* **The 2% promise has a catch:** Schools only get the formula amount “if enough revenue is retained,” and only part of the funds are restricted to teacher pay, smaller classes and career programs, the rest goes to a Children’s Account the legislature controls.
* **A pending measure could shrink it further:** Proposition 137, still too close to call, would reduce the surplus Proposition NN captures if it passes, meaning the final payout remains uncertain.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Proposition 133: Voters passed the tougher version of a bill lawmakers killed](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
_Colorado voters approved life without parole for child sex trafficking with 62% support, the highest yes share of any 2026 measure, after a House committee killed a similar bill 7-4 just nine months earlier._
* **A sentence lawmakers rejected:** Proposition 133 makes child sex trafficking a class 1 felony with mandatory life without parole, stripping judicial discretion, after Rep. Scott Bottoms’ near-identical bill died in House Judiciary in February.
* **Broader than the failed bill:** Unlike the legislature’s version, which required buyers to know a minor was trafficked, Proposition 133 applies to anyone who knowingly trades money for sexual activity with a minor, no trafficking knowledge required.
* **Lawmakers can still change it:** Because it amends statute rather than the constitution, the legislature, where Democrats now hold supermajorities in both chambers, can rewrite or repeal it with a simple majority when it convenes Jan. 11.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Proposition 134: Weiser warns of body checks the measure does not require](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
_Gov.-elect Phil Weiser raised concerns about full-body exams the day after voters passed a measure restricting girls’ sports to biological females, but the measure itself requires no such thing._
* **No exam mandated, text confirms:** The Blue Book states the measure “does not impose a specific method for determining or demonstrating biological sex,” leaving verification up to individual schools, the same approach already used by El Paso County’s District 49 since May 2025 with zero eligibility disputes in 16 months.
* **Body-check language came from opponents, not the measure:** The “invasive testing” claim appeared only in the Blue Book’s arguments-against section, a prediction about how districts might respond, not a requirement in the measure’s actual three-page text.
* **Legislature holds the real power:** Because it’s a statutory change, Democrats, who now hold supermajorities in both chambers, can revise or repeal it with a simple majority when they convene Jan. 11, a point Weiser himself raised.

clean_body: Killin unseats Crank to become the first Democrat elected in Colorado’s 5th | | | | PRESENTED BY | | Hi friends! Want the full news breakdown? Listen to the Mountain Minute podcast , or watch on or . 🗳️ Colorado Election Update As of Thursday, Nov. 5 at 3:16pm. All results are unofficial and ballots are still being counted. Figures are from the Secretary of State and AP, as of the latest postings. Roughly 2.5 million ballots have been counted, a 61.24% turnout. Turnout crossed 60% for the first time in the 2:48 p.m. batch. Larimer and Arapahoe counties added 25,324 and 13,509 ballots, and Adams, Jefferson and Clear Creek counties then added 38,713. AP stands at 100 of 127 calls, with none since CD-5. Congressional races 🔹 CD-5: , 50.56% to 45.98%, a margin of 12,767 votes. AP called the race at 12:38 p.m. Thursday. She is the first Democrat ever elected in the district. A Denver judge had already on Oct. 30 as filed outside the legal window, without ruling on where Killin lives. 🔹 CD-4: Democrat Eileen Laubacher leads Rep. Lauren Boebert by 2,690 votes. Three straight Weld County batches had cut her lead, and it had recovered to 2,857 before easing back. It is still the closest federal or statewide race in Colorado, and AP has not called it. 🔹 CD-3: Republican Rep. Jeff Hurd leads Democrat Dwayne Romero by 6,076 votes, or 49.30%, his strongest position since he took the lead Wednesday. AP has not called the race. Ballot measures 🔹 Life without parole for child sex trafficking passed with 62.05%, the highest yes share of the 14 measures and a margin of 558,873 votes. It is a statute, so by simple majority when it convenes Jan. 11. 🔹 : Both lead, at 52.56% and 52.15% yes, and AP has not called either. Gov.-elect Phil Weiser said Wednesday that schools shouldn’t require “full-body examinations." The measure requires no exam and sets no verification method. “Anytime you have a ballot measure that is statutory, it is a natural and, I believe, appropriate role for the legislature to say, ‘What are the adjustments that need to be added?’” 🔹 Passed with 55.67%. It eliminates TABOR refunds for two years, and the 2% school funding increase is paid . 🔹 Amendment 87 (graduated income tax): 50.75% yes, up from 50.58% this morning and a new high. At 2:48 p.m. it led by 32,837 votes. AP has not called, still too close. 🔹 Prop 137 (conservation): 51.04% yes, crossing 51% for the first time. At 2:48 p.m. it led by 43,058 votes, and it remains uncalled. 🔹 Amendment 85: 51.14% yes, still 3.86 points short of the 55% it needs. Legislature Democrat Tweed leads HD-21 by 240 votes, down from 367 Wednesday midday, and Democrat Marsh’s lead in HD-51 has narrowed to 1,265. In the Senate, Democrat Kevin Leung leads SD-30 by 4,409 votes, unchanged since election night, with Douglas County yet to report since 5:15 p.m. Wednesday. Democrats need both uncalled Senate seats to reach the 24 that make a two-thirds supermajority. Recount watch Bennett Fire Protection District 7F flipped from No to Yes and is now inside the mandatory recount margin. Yes leads 1,851 to 1,846, a 5-vote margin against a threshold of 9. It trailed by 32 votes before Adams County reported. It is the first lead change in any Colorado contest since CD-3 flipped overnight, and the first contest inside the recount margin at any point in this count. The companion question, 7G, trails by 17, just outside the threshold of 9. The judge never reached the question. On Thursday afternoon, Killin became the first Democrat elected to represent Colorado’s 5th Congressional District. The Associated Press called the race at 12:38 p.m. with an estimated 94% of the vote counted, Colorado Newsline reported. | BY SHAINA COLE, Voters approved Proposition NN, eliminating TABOR refunds for two years, though the promised “minimum 2% increase” to schools depends on revenue that isn’t guaranteed. Refunds eliminated, costs vary by income: A $50,000 filer gives up $21 in 2027 and $39 in 2028, while a $500,000 joint filer loses $130 then $352, per the Blue Book analysis. The 2% promise has a catch: Schools only get the formula amount “if enough revenue is retained,” and only part of the funds are restricted to teacher pay, smaller classes and career programs, the rest goes to a Children’s Account the legislature controls. A pending measure could shrink it further: Proposition 137, still too close to call, would reduce the surplus Proposition NN captures if it passes, meaning the final payout remains uncertain. | BY SHAINA COLE, Colorado voters approved life without parole for child sex trafficking with 62% support, the highest yes share of any 2026 measure, after a House committee killed a similar bill 7-4 just nine months earlier. A sentence lawmakers rejected: Proposition 133 makes child sex trafficking a class 1 felony with mandatory life without parole, stripping judicial discretion, after Rep. Scott Bottoms’ near-identical bill died in House Judiciary in February. Broader than the failed bill: Unlike the legislature’s version, which required buyers to know a minor was trafficked, Proposition 133 applies to anyone who knowingly trades money for sexual activity with a minor, no trafficking knowledge required. Lawmakers can still change it: Because it amends statute rather than the constitution, the legislature, where Democrats now hold supermajorities in both chambers, can rewrite or repeal it with a simple majority when it convenes Jan. 11. | BY SHAINA COLE, Gov.-elect Phil Weiser raised concerns about full-body exams the day after voters passed a measure restricting girls’ sports to biological females, but the measure itself requires no such thing. No exam mandated, text confirms: The Blue Book states the measure “does not impose a specific method for determining or demonstrating biological sex,” leaving verification up to individual schools, the same approach already used by El Paso County’s District 49 since May 2025 with zero eligibility disputes in 16 months. Body-check language came from opponents, not the measure: The “invasive testing” claim appeared only in the Blue Book’s arguments-against section, a prediction about how districts might respond, not a requirement in the measure’s actual three-page text. But over the last fourteen months my campaign has traveled all across the state, speaking with every last voter we could find.
[ ](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqte1AKsO1A6D16A1pGserP-y1bY7Oy9-mA0lW9ls8k0-Ib9x_xKyg6yRNK5fbbUZk0I_2PwsoQ9KW5QFIpDg2TnF30TfUP7Di2DN6nuhWZLcLnjIbkC2xTr9CPbE6dquL8Q9t6gUaOcs89cH72rFmMH07qJtVm3tg89uA4GcrcGTv9AR8XEgOMMz9TAEfYBWXNEinPnKrs-E1K1ezEYahkjHpbV0jkO1sgFF6xhgSoyZV4TbKnzoKpQ5pPNIx9t4oyRluDBNeQByXDEdaQDW6FhSg-4TTx6fTnzCCW2WSZmdjLkSUlTm4it6RwyFyndT5dMNO7oo5Jxvhszz05abGOp2CFsYXFyYbQtmsHtkk7cUA/4vh/yce1QAq5QxaFMeF1YmEKRA/h1/h001._g6u9owZBxHRfwgmpcmMWHPizo3gPOum4XpxLvChPWc)

We even spent some time talking to voters outside Trump’s Mississippi rally last month – _because that’s how you win in states like this._
[ ](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqte1AKsO1A6D16A1pGserP-y1bY7Oy9-mA0lW9ls8k0-Ib9x_xKyg6yRNK5fbbUZk0I_2PwsoQ9KW5QFIpDg2TnlNMTa7bZMAmFpK-1Mi07s2-ynfr71O5NBB6hM1HxqC7XHPW47E9VkuINqq6vgs3uzZYBey14O2U_NmMH1EfvfDRlEyEmc9-A17Z8lHcX6sb25AAm97jc-wpWHpI37Dg01u5yOwzREVmD8e8R9DoVCceDme9is16gfQSpsGSlFVY3JWwaT5nHauCtxCXgKeoCBsbC6UR2-jdj2kAYNlmmVIrcVMprHat7atGAeRtcDBZ4r3nhpg3slfitdMawIoF36jeTB6ZCmxJVNZBuPEuJ4g/4vh/yce1QAq5QxaFMeF1YmEKRA/h2/h001.Nopph9UoR9aHt4o2FrHmZukqX296DmwvgTpgCt-2GjE)

Along the way we’ve been funded by grassroots donations of $5, $10, even $50 at a time. And it means the world to me to know that so many people have my back.
But this race isn’t over yet.
We need to make sure that we stand up for the will of the voters from now until this is fully certified. In a state like Mississippi, we can’t afford to get complacent at the finish line.
Closing this race out is going to cost millions of dollars. This is going to be the most closely divided U.S. Senate race in modern American history.

But over the last fourteen months my campaign has traveled all across the state, speaking with every last voter we could find. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142977368/658677420/-700026387?amount=10&source=DPG_EM_FR_110526_B1_ColomSplit_S3&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83OTA4MSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxZDIwOGExYy03MWQ5LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=jdpn-IQ2vojfS_PsmwmOYV_7Ostu9NZgdZYMbNyTRiw=) We even spent some time talking to voters outside Trump’s Mississippi rally last month – _because that’s how you win in states like this_. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142977369/658677421/-700026387?amount=10&source=DPG_EM_FR_110526_B1_ColomSplit_S3&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS83OTA4MSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIxZDIwOGExYy03MWQ5LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=jdpn-IQ2vojfS_PsmwmOYV_7Ostu9NZgdZYMbNyTRiw=) Along the way we’ve been funded by grassroots donations of $5, $10, even $50 at a time. And it means the world to me to know that so many people have my back. But this race isn’t over yet. We need to make sure that we stand up for the will of the voters from now until this is fully certified. In a state like Mississippi, we can’t afford to get complacent at the finish line. Closing this race out is going to cost millions of dollars. This is going to be the most closely divided U.S. Senate race in modern American history. [So please. | | Peter —

What’d I say about counting out Florida or the South?!

Tuesday night was a reminder of what can happen when we organize everywhere, invest early, and refuse to write communities off.

Here in Central Florida, **we flipped six House seats and a Senate seat** , ousting one of Tallahassee’s most powerful Republicans and breaking the GOP supermajority in the Florida Legislature.

**We protected all FOUR blue Congressional districts** that Republicans redrew despite Ron DeSantis’ “dummymander”, and even picked up a **NEW seat in South Florida by electing Pia Dandiya to Congress.**

Across Orange County, the results were just as significant. **Tiffany Moore Russell was elected County Mayor** and every local candidate we backed came out on top, from county commission to school board to circuit judge.

And while **Angie Nixon and David Jolly came up short statewide, both races were close** — a reminder that Florida is far more competitive than too many people are willing to admit.

None of this happened overnight.

For years, we’ve been building a year-round organizing operation here in Central Florida — not just showing up months before Election Day.

This cycle, our team:
* Traveled to more than **15 states**
* Invested nearly **$1 million** in races beyond our own
* Helped organize in state legislative, school board, local, congressional, and U.S. Senate races
* Built one of our largest youth organizing programs yet

**This is what grassroots, progressive organizing looks like. And it was possible because of _your_ support, Peter.**

Your support helped us knock doors, talk to voters, place ads, and support candidates who put working people first.

Florida still has a lot of work ahead of us. But after Tuesday night, nobody should pretend that organizing here — or anywhere across the South — is a lost cause.

body:
# [](https://act.electjon.com/go/4629?t=1&akid=3261%2E5691347%2ETv77Dk)

Peter, it’s Jon Ossoff.
I am writing today to ask you to help Mary Peltola win her toss-up Senate race in Alaska and expand our brand new Democratic Senate majority.
I know it’s been a long election cycle, and you’re probably tired of these emails. _I get it._
But we can’t rest on our laurels — not when the stakes are this high and the opportunity to win is right in front of us.
With a victory in Alaska and an expanded majority, we can better check the power of the depraved President Donald J. Trump. And with an expanded majority, we lay the foundations for major policy achievements on health care, anti-corruption, and civil rights.
Remember: enduring majorities aren’t built in a single election cycle. These are six year terms, and every seat matters.
So please: join me in helping Mary Peltola, and use this link to chip in: [**https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ossoff-em-peltola**](https://act.electjon.com/go/5243?c0=ossoff-em-peltola.IlyHq8&refcode=em261105-1-subs&utm_campaign=em261105-1-subs&t=2&akid=3261%2E5691347%2ETv77Dk)
Here’s the situation in Alaska:
As of this morning, the margin is less than 1,000 votes! This race is _incredibly_ close.
Mary and her team are fighting to ensure every ballot is counted. They’re also preparing for Donald Trump and the Department of Justice to try to overturn the results if she wins.
But fighting back is going to take time — and lots of resources. Resources that Mary doesn’t have right now.
Campaigning in Alaska is difficult and expensive, and Mary and her team put everything into getting out the vote and winning this race.
Peter, Mary needs a huge number of contributions _today_ to keep fighting and make sure she wins this toss-up Senate race. Can you add yours?
[**Please, split a $5 contribution between Mary Peltola in Alaska and my campaign. If we have her back now, I am confident she will win.**](https://act.electjon.com/go/5243?c0=ossoff-em-peltola.IlyHq8&refcode=em261105-1-subs&utm_campaign=em261105-1-subs&amount=5&t=3&akid=3261%2E5691347%2ETv77Dk)
**[DONATE](https://act.electjon.com/go/5243?c0=ossoff-em-peltola.IlyHq8&refcode=em261105-1-subs&utm_campaign=em261105-1-subs&t=4&akid=3261%2E5691347%2ETv77Dk)**
Thank you for staying in the fight.
Jon Ossoff

| **[DONATE](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ossoff-em-peltola?refcode=email-footer&t=5&refcode2=3261_5691347_Tv77Dk&akid=3261%2E5691347%2ETv77Dk)**

subject: Lessons from Tuesday

body:
[ https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20261105-6939-footer&t=1001&akid=6939%2E420207%2ERcNMuM ]Pramila Jayapal

What an exhilarating week,
Peter!

On Tuesday night, voters across the country delivered a resounding message
to change the direction of our country — to reject cruelty, cowardice and
war, and to demand a decent and affordable life for them and their
families.

I’m deeply grateful that I will continue to help lead that fight in
Congress. Thank you so much for your friendship, generosity, and support
not only for me, but for the amazing progressive candidates I supported
across the country.

Winning a Democratic majority in Congress was just the first step — the
next phase begins right now. We have to hit the ground running on Day 1 to
deliver real change that makes people’s lives better.

Here’s what this election taught us:

➡️ Bold ideas win, even in the toughest districts.

Progressives ran on getting Big Money out of politics, lowering the cost
of living, and finally passing Medicare for All. And they won in places
the establishment said were out of reach! We proved that it’s not enough
to just be an opposition party — we also have to be a proposition party.
We have to show working people exactly how and why our ideas will change
their lives. And it worked!

➡️ When we compete everywhere, we can also win everywhere.

We showed up in races where candidates got zero support from the national
party. And we WON! Every campaign, win or lose, helps us build towards
something better the next cycle. Just look at Georgia, where voters
elected the first Black woman to serve as governor anywhere in the
country. A historic win built on years of Stacey Abrams’ organizing.
Change doesn’t happen overnight, but every time we show up to fight, we
chip away at the status quo.

➡️ Our progressive message has become mainstream.

Many of the winning candidates didn’t call themselves progressives, but
they ran on the very issues that we’ve been pushing for years:
affordability and corruption. They took on giant corporations and data
centers, and stood FOR working people who deserve a living wage, universal
childcare and health care. Our message is working.

We won big in the House and Senate. Now, people are counting on us to
deliver. We’ve seen how fast the political landscape can shift, so it’s
critical that we don’t make the mistake of doing too little.

Here’s where I’ll be focused:

* Immigration: As the incoming Chairwoman of the House Judiciary
Subcommittee on Immigration, I’ll make oversight a top priority,
holding accountable the ICE and CBP agents who shot and killed people
in our streets and kidnapped and detained so many. I’ll then lead the
work to fix our broken immigration system and expand pathways to
citizenship.
* Medicare for All: I will continue to lead the fight for Medicare for
All. It’s time to get private insurance companies out of the business
of denying care and making people bankrupt. Every single American
deserves universal health care.
* Money out of politics: We must end Citizens United. We must get money
out of politics. And we must ban stock trading within Congress.
